  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_228b47d6bf5c495991943907247fd497",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/slack/eng-platform/1768427740.json",
    "title": "eng-platform",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/slack",
    "content": "{\n  \"channel\": \"eng-platform\",\n  \"thread_ts\": \"1768427740\",\n  \"first_message_ts\": \"1768427740\",\n  \"last_message_ts\": \"1768433289\",\n  \"participants\": [\n    \"Ethan Park\",\n    \"Benji Okafor\",\n    \"Kaitlyn Nguyen\",\n    \"Thomas Baird\",\n    \"Chloe Martin\",\n    \"Jada Williams\",\n    \"Rafael Mendes\",\n    \"Allison Grant\",\n    \"Connor O'Brien\"\n  ],\n  \"messages\": \"Ethan Park: trying to unblock the Cost Model API shape question for v1. do we want Console to *pull* (sync request -> cost breakdown), or do we want a *push* model (emit events + precomputed aggregates in a store) and Console reads from that?\\n\\nEthan Park: constraints: Console hot paths need p95 < ~150ms end-to-end for the cost panel. also we cannot let this endpoint become a cardinality bomb.\\n\\nThomas Baird: push is the only way you\\u2019re gonna hit p95 reliably for \\u201cdashboards\\u201d use cases. if Console is rendering a table for 7d + group by route/model/customer it\\u2019s basically an analytics query.\\n\\nChloe Martin: +1 on perf concerns, but Console also has \\u201crequest details\\u201d view (per request / trace) where we want to show breakdown for *that* request. that\\u2019s not really a push/agg thing.\\n\\nBenji Okafor: we might be mixing 2 things:\\n1) estimate/breakdown for a single request or small batch -> synchronous\\n2) aggregates for dashboards -> should be precomputed, or at least bounded w/ pagination + caching\\n\\nJada Williams: for Console hot path we can also cache at Console backend. cost breakdown for a request-id is immutable after the request finishes (minus telemetry backfill weirdness). so we can do a read-through cache keyed by (request_id, cost_model_version).\\n\\nThomas Baird: request_id lookups are fine. the danger is \\u201cgive me breakdown for 10k requests\\u201d or \\u201cgroup by 12 dimensions\\u201d. if we expose that as pull, someone will do it.\\n\\nKaitlyn Nguyen: from auth/tenancy POV: push model (events) needs super clear ownership on what\\u2019s allowed to be written + data isolation. pull is simpler because the service can enforce tenant in one place w/ existing service-to-service auth.\\n\\nRafael Mendes: SRE angle: synchronous on Console path means we need strict SLO + graceful degradation. if this API has an outage, Console shouldn\\u2019t blank out cost tabs and page us all day.\\n\\nAllison Grant: API standards reminder: anything \\u201caggregate list\\u201d must have explicit bounding semantics (limit, cursor/pagination, max group-by keys, max time range) and deterministic ordering. no \\u201cunbounded\\u201d queries.\\n\\nEthan Park: ok, so: maybe v1 = pull for (a) single request, (b) small bounded set, and explicitly *not* a general analytics surface. and for dashboards we use telemetry pipeline + a materialized view later.\\n\\nChloe Martin: what does \\u201csmall bounded set\\u201d mean? Console might need e.g. last 50 requests in a trace view or last 100 failed requests in a route view.\\n\\nThomas Baird: propose hard limits:\\n- max 200 request_ids per call\\n- max time range 24h on any \\u201csearch\\u201d endpoint (if we even have it)\\n- max group-by dims = 2\\n- cap number of returned buckets = 500\\nanything else -> async job / offline pipeline\\n\\nBenji Okafor: + add rate limiting by caller + tenant. also return 400 w/ a specific error code if bounds exceeded (so clients can degrade nicely).\\n\\nJada Williams: also prefer endpoint that takes `request_ids` explicitly vs \\u201cfilter\\u201d semantics. filters tend to explode (regex on route etc).\\n\\nEthan Park: i like that. explicit IDs = self-bounding.\\n\\nKaitlyn Nguyen: +1. and require `tenant_id` in auth context, not in request body. don\\u2019t want clients \\u201ctyping\\u201d tenant ids.\\n\\nAllison Grant: caching strategy: if response is deterministic given inputs, we can support ETag / `If-None-Match` so Console can avoid re-downloading payload. also stable `schema_version` field and clear forward-compat rules.\\n\\nRafael Mendes: also need to define what happens when telemetry is lagging. if we do request_id lookup but telemetry store hasn\\u2019t ingested KV-cache stats yet, do we return partial breakdown or 404 or \\u201cpending\\u201d?\\n\\nEthan Park: good call. probably `status=partial` w/ `missing_inputs=[...]` and an `advice=retry_after_ms`.\\n\\nThomas Baird: careful: \\u201cretry after\\u201d could cause thundering herd. Console will refresh like crazy.\\n\\nChloe Martin: we can handle in Console: only retry on user action or after a backoff, and show \\u201ccost breakdown still processing\\u201d.\\n\\nBenji Okafor: service-side caching/memoization can help too. if the same request_id is asked 20x in 30s, just serve from cache.\\n\\nEthan Park: yes. plan:\\n- L1 in-process cache in cost-model svc keyed by (tenant, request_id, schema_version)\\n- TTL maybe 5m for partial, 1h for complete\\n- optional L2 (redis) later if needed\\n\\nAllison Grant: note: TTL rules need to match determinism expectations. if breakdown can change due to backfills, then we should expose `data_freshness_ts` and be explicit: v1 returns \\u201cbest available at query time\\u201d and backfills may adjust for N hours.\\n\\nJada Williams: finance will want auditability. but for Console UX it\\u2019s ok if we show \\u201cestimated\\u201d and then reconciles later. we just need consistency between Console and Optimize, not necessarily perfect instant truth.\\n\\nThomas Baird: still think push for aggregates is mandatory. otherwise every dashboard load is going to compute sums on the fly.\\n\\nEthan Park: agree. but that\\u2019s phase 2. for v1 we only commit to request-level + bounded lists, and Console\\u2019s dashboard panels continue to read from existing aggregates until we migrate.\\n\\nRafael Mendes: +1, reduces outage blast radius.\\n\\nKaitlyn Nguyen: what about \\u201cwhat-if\\u201d endpoints? those can be expensive. also a pull model there could be abused.\\n\\nBenji Okafor: for what-if, require a \\u201cworkload summary\\u201d input (counts + token histograms) not raw request lists. and enforce max bins / max scenarios.\\n\\nThomas Baird: yes. if Optimize wants to run 50 scenarios x 20 models, that\\u2019s not a request/response endpoint.\\n\\nEthan Park: setting guardrails:\\n- `max_scenarios_per_request=5`\\n- `max_histogram_bins=50`\\n- `max_models_compared=3`\\n- compute budget per request, fail fast with `RESOURCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`\\n\\nAllison Grant: make sure error codes are standardized (e.g. `RW_COSTMODEL_BOUNDS_EXCEEDED`, `RW_COSTMODEL_RESOURCE_LIMIT`, `RW_COSTMODEL_PARTIAL_INPUTS`).\\n\\nConnor O'Brien: (jumping in) for release train, would be great if the v1 decision is \\u201cpull w/ hard bounds + caching + explicit IDs\\u201d so we can scope work for next sprint. :thumbsup:\\n\\nChloe Martin: caching question: should Console cache or should we tell them to rely on server caching? i\\u2019d rather cache in Console backend to keep UI stable even if service p95 jitters.\\n\\nRafael Mendes: do both. server caching protects us from thundering herd + retries. client caching protects end user p95.\\n\\nEthan Park: ok summary:\\n- v1 is PULL for request-level estimate/breakdown and small bounded lists (explicit request_ids)\\n- NO general \\u201caggregate/group-by over time range\\u201d in v1 for Console dashboards\\n- strict request bounding + rate limits + clear error codes\\n- caching: server memoization + recommend Console backend read-through cache; add ETag if feasible\\n- partial results + `missing_inputs` when telemetry lag/backfill\\n\\nEthan Park: i\\u2019ll write this into the design spec + API guidelines addendum. if anyone strongly disagrees, pls say now.\\n\\nThomas Baird: no disagreement as long as \\u201caggregate dashboards\\u201d are explicitly out-of-scope for v1 and we don\\u2019t sneak in filter endpoints.\\n\\nJada Williams: +1. i\\u2019ll coordinate with Chloe on Console caching behavior + fallback (if API degraded, show legacy values / hide breakdown).\\n\\nChloe Martin: sounds good. pls include recommended limits in doc so we don\\u2019t guess.\\n\\nBenji Okafor: i\\u2019ll add quota/rate limit notes + suggested defaults.\\n\\nKaitlyn Nguyen: and i\\u2019ll review the auth section (no tenant_id in body, service-to-service only).\\n\\nRafael Mendes: loop me on SLO/failure modes once you have draft.\\n\\nAllison Grant: same, I\\u2019ll sanity check bounding/pagination language.\\n\\nEthan Park: thanks all. action item: i\\u2019ll post doc link in-thread once updated.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"channel\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_228b47d6bf5c495991943907247fd497\"\n}",

{
  "channel": "eng-platform",
  "thread_ts": "1768427740",
  "first_message_ts": "1768427740",
  "last_message_ts": "1768433289",
  "participants": [
    "Ethan Park",
    "Benji Okafor",
    "Kaitlyn Nguyen",
    "Thomas Baird",
    "Chloe Martin",
    "Jada Williams",
    "Rafael Mendes",
    "Allison Grant",
    "Connor O'Brien"
  ],
  "messages": "Ethan Park: trying to unblock the Cost Model API shape question for v1. do we want Console to *pull* (sync request -> cost breakdown), or do we want a *push* model (emit events + precomputed aggregates in a store) and Console reads from that?

Ethan Park: constraints: Console hot paths need p95 < ~150ms end-to-end for the cost panel. also we cannot let this endpoint become a cardinality bomb.

Thomas Baird: push is the only way you’re gonna hit p95 reliably for “dashboards” use cases. if Console is rendering a table for 7d + group by route/model/customer it’s basically an analytics query.

Chloe Martin: +1 on perf concerns, but Console also has “request details” view (per request / trace) where we want to show breakdown for *that* request. that’s not really a push/agg thing.

Benji Okafor: we might be mixing 2 things:
1) estimate/breakdown for a single request or small batch -> synchronous
2) aggregates for dashboards -> should be precomputed, or at least bounded w/ pagination + caching

Jada Williams: for Console hot path we can also cache at Console backend. cost breakdown for a request-id is immutable after the request finishes (minus telemetry backfill weirdness). so we can do a read-through cache keyed by (request_id, cost_model_version).

Thomas Baird: request_id lookups are fine. the danger is “give me breakdown for 10k requests” or “group by 12 dimensions”. if we expose that as pull, someone will do it.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: from auth/tenancy POV: push model (events) needs super clear ownership on what’s allowed to be written + data isolation. pull is simpler because the service can enforce tenant in one place w/ existing service-to-service auth.

Rafael Mendes: SRE angle: synchronous on Console path means we need strict SLO + graceful degradation. if this API has an outage, Console shouldn’t blank out cost tabs and page us all day.

Allison Grant: API standards reminder: anything “aggregate list” must have explicit bounding semantics (limit, cursor/pagination, max group-by keys, max time range) and deterministic ordering. no “unbounded” queries.

Ethan Park: ok, so: maybe v1 = pull for (a) single request, (b) small bounded set, and explicitly *not* a general analytics surface. and for dashboards we use telemetry pipeline + a materialized view later.

Chloe Martin: what does “small bounded set” mean? Console might need e.g. last 50 requests in a trace view or last 100 failed requests in a route view.

Thomas Baird: propose hard limits:
- max 200 request_ids per call
- max time range 24h on any “search” endpoint (if we even have it)
- max group-by dims = 2
- cap number of returned buckets = 500
anything else -> async job / offline pipeline

Benji Okafor: + add rate limiting by caller + tenant. also return 400 w/ a specific error code if bounds exceeded (so clients can degrade nicely).

Jada Williams: also prefer endpoint that takes `request_ids` explicitly vs “filter” semantics. filters tend to explode (regex on route etc).

Ethan Park: i like that. explicit IDs = self-bounding.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: +1. and require `tenant_id` in auth context, not in request body. don’t want clients “typing” tenant ids.

Allison Grant: caching strategy: if response is deterministic given inputs, we can support ETag / `If-None-Match` so Console can avoid re-downloading payload. also stable `schema_version` field and clear forward-compat rules.

Rafael Mendes: also need to define what happens when telemetry is lagging. if we do request_id lookup but telemetry store hasn’t ingested KV-cache stats yet, do we return partial breakdown or 404 or “pending”?

Ethan Park: good call. probably `status=partial` w/ `missing_inputs=[...]` and an `advice=retry_after_ms`.

Thomas Baird: careful: “retry after” could cause thundering herd. Console will refresh like crazy.

Chloe Martin: we can handle in Console: only retry on user action or after a backoff, and show “cost breakdown still processing”.

Benji Okafor: service-side caching/memoization can help too. if the same request_id is asked 20x in 30s, just serve from cache.

Ethan Park: yes. plan:
- L1 in-process cache in cost-model svc keyed by (tenant, request_id, schema_version)
- TTL maybe 5m for partial, 1h for complete
- optional L2 (redis) later if needed

Allison Grant: note: TTL rules need to match determinism expectations. if breakdown can change due to backfills, then we should expose `data_freshness_ts` and be explicit: v1 returns “best available at query time” and backfills may adjust for N hours.

Jada Williams: finance will want auditability. but for Console UX it’s ok if we show “estimated” and then reconciles later. we just need consistency between Console and Optimize, not necessarily perfect instant truth.

Thomas Baird: still think push for aggregates is mandatory. otherwise every dashboard load is going to compute sums on the fly.

Ethan Park: agree. but that’s phase 2. for v1 we only commit to request-level + bounded lists, and Console’s dashboard panels continue to read from existing aggregates until we migrate.

Rafael Mendes: +1, reduces outage blast radius.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: what about “what-if” endpoints? those can be expensive. also a pull model there could be abused.

Benji Okafor: for what-if, require a “workload summary” input (counts + token histograms) not raw request lists. and enforce max bins / max scenarios.

Thomas Baird: yes. if Optimize wants to run 50 scenarios x 20 models, that’s not a request/response endpoint.

Ethan Park: setting guardrails:
- `max_scenarios_per_request=5`
- `max_histogram_bins=50`
- `max_models_compared=3`
- compute budget per request, fail fast with `RESOURCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`

Allison Grant: make sure error codes are standardized (e.g. `RW_COSTMODEL_BOUNDS_EXCEEDED`, `RW_COSTMODEL_RESOURCE_LIMIT`, `RW_COSTMODEL_PARTIAL_INPUTS`).

Connor O'Brien: (jumping in) for release train, would be great if the v1 decision is “pull w/ hard bounds + caching + explicit IDs” so we can scope work for next sprint. :thumbsup:

Chloe Martin: caching question: should Console cache or should we tell them to rely on server caching? i’d rather cache in Console backend to keep UI stable even if service p95 jitters.

Rafael Mendes: do both. server caching protects us from thundering herd + retries. client caching protects end user p95.

Ethan Park: ok summary:
- v1 is PULL for request-level estimate/breakdown and small bounded lists (explicit request_ids)
- NO general “aggregate/group-by over time range” in v1 for Console dashboards
- strict request bounding + rate limits + clear error codes
- caching: server memoization + recommend Console backend read-through cache; add ETag if feasible
- partial results + `missing_inputs` when telemetry lag/backfill

Ethan Park: i’ll write this into the design spec + API guidelines addendum. if anyone strongly disagrees, pls say now.

Thomas Baird: no disagreement as long as “aggregate dashboards” are explicitly out-of-scope for v1 and we don’t sneak in filter endpoints.

Jada Williams: +1. i’ll coordinate with Chloe on Console caching behavior + fallback (if API degraded, show legacy values / hide breakdown).

Chloe Martin: sounds good. pls include recommended limits in doc so we don’t guess.

Benji Okafor: i’ll add quota/rate limit notes + suggested defaults.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: and i’ll review the auth section (no tenant_id in body, service-to-service only).

Rafael Mendes: loop me on SLO/failure modes once you have draft.

Allison Grant: same, I’ll sanity check bounding/pagination language.

Ethan Park: thanks all. action item: i’ll post doc link in-thread once updated.",

  "content_field_names": [
    "messages"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_228b47d6bf5c495991943907247fd497"
}

    "content": "{\n  \"channel\": \"eng-platform\",\n  \"thread_ts\": \"1764017782\",\n  \"first_message_ts\": \"1764017782\",\n  \"last_message_ts\": \"1764021564\",\n  \"participants\": [\n    \"Ethan Park\",\n    \"Chloe Martin\",\n    \"Dylan Brooks\",\n    \"Felix Schneider\",\n    \"Benji Okafor\",\n    \"Jordan Lee\",\n    \"Caleb Johnson\",\n    \"Yara Haddad\",\n    \"Kenji Nakamura\",\n    \"Alicia Perez\",\n    \"Logan Wright\",\n    \"api-contract-bot\"\n  ],\n  \"body\": \"Ethan Park: heads up: Console needs to show quality gate results + artifact links for Optimize recommendations. Can we align on what the Console API needs from Optimize service vs a separate artifacts endpoint?\\n\\nChloe Martin: yup, we\\u2019re building the Console backend slice now. Need an explicit contract from Optimize. Biggest questions: (1) what IDs we get back, (2) how to fetch artifacts securely, (3) what\\u2019s included in the \\u201csummary\\u201d vs \\u201cdetails\\u201d.\\n\\nDylan Brooks: +1. UX wants a compact banner in the recommendation drawer + a drilldown page with comparisons. We can\\u2019t render if we only have a single pass/fail boolean.\\n\\nYara Haddad: from Optimize side we already store gate runs (state machine). Can return `gate_run_id` + status and some rollup metrics. For artifacts we currently have S3 object keys + eval-harness run id.\\n\\nBenji Okafor: request: please don\\u2019t leak raw S3 keys to Console clients. We should give Console an `artifact_id` list and Console calls a server-side endpoint to mint presigned URLs (RBAC + audit).\\n\\nJordan Lee: also note policy: some accounts will have override-only visibility (enterprise). So artifact access needs to check route/account permissions, not just \\u201cuser logged in\\u201d.\\n\\nFelix Schneider: what do we need for the dashboard view? We want pass/fail by config type and model family; but for the drilldown we\\u2019ll show: baseline config, proposed config, delta metrics, flake score, and links to prompt-level diffs.\\n\\nChloe Martin: proposing two endpoints:\\n1) `GET /v1/optimize/recommendations/{id}` returns recommendation + embedded `gate_summary`.\\n2) `GET /v1/quality-gates/{gate_run_id}` returns `gate_details` (metrics, thresholds, prompt set coverage, artifact refs).\\nThen Console backend calls an artifact url endpoint per artifact ref.\\n\\nEthan Park: +1. Keep rec endpoint small/fast. Question: do we need `gate_summary` in the list view too (recommendations table)?\\n\\nDylan Brooks: yes. List view should show \\u201cGates: Pending/Passed/Failed/Override required\\u201d without extra round trips. If user clicks, then we fetch the gate details.\\n\\nKenji Nakamura: UX notes: for fail state we need \\u201ctop 3 reasons\\u201d copy. Ex: \\u201cRubric score -0.7 below threshold (-0.3)\\u201d + \\u201cTask success -1.2pp (min -0.5pp)\\u201d. Also show \\u201cArtifacts\\u201d with labels: \\u201csummary.json\\u201d, \\u201cprompt_diffs.html\\u201d, \\u201craw_results.parquet\\u201d.\\n\\nAlicia Perez: +1 and we need to show \\u201cCompare\\u201d CTA. So we need enough info to link baseline vs candidate outputs. If that\\u2019s a single artifact, fine, but it must be labeled.\\n\\nYara Haddad: on Optimize side we can populate:\\n- `status`: pending | running | passed | failed | overridden | canceled\\n- `gate_tier`: smoke | full\\n- `started_at`, `completed_at`\\n- `baseline_id` (or baseline config hash)\\n- `config_diff_id`\\n- `metrics_rollup`: list of key metric deltas + threshold\\n- `failure_reasons`: strings (already in PR-19531)\\n- `artifact_refs`: typed list (summary, prompt_diff, logs)\\n\\nBenji Okafor: can we make `artifact_refs` stable? Like `{id, type, display_name, content_type, size_bytes}`. Display name is important for the UI.\\n\\nChloe Martin: we can do that, but reminder: our JSON responses need to be consistent across services. If Optimize owns artifact IDs, it should also own the minting endpoint.\\n\\nCaleb Johnson: observability note: if Console is fetching artifacts through backend, include headers/tags so we can attribute download volume and errors. Also any presign should be short-lived (<= 15 min) and logged (audit).\\n\\nJordan Lee: +1 and we should include `requires_permission: true` on artifacts? Some artifacts might contain customer prompts (PII). We may want to hide prompt-level diffs unless the user has `prompt_viewer` role.\\n\\nEthan Park: good call. RBAC matrix:\\n- everyone with Optimize access can see gate summary and aggregate metrics.\\n- prompt-level artifacts require elevated role (or enterprise admin).\\n- raw logs should probably be internal only.\\n\\nLogan Wright: if we\\u2019re doing that, don\\u2019t bake \\u201crole names\\u201d into payloads. Use `artifact_access_level`: `aggregate_only` | `prompt_level` | `internal` and let Console map to UI.\\n\\napi-contract-bot: Reminder: API changes must be captured in the OpenAPI spec before merge. Please add to `optimize-service/openapi.yaml` and tag @api-review.\\n\\nFelix Schneider: for drilldown page, do we need per-prompt metrics in the gate details payload, or is that always via artifact? If it\\u2019s in payload it can get huge.\\n\\nYara Haddad: we prefer artifact for per-prompt. Gate details payload will include:\\n- metric aggregates (mean/median), and maybe top-N prompt ids affected\\n- prompt set coverage summary (N prompts, categories)\\n- `flake_score` + rerun count\\n- `artifact_refs` for everything else\\n\\nDylan Brooks: sounds fine. Can we also include a `ui_links` object? Like direct link to eval-harness UI.\\n\\nChloe Martin: we can\\u2019t add nested objects in some of our Console templates? (for this file maybe irrelevant) \\u2014 but as a service contract, sure. Alternatively, a string `external_run_url`.\\n\\nEthan Park: keep it simple: `external_run_url` as string in gate details.\\n\\nBenji Okafor: re: artifact URL minting: suggest `POST /v1/quality-gates/{gate_run_id}/artifacts/{artifact_id}:mintUrl` with body `{\\\"ttl_seconds\\\":900}`. Response includes `url` + `expires_at`. Console backend only.\\n\\nChloe Martin: ok. Action items:\\n- @Yara Haddad to draft the `gate_summary` + `gate_details` schema fields + artifact ref fields.\\n- @Benji Okafor + @Jordan Lee to confirm access levels + enforcement points.\\n- @Dylan Brooks/@Kenji Nakamura to confirm which 3 failure reasons to surface + naming conventions.\\nWe\\u2019ll start wiring Console backend with stubbed fields this week.\\n\\nEthan Park: perfect. please post the draft schema in #eng-platform once ready; we\\u2019ll do quick API review async.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"channel\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_de6832ea60f24e0b8ba930b423563ba8\"\n}",

{
  "channel": "eng-platform",
  "thread_ts": "1764017782",
  "first_message_ts": "1764017782",
  "last_message_ts": "1764021564",
  "participants": [
    "Ethan Park",
    "Chloe Martin",
    "Dylan Brooks",
    "Felix Schneider",
    "Benji Okafor",
    "Jordan Lee",
    "Caleb Johnson",
    "Yara Haddad",
    "Kenji Nakamura",
    "Alicia Perez",
    "Logan Wright",
    "api-contract-bot"
  ],
  "body": "Ethan Park: heads up: Console needs to show quality gate results + artifact links for Optimize recommendations. Can we align on what the Console API needs from Optimize service vs a separate artifacts endpoint?

Chloe Martin: yup, we’re building the Console backend slice now. Need an explicit contract from Optimize. Biggest questions: (1) what IDs we get back, (2) how to fetch artifacts securely, (3) what’s included in the “summary” vs “details”.

Dylan Brooks: +1. UX wants a compact banner in the recommendation drawer + a drilldown page with comparisons. We can’t render if we only have a single pass/fail boolean.

Yara Haddad: from Optimize side we already store gate runs (state machine). Can return `gate_run_id` + status and some rollup metrics. For artifacts we currently have S3 object keys + eval-harness run id.

Benji Okafor: request: please don’t leak raw S3 keys to Console clients. We should give Console an `artifact_id` list and Console calls a server-side endpoint to mint presigned URLs (RBAC + audit).

Jordan Lee: also note policy: some accounts will have override-only visibility (enterprise). So artifact access needs to check route/account permissions, not just “user logged in”.

Felix Schneider: what do we need for the dashboard view? We want pass/fail by config type and model family; but for the drilldown we’ll show: baseline config, proposed config, delta metrics, flake score, and links to prompt-level diffs.

Chloe Martin: proposing two endpoints:
1) `GET /v1/optimize/recommendations/{id}` returns recommendation + embedded `gate_summary`.
2) `GET /v1/quality-gates/{gate_run_id}` returns `gate_details` (metrics, thresholds, prompt set coverage, artifact refs).
Then Console backend calls an artifact url endpoint per artifact ref.

Ethan Park: +1. Keep rec endpoint small/fast. Question: do we need `gate_summary` in the list view too (recommendations table)?

Dylan Brooks: yes. List view should show “Gates: Pending/Passed/Failed/Override required” without extra round trips. If user clicks, then we fetch the gate details.

Kenji Nakamura: UX notes: for fail state we need “top 3 reasons” copy. Ex: “Rubric score -0.7 below threshold (-0.3)” + “Task success -1.2pp (min -0.5pp)”. Also show “Artifacts” with labels: “summary.json”, “prompt_diffs.html”, “raw_results.parquet”.

Alicia Perez: +1 and we need to show “Compare” CTA. So we need enough info to link baseline vs candidate outputs. If that’s a single artifact, fine, but it must be labeled.

Yara Haddad: on Optimize side we can populate:
- `status`: pending | running | passed | failed | overridden | canceled
- `gate_tier`: smoke | full
- `started_at`, `completed_at`
- `baseline_id` (or baseline config hash)
- `config_diff_id`
- `metrics_rollup`: list of key metric deltas + threshold
- `failure_reasons`: strings (already in PR-19531)
- `artifact_refs`: typed list (summary, prompt_diff, logs)

Benji Okafor: can we make `artifact_refs` stable? Like `{id, type, display_name, content_type, size_bytes}`. Display name is important for the UI.

Chloe Martin: we can do that, but reminder: our JSON responses need to be consistent across services. If Optimize owns artifact IDs, it should also own the minting endpoint.

Caleb Johnson: observability note: if Console is fetching artifacts through backend, include headers/tags so we can attribute download volume and errors. Also any presign should be short-lived (<= 15 min) and logged (audit).

Jordan Lee: +1 and we should include `requires_permission: true` on artifacts? Some artifacts might contain customer prompts (PII). We may want to hide prompt-level diffs unless the user has `prompt_viewer` role.

Ethan Park: good call. RBAC matrix:
- everyone with Optimize access can see gate summary and aggregate metrics.
- prompt-level artifacts require elevated role (or enterprise admin).
- raw logs should probably be internal only.

Logan Wright: if we’re doing that, don’t bake “role names” into payloads. Use `artifact_access_level`: `aggregate_only` | `prompt_level` | `internal` and let Console map to UI.

api-contract-bot: Reminder: API changes must be captured in the OpenAPI spec before merge. Please add to `optimize-service/openapi.yaml` and tag @api-review.

Felix Schneider: for drilldown page, do we need per-prompt metrics in the gate details payload, or is that always via artifact? If it’s in payload it can get huge.

Yara Haddad: we prefer artifact for per-prompt. Gate details payload will include:
- metric aggregates (mean/median), and maybe top-N prompt ids affected
- prompt set coverage summary (N prompts, categories)
- `flake_score` + rerun count
- `artifact_refs` for everything else

Dylan Brooks: sounds fine. Can we also include a `ui_links` object? Like direct link to eval-harness UI.

Chloe Martin: we can’t add nested objects in some of our Console templates? (for this file maybe irrelevant) — but as a service contract, sure. Alternatively, a string `external_run_url`.

Ethan Park: keep it simple: `external_run_url` as string in gate details.

Benji Okafor: re: artifact URL minting: suggest `POST /v1/quality-gates/{gate_run_id}/artifacts/{artifact_id}:mintUrl` with body `{"ttl_seconds":900}`. Response includes `url` + `expires_at`. Console backend only.

Chloe Martin: ok. Action items:
- @Yara Haddad to draft the `gate_summary` + `gate_details` schema fields + artifact ref fields.
- @Benji Okafor + @Jordan Lee to confirm access levels + enforcement points.
- @Dylan Brooks/@Kenji Nakamura to confirm which 3 failure reasons to surface + naming conventions.
We’ll start wiring Console backend with stubbed fields this week.

Ethan Park: perfect. please post the draft schema in #eng-platform once ready; we’ll do quick API review async.",

  "content_field_names": [
    "body"
  ],

}

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_9f800429ef72472f94b65368044df633",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/slack/eng-platform/1769536063.json",
    "title": "eng-platform",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/slack",
    "content": "{\n  \"channel\": \"eng-platform\",\n  \"thread_ts\": \"1769536063\",\n  \"first_message_ts\": \"1769536063\",\n  \"last_message_ts\": \"1769539748\",\n  \"participants\": [\n    \"Ethan Park\",\n    \"Chloe Martin\",\n    \"Thomas Baird\",\n    \"Rafael Mendes\",\n    \"Allison Grant\",\n    \"Benji Okafor\",\n    \"Logan Wright\",\n    \"Jada Williams\",\n    \"Marissa Cole\",\n    \"CostOps Bot\"\n  ],\n  \"text\": \"Ethan Park: quick q for folks thinking about Console integration: should the cost-model API be called synchronously on the request path, or should Console only consume async aggregates (dashboards) and keep request-path stuff out of it?\\n\\nChloe Martin: for Console, the cost breakdown page is effectively \\u201chot path\\u201d when customers click around, but not *the* inference request path. still needs to be snappy (sub-second) and reliable.\\n\\nThomas Baird: +1 to being careful. if we make the API do heavy aggregation synchronously over high-cardinality telemetry (filters + group-bys) we\\u2019ll get cardinality blowups and p95 will go sideways.\\n\\nBenji Okafor: I think we\\u2019re mixing 2 use cases:\\n1) per-request estimate/breakdown (bounded inputs, deterministic)\\n2) time-window aggregates for dashboards (potentially huge)\\nWe can do (1) sync. (2) should be async or pre-aggregated.\\n\\nJada Williams: Console pages we\\u2019re building:\\n- \\u201cRequest details\\u201d drill-down (single request_id) => sync call is fine\\n- \\u201cCost by model/route over time\\u201d (time series) => we currently query analytics tables. if this becomes sync cost-model API doing the same scan, that\\u2019ll be bad.\\n\\nAllison Grant: observability principle: anything that can fan out / scan should not sit behind a synchronous API in the user click path unless it\\u2019s strictly bounded and cached.\\n\\nEthan Park: makes sense. was thinking whether we should force Console to only use async \\u201creporting\\u201d endpoints so we don\\u2019t get pulled into dashboard-style queries.\\n\\nRafael Mendes: from SRE POV: we can SLO the sync endpoints if they\\u2019re predictable. if you put \\u201caggregate over last 7d by tag=customer_id\\u201d into the same service, that SLO becomes meaningless. we\\u2019ll be oncall for BI.\\n\\nLogan Wright: telemetry reality check: token-level events have some lag + late arrivals. if Console expects real-time exactness for dashboards, sync aggregation will also look \\u201cwrong\\u201d until lag catches up.\\n\\nChloe Martin: what if the design is:\\n- sync endpoints are ONLY for request-bounded queries\\n  - `estimate` (given request inputs)\\n  - `breakdown` (given request_id)\\n- dashboards use async aggregates computed from the same primitives (hourly/daily rollups)\\nConsole calls an aggregates API that\\u2019s backed by precomputed tables, not raw telemetry.\\n\\nThomas Baird: yes. \\u201cCost Model API\\u201d doesn\\u2019t have to mean \\u201cdo all analytics live.\\u201d it can serve *standardized cost primitives* + read from rollups.\\n\\nBenji Okafor: + caching. Console will spam the same query during page load / refresh. we should explicitly document recommended caching TTLs for dashboard queries.\\n\\nEthan Park: if we add an aggregates endpoint, should it be async job-based (`POST /aggregate:query` -> job_id -> `GET /aggregate:result`), or synchronous but only for precomputed buckets?\\n\\nAllison Grant: if it\\u2019s precomputed buckets, synchronous is ok. make the contract explicit:\\n- max time window\\n- fixed granularity options\\n- max group-by dimensions\\n- bounded response size\\nOtherwise you\\u2019ll be reinventing a query engine.\\n\\nJada Williams: +1. job-based will add a lot of product complexity in Console (polling, empty states, etc). if we can keep it \\u201csync read from rollups\\u201d with strict bounds, that\\u2019s preferable.\\n\\nRafael Mendes: job-based also creates a new failure mode (jobs stuck / queue backed up). I\\u2019d avoid unless necessary.\\n\\nLogan Wright: we can get rollups in the analytics pipeline. easiest path: cost-model service reads from `cost_rollup_hourly` (or whatever) keyed by (org, env, model_id, route, region, deployment_mode). Anything beyond that is \\u201cgo to analytics.\\u201d\\n\\nThomas Baird: constraints I\\u2019d like in writing (rough numbers):\\n- max lookback: 30d\\n- min granularity: 1h\\n- max series returned: 200 (after top-k)\\n- group_by limited to <=2 dims\\n- server-enforced `top_k` + \\u201cother\\u201d bucket\\n\\nChloe Martin: that works for the current Console mocks. we mostly need model/route + deployment mode. maybe region.\\n\\nMarissa Cole: product view: we should be clear in UI when numbers are \\u201cestimated/standardized cost\\u201d vs \\u201cinvoice total.\\u201d support tickets are already coming in on mismatch.\\n\\nEthan Park: ok, so answer is: sync is fine for request-bounded stuff; dashboards should not call raw aggregation sync. use precomputed rollups (sync read) w/ bounds.\\n\\nCostOps Bot: :memo: Reminder: ENG-4821/4822 are tracking service + schema; please add follow-up tasks in the epic if new endpoints are introduced.\\n\\nBenji Okafor: propose language for design spec:\\n- \\u201cThe Cost Model API MUST be safe for synchronous invocation by internal services. Endpoints MUST have predictable complexity and bounded response size.\\u201d\\n- \\u201cAggregate views MUST be served from precomputed rollups; ad hoc scans are out of scope.\\u201d\\n\\nAllison Grant: also add: \\u201cIf rollups are stale due to telemetry lag, service returns `data_freshness` header/field.\\u201d helps Console annotate.\\n\\nLogan Wright: we can provide `fresh_through_ts` per org/env. easy.\\n\\nJada Williams: for Console integration, we\\u2019ll implement fallback:\\n- if cost-model aggregate endpoint errors or is slow, show cached last-known + banner\\n- for request drill-down, if cost-model breakdown fails, hide breakdown section and log metric (don\\u2019t 500 the page)\\n\\nRafael Mendes: +1. please make sure we track:\\n- `cost_model_api.degraded` flag rate\\n- timeouts vs 5xx separately\\nAnd set sane timeouts (e.g., 250ms client-side for sync endpoints).\\n\\nThomas Baird: action item: I\\u2019ll drop a comment on the design spec doc re: explicit bounds + top-k behavior.\\n\\nEthan Park: I\\u2019ll update the v1 design spec with: (a) sync bounded endpoints, (b) aggregates-from-rollups, and (c) freshness semantics. thanks all. :thumbsup:\\n\\nChloe Martin: :thumbsup: when you update, tag me + Jada so we can sanity check against Console mock payload needs.\\n\\nEthan Park: will do.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"channel\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"text\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_9f800429ef72472f94b65368044df633\"\n}",

{
  "channel": "eng-platform",
  "thread_ts": "1769536063",
  "first_message_ts": "1769536063",
  "last_message_ts": "1769539748",
  "participants": [
    "Ethan Park",
    "Chloe Martin",
    "Thomas Baird",
    "Rafael Mendes",
    "Allison Grant",
    "Benji Okafor",
    "Logan Wright",
    "Jada Williams",
    "Marissa Cole",
    "CostOps Bot"
  ],
  "text": "Ethan Park: quick q for folks thinking about Console integration: should the cost-model API be called synchronously on the request path, or should Console only consume async aggregates (dashboards) and keep request-path stuff out of it?

Chloe Martin: for Console, the cost breakdown page is effectively “hot path” when customers click around, but not *the* inference request path. still needs to be snappy (sub-second) and reliable.

Thomas Baird: +1 to being careful. if we make the API do heavy aggregation synchronously over high-cardinality telemetry (filters + group-bys) we’ll get cardinality blowups and p95 will go sideways.

Benji Okafor: I think we’re mixing 2 use cases:
1) per-request estimate/breakdown (bounded inputs, deterministic)
2) time-window aggregates for dashboards (potentially huge)
We can do (1) sync. (2) should be async or pre-aggregated.

Jada Williams: Console pages we’re building:
- “Request details” drill-down (single request_id) => sync call is fine
- “Cost by model/route over time” (time series) => we currently query analytics tables. if this becomes sync cost-model API doing the same scan, that’ll be bad.

Allison Grant: observability principle: anything that can fan out / scan should not sit behind a synchronous API in the user click path unless it’s strictly bounded and cached.

Ethan Park: makes sense. was thinking whether we should force Console to only use async “reporting” endpoints so we don’t get pulled into dashboard-style queries.

Rafael Mendes: from SRE POV: we can SLO the sync endpoints if they’re predictable. if you put “aggregate over last 7d by tag=customer_id” into the same service, that SLO becomes meaningless. we’ll be oncall for BI.

Logan Wright: telemetry reality check: token-level events have some lag + late arrivals. if Console expects real-time exactness for dashboards, sync aggregation will also look “wrong” until lag catches up.

Chloe Martin: what if the design is:
- sync endpoints are ONLY for request-bounded queries
  - `estimate` (given request inputs)
  - `breakdown` (given request_id)
- dashboards use async aggregates computed from the same primitives (hourly/daily rollups)
Console calls an aggregates API that’s backed by precomputed tables, not raw telemetry.

Thomas Baird: yes. “Cost Model API” doesn’t have to mean “do all analytics live.” it can serve *standardized cost primitives* + read from rollups.

Benji Okafor: + caching. Console will spam the same query during page load / refresh. we should explicitly document recommended caching TTLs for dashboard queries.

Ethan Park: if we add an aggregates endpoint, should it be async job-based (`POST /aggregate:query` -> job_id -> `GET /aggregate:result`), or synchronous but only for precomputed buckets?

Allison Grant: if it’s precomputed buckets, synchronous is ok. make the contract explicit:
- max time window
- fixed granularity options
- max group-by dimensions
- bounded response size
Otherwise you’ll be reinventing a query engine.

Jada Williams: +1. job-based will add a lot of product complexity in Console (polling, empty states, etc). if we can keep it “sync read from rollups” with strict bounds, that’s preferable.

Rafael Mendes: job-based also creates a new failure mode (jobs stuck / queue backed up). I’d avoid unless necessary.

Logan Wright: we can get rollups in the analytics pipeline. easiest path: cost-model service reads from `cost_rollup_hourly` (or whatever) keyed by (org, env, model_id, route, region, deployment_mode). Anything beyond that is “go to analytics.”

Thomas Baird: constraints I’d like in writing (rough numbers):
- max lookback: 30d
- min granularity: 1h
- max series returned: 200 (after top-k)
- group_by limited to <=2 dims
- server-enforced `top_k` + “other” bucket

Chloe Martin: that works for the current Console mocks. we mostly need model/route + deployment mode. maybe region.

Marissa Cole: product view: we should be clear in UI when numbers are “estimated/standardized cost” vs “invoice total.” support tickets are already coming in on mismatch.

Ethan Park: ok, so answer is: sync is fine for request-bounded stuff; dashboards should not call raw aggregation sync. use precomputed rollups (sync read) w/ bounds.

CostOps Bot: :memo: Reminder: ENG-4821/4822 are tracking service + schema; please add follow-up tasks in the epic if new endpoints are introduced.

Benji Okafor: propose language for design spec:
- “The Cost Model API MUST be safe for synchronous invocation by internal services. Endpoints MUST have predictable complexity and bounded response size.”
- “Aggregate views MUST be served from precomputed rollups; ad hoc scans are out of scope.”

Allison Grant: also add: “If rollups are stale due to telemetry lag, service returns `data_freshness` header/field.” helps Console annotate.

Logan Wright: we can provide `fresh_through_ts` per org/env. easy.

Jada Williams: for Console integration, we’ll implement fallback:
- if cost-model aggregate endpoint errors or is slow, show cached last-known + banner
- for request drill-down, if cost-model breakdown fails, hide breakdown section and log metric (don’t 500 the page)

Rafael Mendes: +1. please make sure we track:
- `cost_model_api.degraded` flag rate
- timeouts vs 5xx separately
And set sane timeouts (e.g., 250ms client-side for sync endpoints).

Thomas Baird: action item: I’ll drop a comment on the design spec doc re: explicit bounds + top-k behavior.

Ethan Park: I’ll update the v1 design spec with: (a) sync bounded endpoints, (b) aggregates-from-rollups, and (c) freshness semantics. thanks all. :thumbsup:

Chloe Martin: :thumbsup: when you update, tag me + Jada so we can sanity check against Console mock payload needs.

Ethan Park: will do.",

\"Done\",\n  \"priority\": \"P0\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-06\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-02-14\",\n  \"creator\": \"Marissa Cole\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Talia Benson\",\n  \"project\": \"Standard Cost Model Spec + API\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W02\",\n  \"estimate\": \"5\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-01-24\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"cost-model\",\n    \"prd\",\n    \"console\",\n    \"optimize\",\n \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"description\": \"We need a single PRD that sets v1 scope and a shared definition of \\u201cinference cost\\u201d so Console dashboards and Optimize ROI estimates stop diverging across telemetry, billing hooks, and ad-hoc models.\\n\\nThis ticket covers:\\n- Drafting the Standard Cost Model PRD (problem, goals/non-goals, v1 scope, phased rollout)\\n- Socializing with stakeholders (Platform, Telemetry, Runtime, Console, Optimize, SRE, Finance)\\n- Capturing decisions + open questions (especially breakdown taxonomy + overhead allocation)\\n- Defining measurable success metrics + acceptance criteria for \\u201cv1 shipped\\u201d\\n\\nOut of scope for this PM ticket: implementing endpoints/schemas (tracked in ENG tickets).\",\n  \"problem_statement\": \"Today we have inconsistent cost numbers and semantics across:\\n- Console cost breakdown views (observability)\\n- Optimize \\u201cwhat-if\\u201d savings estimates\\n- Telemetry aggregation and attribution\\n- Billing hooks / invoicing primitives\\n\\nCommon failure modes:\\n- Prefill vs decode token accounting differs between runtime metrics and downstream aggregation\\n- Cache hits and batch efficiency are represented differently across teams (units/definitions)\\n- Quantization impacts (throughput/memory/quality constraints) aren\\u2019t modeled consistently\\n- Overhead allocation is treated inconsistently (request-attributable vs pooled costs)\\n\\nResult: Customers and internal teams can\\u2019t trust cost breakdowns; support escalations occur when Console does not match invoice totals or when ROI claims appear inflated.\",\n  \"goals\": [\n    \"Publish a v1 PRD that defines canonical cost semantics and the minimum fields/endpoints needed for Console + Optimize adoption in Q1 2026.\",\n    \"Align on a versioned spec + API approach (owned by Platform) with backward compatibility rules.\",\n    \"Define how standardized cost outputs map to finance/unit economics reporting (including overhead allocation policy and reporting windows).\",\n    \"Set measurable success criteria (latency budget, drift tolerances, adoption milestones, supportability).\"\n  ],\n  \"non_goals\": [\n    \"Replacing billing/RevRec systems (cost model is not the system of record for invoicing).\",\n    \"Shipping a customer-facing pricing calculator in v1.\",\n    \"Perfectly modeling every hardware SKU/edge case in v1; we will define an extension path (v2+) with explicit versioning.\"\n  ],\n  \"v1_scope_must_haves\": [\n    \"Canonical cost breakdown taxonomy for v1 (prefill vs decode; cache attribution; batching efficiency; overhead allocation category).\",\n    \"Versioned schema package (inputs/outputs) with deterministic semantics (same inputs => same outputs).\",\n    \"Internal Cost Model API endpoints for: per-request estimate, aggregated breakdown (bounded), and limited what-if projections for config changes.\",\n    \"Schema version negotiation guidance for clients (Console/Optimize) and deprecation rules.\",\n    \"Telemetry input contracts: required runtime + metering fields, units, and data quality checks.\",\n    \"Rollout plan with feature flags, fallback behavior, and validation dashboards (predicted vs observed spend drift).\"\n  ],\n  \"v1_scope_nice_to_haves\": [\n    \"Confidence intervals for what-if projections (where data supports it) and explicit \\u2018assumptions\\u2019 surfaced in response metadata.\",\n    \"Region/SKU-level overhead breakdown for finance drill-down (may be v2 depending on data availability).\",\n    \"Self-serve debugging UI for internal support to compare invoice vs standardized primitives.\"\n  ],\n  \"personas_and_use_cases\": \"Console (Chloe/Jada/Felix):\\n- Show cost breakdown by route/model/customer/workspace for dashboards.\\n- Must be fast for hot paths; requires bounded payloads and caching guidance.\\n\\nOptimize (Aditya/Maya/Jonas):\\n- Compute ROI of recommendations (batching, caching, quantization) using a what-if endpoint.\\n- Must include guardrails (parameter bounds, assumptions) to avoid optimistic or misleading estimates.\\n\\nFinance/FP&A (Laura/Rishi):\\n- Consume standardized primitives to improve unit economics reporting consistency.\\n- Needs stability across reporting windows + explicit overhead allocation policy.\\n\\nSRE/Platform:\\n- Operate a reliable internal service with SLOs and drift monitoring; manage schema version distribution.\",\n  \"success_metrics\": \"Product metrics:\\n- Console cost breakdown pages powered by Cost Model API for >= 80% of workspaces within 2 weeks of GA (behind feature flag initially).\\n- Optimize ROI calculations for batching/caching/quantization using standardized outputs for >= 90% of recommendations shown to users (excluding explicitly unsupported models).\\n\\nQuality metrics:\\n- Drift SLI: aggregated predicted cost vs observed spend within agreed tolerance band for stable workloads (initial target: within 5\\u201310% weekly, with documented exclusions for telemetry lag and known gaps).\\n- Support: reduce cost mismatch tickets tagged \\u201cConsole vs invoice\\u201d by 50% within 1 quarter post-launch.\\n\\nOperational metrics:\\n- API p95 latency within budget for Console hot path (target to be set in design spec; PRD proposes p95 <= 150ms for cached/steady-state estimate calls, <= 400ms for uncached within bounded inputs).\\n- Error rate within SLO target (tbd by SRE) and automatic fallback behavior does not degrade Console UX.\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria_v1\": \"PRD is considered complete when:\\n1) The PRD is published in Confluence and reviewed/approved (explicit +1) by Platform, Telemetry, Console, Optimize, SRE, and Finance stakeholders.\\n2) v1 breakdown taxonomy is written unambiguously with examples (what counts as prefill vs decode, how cache hits are attributed, what overhead categories exist).\\n3) v1 endpoint list and required fields are defined (even if exact schema is finalized in ENG-4822).\\n4) v1 rollout plan is defined: feature flags, staging validation, canary/rollback conditions, and ownership.\\n5) Open questions are documented with owners and dates for resolution (no unresolved \\u201cblocking\\u201d items).\\n\\nLaunch readiness criteria (to be verified later during implementation):\\n- Conformance tests/golden fixtures exist for core computations.\\n- Drift dashboard exists and is reviewed with SRE + Finance.\\n- Console and Optimize integration plans have explicit fallback behavior if API is degraded.\",\n  \"stakeholders\": [\n    \"Priya Natarajan (Exec sponsor, Platform)\",\n    \"Ethan Park (Service/API lead)\",\n    \"Logan Wright (Telemetry lead)\",\n    \"Chloe Martin (Console integration lead)\",\n    \"Aditya Rao (Optimize product owner)\",\n    \"Dr. Maya Srinivasan (Applied ML sponsor)\",\n    \"Rafael Mendes (SRE reliability lead)\",\n    \"Laura Bennett (Finance stakeholder)\"\n  ],\n  \"stakeholder_review_checklist\": \"Platform / Control Plane (Ethan/Benji/Kaitlyn/Cole):\\n- [ ] rollout\\n\\nTelemetry & Analytics (Logan/Nadia/Caleb/Mei/Thomas):\\n- [ ] Inputs are available or have a committed instrumentation plan\\n- [ ] Units/definitions for token accounting and cache/batch metrics are precise\\n- [ ] Aggregation strategy does not explode cardinality\\n\\nRuntime Scheduling/Kernels (Sofia/Omar/Grace):\\n- [ ] Prefill/decode split aligns with runtime realities\\n- [ ] Quantization identifiers and execution paths can be modeled deterministically\\n\\nConsole (Chloe/Jada/Felix/Marissa):\\n- [ ] Required fields for UI breakdown tables are covered (and optional fields have safe defaults)\\n- [ ] Latency expectations and caching guidance are acceptable\\n- [ ] Fallback behavior is defined (what happens if service is unavailable)\\n\\nOptimize (Aditya/Maya/Jonas/Arjun/Hassan):\\n- [ ] What-if parameters are expressive enough for v1 recommendations\\n- [ ] Guardrails prevent unrealistic ROI projections\\n- [ ] Response includes assumptions/confidence where relevant\\n\\nSRE (Rafael/Allison):\\n- [ ] SLOs/SLIs proposed (availability/latency/drift correctness) are measurable\\n- [ ] Alerting risks and telemetry lag considerations are called out\\n\\nFinance/FP&A (Laura/Rishi):\\n- [ ] Overhead allocation policy is reflected in breakdown outputs\\n- [ ] Reporting window stability and change management are addressed\",\n  \"open_questions\": [\n    \"Overhead allocation: exact categories and whether overhead is returned as a separate component or folded into unit costs (owner: Laura Bennett + Ethan Park).\",\n    \"Drift definition: what is the \\u2018observed\\u2019 comparator (GPU spend by pool? amortized commitments?) and what exclusions apply (owner: Rafael Mendes + Rishi Malhotra).\",\n    \"Cache attribution: how to attribute shared KV cache benefits across requests (owner: Omar El-Sayed + Nadia Rahman).\",\n    \"What-if warm cache assumption: whether to include a cache warm-rate input in v1 or defer to v2 (owner: Jonas Weber + Ethan Park).\",\n    \"Bounding: max number of breakdown dimensions returned per query for Console (owner: Jada Williams + Thomas Baird).\"\n  ],\n  \"risks_and_mitigations\": \"Risk: Cardinality blowups for aggregated breakdown endpoints.\\nMitigation: Enforce strict request bounds; provide top-K + \\u2018other\\u2019 buckets; require time window   "customer_impact": "medium",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "We need a single PRD that sets v1 scope and a shared definition of \u201cinference cost\u201d so Console dashboards and Optimize ROI estimates stop diverging across telemetry, billing hooks, and ad-hoc models.\n\nThis ticket covers:\n- Drafting the Standard Cost Model PRD (problem, goals/non-goals, v1 scope, phased rollout)\n- Socializing with stakeholders (Platform, Telemetry, Runtime, Console, Optimize, SRE, Finance)\n- Capturing decisions + open questions (especially breakdown taxonomy + overhead allocation)\n- Defining measurable success metrics + acceptance criteria for \u201cv1 shipped\u201d\n\nOut of scope for this PM ticket: implementing endpoints/schemas (tracked in ENG tickets).",
  "problem_statement": "Today we have inconsistent cost numbers and semantics across:\n- Console cost breakdown views (observability)\n- Optimize \u201cwhat-if\u201d savings estimates\n- Telemetry aggregation and attribution\n- Billing hooks / invoicing primitives\n\nCommon failure modes:\n- Prefill vs decode token accounting differs between runtime metrics and downstream aggregation\n- Cache hits and batch efficiency are represented differently across teams (units/definitions)\n- Quantization impacts (throughput/memory/quality constraints) aren\u2019t modeled consistently\n- Overhead allocation is treated inconsistently (request-attributable vs pooled costs)\n\nResult: Customers and internal teams can\u2019t trust cost breakdowns; support escalations occur when Console does not match invoice totals or when ROI claims appear inflated.",
  "goals": [
    "Publish a v1 PRD that defines canonical cost semantics and the minimum fields/endpoints needed for Console + Optimize adoption in Q1 2026.",
    "Align on a versioned spec + API approach (owned by Platform) with backward compatibility rules.",
    "Define how standardized cost outputs map to finance/unit economics reporting (including overhead allocation policy and reporting windows).",
    "Set measurable success criteria (latency budget, drift tolerances, adoption milestones, supportability)."
  ],
  "non_goals": [
    "Replacing billing/RevRec systems (cost model is not the system of record for invoicing).",
    "Shipping a customer-facing pricing calculator in v1.",
    "Perfectly modeling every hardware SKU/edge case in v1; we will define an extension path (v2+) with explicit versioning."
  ],
  "v1_scope_must_haves": [
    "Canonical cost breakdown taxonomy for v1 (prefill vs decode; cache attribution; batching efficiency; overhead allocation category).",
    "Versioned schema package (inputs/outputs) with deterministic semantics (same inputs => same outputs).",
    "Internal Cost Model API endpoints for: per-request estimate, aggregated breakdown (bounded), and limited what-if projections for config changes.",
    "Schema version negotiation guidance for clients (Console/Optimize) and deprecation rules.",
    "Telemetry input contracts: required runtime + metering fields, units, and data quality checks.",
    "Rollout plan with feature flags, fallback behavior, and validation dashboards (predicted vs observed spend drift)."
  ],
  "v1_scope_nice_to_haves": [
    "Confidence intervals for what-if projections (where data supports it) and explicit \u2018assumptions\u2019 surfaced in response metadata.",
    "Region/SKU-level overhead breakdown for finance drill-down (may be v2 depending on data availability).",
    "Self-serve debugging UI for internal support to compare invoice vs standardized primitives."
  ],
  "personas_and_use_cases": "Console (Chloe/Jada/Felix):\n- Show cost breakdown by route/model/customer/workspace for dashboards.\n- Must be fast for hot paths; requires bounded payloads and caching guidance.\n\nOptimize (Aditya/Maya/Jonas):\n- Compute ROI of recommendations (batching, caching, quantization) using a what-if endpoint.\n- Must include guardrails (parameter bounds, assumptions) to avoid optimistic or misleading estimates.\n\nFinance/FP&A (Laura/Rishi):\n- Consume standardized primitives to improve unit economics reporting consistency.\n- Needs stability across reporting windows + explicit overhead allocation policy.\n\nSRE/Platform:\n- Operate a reliable internal service with SLOs and drift monitoring; manage schema version distribution.",
  "success_metrics": "Product metrics:\n- Console cost breakdown pages powered by Cost Model API for >= 80% of workspaces within 2 weeks of GA (behind feature flag initially).\n- Optimize ROI calculations for batching/caching/quantization using standardized outputs for >= 90% of recommendations shown to users (excluding explicitly unsupported models).\n\nQuality metrics:\n- Drift SLI: aggregated predicted cost vs observed spend within agreed tolerance band for stable workloads (initial target: within 5\u201310% weekly, with documented exclusions for telemetry lag and known gaps).\n- Support: reduce cost mismatch tickets tagged \u201cConsole vs invoice\u201d by 50% within 1 quarter post-launch.\n\nOperational metrics:\n- API p95 latency within budget for Console hot path (target to be set in design spec; PRD proposes p95 <= 150ms for cached/steady-state estimate calls, <= 400ms for uncached within bounded inputs).\n- Error rate within SLO target (tbd by SRE) and automatic fallback behavior does not degrade Console UX.",
  "acceptance_criteria_v1": "PRD is considered complete when:\n1) The PRD is published in Confluence and reviewed/approved (explicit +1) by Platform, Telemetry, Console, Optimize, SRE, and Finance stakeholders.\n2) v1 breakdown taxonomy is written unambiguously with examples (what counts as prefill vs decode, how cache hits are attributed, what overhead categories exist).\n3) v1 endpoint list and required fields are defined (even if exact schema is finalized in ENG-4822).\n4) v1 rollout plan is defined: feature flags, staging validation, canary/rollback conditions, and ownership.\n5) Open questions are documented with owners and dates for resolution (no unresolved \u201cblocking\u201d items).\n\nLaunch readiness criteria (to be verified later during implementation):\n- Conformance tests/golden fixtures exist for core computations.\n- Drift dashboard exists and is reviewed with SRE + Finance.\n- Console and Optimize integration plans have explicit fallback behavior if API is degraded.",
  "stakeholders": [
    "Priya Natarajan (Exec sponsor, Platform)",
    "Ethan Park (Service/API lead)",
    "Logan Wright (Telemetry lead)",
    "Chloe Martin (Console integration lead)",
    "Aditya Rao (Optimize product owner)",
    "Dr. Maya Srinivasan (Applied ML sponsor)",
    "Rafael Mendes (SRE reliability lead)",
    "Laura Bennett (Finance stakeholder)"
  ],
  "stakeholder_review_checklist": "Platform / Control Plane (Ethan/Benji/Kaitlyn/Cole):\n- [ ] Endpoint list + request bounds are feasible for hot paths\n- [ ] Auth/tenancy model is consistent with internal service standards\n- [ ] Versioning/deprecation policy is compatible with multi-client rollout\n\nTelemetry & Analytics (Logan/Nadia/Caleb/Mei/Thomas):\n- [ ] Inputs are available or have a committed instrumentation plan\n- [ ] Units/definitions for token accounting and cache/batch metrics are precise\n- [ ] Aggregation strategy does not explode cardinality\n\nRuntime Scheduling/Kernels (Sofia/Omar/Grace):\n- [ ] Prefill/decode split aligns with runtime realities\n- [ ] Quantization identifiers and execution paths can be modeled deterministically\n\nConsole (Chloe/Jada/Felix/Marissa):\n- [ ] Required fields for UI breakdown tables are covered (and optional fields have safe defaults)\n- [ ] Latency expectations and caching guidance are acceptable\n- [ ] Fallback behavior is defined (what happens if service is unavailable)\n\nOptimize (Aditya/Maya/Jonas/Arjun/Hassan):\n- [ ] What-if parameters are expressive enough for v1 recommendations\n- [ ] Guardrails prevent unrealistic ROI projections\n- [ ] Response includes assumptions/confidence where relevant\n\nSRE (Rafael/Allison):\n- [ ] SLOs/SLIs proposed (availability/latency/drift correctness) are measurable\n- [ ] Alerting risks and telemetry lag considerations are called out\n\nFinance/FP&A (Laura/Rishi):\n- [ ] Overhead allocation policy is reflected in breakdown outputs\n- [ ] Reporting window stability and change management are addressed",
  "open_questions": [
    "Overhead allocation: exact categories and whether overhead is returned as a separate component or folded into unit costs (owner: Laura Bennett + Ethan Park).",
    "Drift definition: what is the \u2018observed\u2019 comparator (GPU spend by pool? amortized commitments?) and what exclusions apply (owner: Rafael Mendes + Rishi Malhotra).",
    "Cache attribution: how to attribute shared KV cache benefits across requests (owner: Omar El-Sayed + Nadia Rahman).",
    "What-if warm cache assumption: whether to include a cache warm-rate input in v1 or defer to v2 (owner: Jonas Weber + Ethan Park).",
    "Bounding: max number of breakdown dimensions returned per query for Console (owner: Jada Williams + Thomas Baird)."
  ],
  "risks_and_mitigations": "Risk: Cardinality blowups for aggregated breakdown endpoints.\nMitigation: Enforce strict request bounds; provide top-K + \u2018other\u2019 buckets; require time window constraints; pre-aggregation where needed.\n\nRisk: Console performance regression due to synchronous dependency.\nMitigation: Provide caching guidance + client library; require fallbacks to existing estimates when service is degraded; stage rollout behind feature flags.\n\nRisk: Drift alerts fire due to telemetry lag, causing low trust in system.\nMitigation: Define lag-aware SLIs; add lag signals to dashboards; use backfill for comparisons; document expected lag.\n\nRisk: Optimize ROI claims become misleading due to optimistic assumptions.\nMitigation: Guardrails + bounded parameter ranges; surface assumptions and confidence; require conservative defaults.\n\nRisk: Finance reporting instability due to schema/semantics changes.\nMitigation: Versioned schema, explicit deprecation windows, and release notes tied to reporting windows.",
  "rollout_plan_summary": "Phase 1 (Discovery): inventory current definitions; confirm Console/Optimize v1 requirements; agree on minimal v1 fields.\nPhase 2 (Spec): publish schema semantics + ADRs; finalize breakdown taxonomy and overhead policy.\nPhase 3 (Implementation): ship service/library + conformance tests.\nPhase 4 (Integration): Console + Optimize behind flags; validate against drift dashboards; run backtests.\nPhase 5 (Launch): expand flag rollout; publish governance docs and runbooks; begin deprecation of legacy cost paths.",
  "links": [
    "Confluence PRD (target): sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/standard-cost-model-prd.json",
    "Design spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/cost-model-api-v1-design-spec.json",
    "ADR-021: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-021-standardize-cost-model-interfaces.json",
    "ADR-022: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-022-cost-breakdown-taxonomy.json",
    "Console mock payloads: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts/console-cost-breakdown-mock-data.json",
    "Optimize working doc: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/optimize/cost-model-v1-field-requirements-working-doc.json",
    "Customer support mismatch ticket: sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-31844-console-cost-breakdown-does-not-match-invoice.json"
  ],
  "comments": [
    "2026-01-06 (Marissa Cole): Creating PRD ticket. Console needs consistent breakdown fields + clear definitions of prefill/decode + cache attribution; we\u2019ve had repeated customer confusion when charts don\u2019t match invoice totals.",
    "2026-01-08 (Talia Benson): Draft PRD outline prepared. Scheduling stakeholder review sessions (Platform, Telemetry, Optimize, Finance). Goal is to lock v1 must-haves by end of week 3.",
    "2026-01-12 (Aditya Rao): Optimize request: what-if endpoint must support batching and KV cache scenarios. We can live without per-layer kernel details in v1, but need quantization profile IDs + guardrails to avoid inflated savings.",
    "2026-01-14 (Ethan Park): Platform feedback: PRD should explicitly state request bounding + determinism requirements. Also call out schema version negotiation strategy for Console/Optimize clients.",
    "2026-01-16 (Laura Bennett): Finance note: overhead allocation must be explicit and stable for reporting windows. We can accept a separate overhead line item in v1; avoid silently changing unit costs mid-quarter without a version bump + comms.",
    "2026-01-20 (Rafael Mendes): SRE request: PRD should define a drift SLI at a high level and acknowledge telemetry lag. Recommend adding \u2018telemetry freshness\u2019 signals so drift alerts aren\u2019t noisy.",
    "2026-01-23 (Talia Benson): PRD v1 draft shared for final review. Remaining open items: cache warm-rate assumption for Optimize, and exact overhead category naming.",
    "2026-02-03 (Talia Benson): PRD published in Confluence with v1 scope and success metrics. Captured open questions with owners; unblocked ENG-4822 schema work to proceed with agreed taxonomy.",
    "2026-02-14 (Marissa Cole): Marking Done. All required stakeholder approvals recorded; rollout and validation plan aligns with Console feature flag approach and Finance overhead policy email thread."
  ],

    "id": "dsid_d2166cc007154e879c65495d8cba1ac0",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4821-cost-model-service-skeleton.json",
    "title": "Create Cost Model service skeleton (routing, auth/tenancy middleware, and endpoint scaffolding)",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-4821\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Create Cost Model service skeleton (routing, auth/tenancy middleware, and endpoint scaffolding)\",\n  \"status\": \"Done\",\n  \"priority\": \"P0\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-06\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-01-22\",\n  \"creator\": \"Ethan Park\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Benji Okafor\",\n  \"project\": \"Standard Cost Model Spec + API\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W02\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-01-23\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"standard-cost-model\",\n    \"cost-model-api\",\n    \"platform-control-plane\",\n    \"service-skeleton\",\n    \"auth-tenancy\",\n    \"routing\",\n    \"observability\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-4822\",\n    \"ENG-4830\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"medium\",\n  \"release\": \"platform-2026.02\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"true\",\n  \"description\": \"Goal\\nCreate the initial monorepo service skeleton for the internal Cost Model API so downstream work (schema wiring, telemetry inputs, and Console/Optimize adoption) has a stable, reviewable foundation.\\n\\nThis ticket is intentionally NOT implementing the cost math. It establishes:\\n- Service scaffolding + deployable binary/container\\n- Request routing (internal gateway -> service), tenancy/auth middleware, and request bounds\\n- Endpoint stubs and response envelope conventions\\n- Baseline observability (metrics, tracing, logs), config plumbing, and CI wiring\\n\\nContext\\nWe are standardizing cost primitives so Console + Optimize + billing hooks use the same canonical definitions. Early work has been blocked by each team prototyping their own endpoint shapes and auth patterns. This skeleton should lock in the service shape and safety rails before we start filling in computation logic.\\n\\nScope / Deliverables\\n1) New service package in monorepo\\n- Service name: cost-model-service (internal)\\n- Build target + docker image + dev runner\\n- Standard service config (env, region, stage) aligned to platform conventions\\n\\n2) Routing + auth/tenancy\\n- Internal-only endpoint exposure (no public edge)\\n- Service-to-service auth: verify Redwood internal identity token (OIDC) OR mTLS identity, depending on environment\\n- Enforce org_id + project_id/tenant_id resolution via standard tenancy middleware\\n- Authorize callers: Console backend + Optimize backend + billing hooks (service principals)\\n- Reject cross-tenant access; emit audit log fields (caller, org_id, project_id, request_id)\\n\\n3) Endpoint scaffolding (stubs)\\nImplement handlers with request/response scaffolding (no cost calculations yet). Target endpoints for v1:\\n- POST /internal/cost-model/v1/estimate\\n- POST /internal/cost-model/v1/breakdown\\n- POST /internal/cost-model/v1/what-if\\n\\nMinimum behavior:\\n- Validate payload size and high-level required fields (don\\u2019t parse deeply until ENG-4822 lands)\\n- Return 501 Not Implemented for computation fields, but with stable error shape and request_id\\n- Support schema_version negotiation header (draft):\\n  - Request header: X-Redwood-Cost-Schema-Version: 1\\n  - Response header: X-Redwood-Cost-Schema-Version: 1\\n  - If unknown version: return 400 with explicit error code COST_SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED\\n\\n4) Request bounding / safety rails (initial)\\n- Max request body size (proposed: 256KB)\\n- Max items per request for batch estimation (proposed: 200)\\n- Timeouts: server handler timeout 250ms (stubs should be fast); client guidance will be in ENG-4830\\n- Add placeholders for cache layer hooks (no caching logic required in this ticket)\\n\\n5) Observability + runbook hooks\\n- Metrics: request_count, error_count by route + status_code, latency_ms p50/p95\\n- Structured logs including request_id, caller_service, org_id, schema_version\\n- Tracing: propagate trace context from caller; create server spans per endpoint\\n- Dashboard links placeholder (Grafana) and oncall ownership annotation\\n\\nNon-goals\\n- Implementing cost computations or breakdown taxonomy (tracked in ENG-4822, ADRs)\\n- Telemetry ingestion/aggregation pipelines (ENG-4823)\\n- Client library (ENG-4830)\\n- Any customer-facing exposure or docs beyond internal engineering notes\\n\\nImplementation notes\\n- Use standard Redwood service template (http server + middleware stack)\\n- Tenancy middleware should use the shared control-plane resolver (same as quotas/billing hooks)\\n- Prefer consistent error envelope fields:\\n  - error_code (stable string)\\n  - message (human readable)\\n  - request_id\\n  - retryable (true/false)\\n\\nAcceptance Criteria\\n- [x] Service builds in CI and runs locally with a stub config\\n- [x] Endpoints are reachable behind internal gateway in staging\\n- [x] AuthN: requests without valid service identity are rejected\\n- [x] AuthZ: tenancy middleware rejects cross-org access; audit fields are logged\\n- [x] Request bounds enforced (payload size + item count)\\n- [x] Standard error shape implemented for validation/auth/version errors\\n- [x] Metrics + traces emitted and visible in staging\\n- [x] Security review checklist completed (internal-only, auth, logging)\\n\\nTesting\\n- Unit tests: middleware ordering, auth failure modes, version header validation, bounds checks\\n- Smoke test in staging: curl via internal tooling using Console service principal\\n\\nLinks\\n- Confluence design spec (draft): sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/cost-model-api-v1-design-spec.json\\n- API guidelines addendum: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/cost-model-api-guidelines.json\\n- Related tickets: ENG-4822 (schema v1), ENG-4823 (telemetry inputs), ENG-4830 (client library)\\n\\nRollout plan\\n- Stage 1: deploy skeleton to staging only, allowlisted callers (console-backend-stg, optimize-backend-stg)\\n- Stage 2: deploy to prod with endpoints returning 501 but fully authenticated/authorized (safe no-op)\\n- Stage 3: begin enabling estimate endpoint once schema + computation lands (separate ticket/PR)\\n\\nOwner\\nBenji Okafor (Platform Control Plane)\\n\\nReviewers (suggested)\\n- Kaitlyn Nguyen (auth/tenancy)\\n- Chloe Martin (Console integration)\\n- Aditya Rao / Jonas Weber (Optimize what-if expectations)\\n- Rafael Mendes (SRE: SLO/alerts readiness)\",\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2026-01-07 (Ethan Park): Please keep the routing path internal-only. We should not accidentally make this reachable from public edge. Also align error envelope with existing quota-service errors so Console can reuse parsing.\",\n    \"2026-01-08 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): For auth, in prod we should prefer the standard s2s OIDC token verification. mTLS identity is fine for local/dev. Make sure org_id resolution comes from the tenancy resolver middleware, not caller-provided fields.\",\n    \"2026-01-10 (Rafael Mendes): Add basic RED metrics + tracing now, even if endpoints are 501. Otherwise we\\u2019ll be blind during Console integration. Also please annotate the service with oncall=platform-control-plane in the service registry metadata.\",\n    \"2026-01-14 (Benji Okafor): Implemented skeleton using the standard service template. Added middleware stack: request_id -> tracing -> authn -> tenancy -> bounds -> handler. Endpoints return COST_NOT_IMPLEMENTED with request_id. Pushing PR for review.\",\n    \"2026-01-16 (Chloe Martin): Thanks. One request: keep latency overhead minimal since Console may call this on hot paths. Please ensure no synchronous calls to telemetry store are added in this skeleton (even as placeholders).\",\n    \"2026-01-20 (Benji Okafor): Updated to enforce max 256KB and max_items=200 (configurable). Added version header validation and error_code COST_SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED. Added basic Prometheus metrics + structured logs.\",\n    \"2026-01-22 (Ethan Park): Approved. Marking done; follow-ups will land in ENG-4822/4823/4830. Please confirm prod deploy is internal-only + allowlisted.\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"comments\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_d2166cc007154e879c65495d8cba1ac0\"\n}",
