document.title: Create Cost Model service skeleton (routing, auth/tenancy middleware, and endpoint scaffolding)
document.content:
{
  "key": "ENG-4821",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Create Cost Model service skeleton (routing, auth/tenancy middleware, and endpoint scaffolding)",
  "status": "Done",
  "priority": "P0",
  "created_at": "2026-01-06",
  "updated_at": "2026-01-22",
  "creator": "Ethan Park",
  "assignee": "Benji Okafor",
  "project": "Standard Cost Model Spec + API",
  "cycle": "2026-W02",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2026-01-23",
  "labels": [
    "standard-cost-model",
    "cost-model-api",
    "platform-control-plane",
    "service-skeleton",
    "auth-tenancy",
    "routing",
    "observability"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-4822",
    "ENG-4830"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "medium",
  "release": "platform-2026.02",
  "security_review_required": "true",
  "description": "Goal
Create the initial monorepo service skeleton for the internal Cost Model API so downstream work (schema wiring, telemetry inputs, and Console/Optimize adoption) has a stable, reviewable foundation.

This ticket is intentionally NOT implementing the cost math. It establishes:
- Service scaffolding + deployable binary/container
- Request routing (internal gateway -> service), tenancy/auth middleware, and request bounds
- Endpoint stubs and response envelope conventions
- Baseline observability (metrics, tracing, logs), config plumbing, and CI wiring

Context
We are standardizing cost primitives so Console + Optimize + billing hooks use the same canonical definitions. Early work has been blocked by each team prototyping their own endpoint shapes and auth patterns. This skeleton should lock in the service shape and safety rails before we start filling in computation logic.

Scope / Deliverables
1) New service package in monorepo
- Service name: cost-model-service (internal)
- Build target + docker image + dev runner
- Standard service config (env, region, stage) aligned to platform conventions

2) Routing + auth/tenancy
- Internal-only endpoint exposure (no public edge)
- Service-to-service auth: verify Redwood internal identity token (OIDC) OR mTLS identity, depending on environment
- Enforce org_id + project_id/tenant_id resolution via standard tenancy middleware
- Authorize callers: Console backend + Optimize backend + billing hooks (service principals)
- Reject cross-tenant access; emit audit log fields (caller, org_id, project_id, request_id)

3) Endpoint scaffolding (stubs)
Implement handlers with request/response scaffolding (no cost calculations yet). Target endpoints for v1:
- POST /internal/cost-model/v1/estimate
- POST /internal/cost-model/v1/breakdown
- POST /internal/cost-model/v1/what-if

Minimum behavior:
- Validate payload size and high-level required fields (don’t parse deeply until ENG-4822 lands)
- Return 501 Not Implemented for computation fields, but with stable error shape and request_id
- Support schema_version negotiation header (draft):
  - Request header: X-Redwood-Cost-Schema-Version: 1
  - Response header: X-Redwood-Cost-Schema-Version: 1
  - If unknown version: return 400 with explicit error code COST_SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED

4) Request bounding / safety rails (initial)
- Max request body size (proposed: 256KB)
- Max items per request for batch estimation (proposed: 200)
- Timeouts: server handler timeout 250ms (stubs should be fast); client guidance will be in ENG-4830
- Add placeholders for cache layer hooks (no caching logic required in this ticket)

5) Observability + runbook hooks
- Metrics: request_count, error_count by route + status_code, latency_ms p50/p95
- Structured logs including request_id, caller_service, org_id, schema_version
- Tracing: propagate trace context from caller; create server spans per endpoint
- Dashboard links placeholder (Grafana) and oncall ownership annotation

Non-goals
- Implementing cost computations or breakdown taxonomy (tracked in ENG-4822, ADRs)
- Telemetry ingestion/aggregation pipelines (ENG-4823)
- Client library (ENG-4830)
- Any customer-facing exposure or docs beyond internal engineering notes

Implementation notes
- Use standard Redwood service template (http server + middleware stack)
- Tenancy middleware should use the shared control-plane resolver (same as quotas/billing hooks)
- Prefer consistent error envelope fields:
  - error_code (stable string)
  - message (human readable)
  - request_id
  - retryable (true/false)

Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Service builds in CI and runs locally with a stub config
- [x] Endpoints are reachable behind internal gateway in staging
- [x] AuthN: requests without valid service identity are rejected
- [x] AuthZ: tenancy middleware rejects cross-org access; audit fields are logged
- [x] Request bounds enforced (payload size + item count)
- [x] Standard error shape implemented for validation/auth/version errors
- [x] Metrics + traces emitted and visible in staging
- [x] Security review checklist completed (internal-only, auth, logging)

Testing
- Unit tests: middleware ordering, auth failure modes, version header validation, bounds checks
- Smoke test in staging: curl via internal tooling using Console service principal

Links
- Confluence design spec (draft): sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/cost-model-api-v1-design-spec.json
- API guidelines addendum: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/cost-model-api-guidelines.json
- Related tickets: ENG-4822 (schema v1), ENG-4823 (telemetry inputs), ENG-4830 (client library)

Rollout plan
- Stage 1: deploy skeleton to staging only, allowlisted callers (console-backend-stg, optimize-backend-stg)
- Stage 2: deploy to prod with endpoints returning 501 but fully authenticated/authorized (safe no-op)
- Stage 3: begin enabling estimate endpoint once schema + computation lands (separate ticket/PR)

Owner
Benji Okafor (Platform Control Plane)

Reviewers (suggested)
- Kaitlyn Nguyen (auth/tenancy)
- Chloe Martin (Console integration)
- Aditya Rao / Jonas Weber (Optimize what-if expectations)
- Rafael Mendes (SRE: SLO/alerts readiness)",
  "comments": [
    "2026-01-07 (Ethan Park): Please keep the routing path internal-only. We should not accidentally make this reachable from public edge. Also align error envelope with existing quota-service errors so Console can reuse parsing.",
    "2026-01-08 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): For auth, in prod we should prefer the standard s2s OIDC token verification. mTLS identity is fine for local/dev. Make sure org_id resolution comes from the tenancy resolver middleware, not caller-provided fields.",
    "2026-01-10 (Rafael Mendes): Add basic RED metrics + tracing now, even if endpoints are 501. Otherwise we’ll be blind during Console integration. Also please annotate the service with oncall=platform-control-plane in the service registry metadata.",
    "2026-01-14 (Benji Okafor): Implemented skeleton using the standard service template. Added middleware stack: request_id -> tracing -> authn -> tenancy -> bounds -> handler. Endpoints return COST_NOT_IMPLEMENTED with request_id. Pushing PR for review.",
    "2026-01-16 (Chloe Martin): Thanks. One request: keep latency overhead minimal since Console may call this on hot paths. Please ensure no synchronous calls to telemetry store are added in this skeleton (even as placeholders).",
    "2026-01-20 (Benji Okafor): Updated to enforce max 256KB and max_items=200 (configurable). Added version header validation and error_code COST_SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED. Added basic Prometheus metrics + structured logs.",
    "2026-01-22 (Ethan Park): Approved. Marking done; follow-ups will land in ENG-4822/4823/4830. Please confirm prod deploy is internal-only + allowlisted."
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "comments"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_d2166cc007154e879c65495d8cba1ac0"
}

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_7a665e549f804bd9aef1dbd6c4650487",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4822-define-cost-model-schema-v1.json",
    "title": "Define Standard Cost Model schema v1 (inputs/outputs), versioning rules, and codegen",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-4822\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Define Standard Cost Model schema v1 (inputs/outputs), versioning rules, and codegen\",\n  \"status\": \"Done\",\n  \"priority\": \"P0\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-08\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-02-18\",\n  \"creator\": \"Ethan Park\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Benji Okafor\",\n  \"project\": \"Standard Cost Model Spec + API\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W03\",\n  \"estimate\": \"5\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-02-14\",\n  \"customer_impact\": \"medium\",\n  \"release\": \"platform-2026.02\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"cost-model\",\n    \"schema\",\n    \"versioning\",\n    \"codegen\",\n    \"api-contract\",\n    \"console\",\n    \"optimize\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"PM-1482\",\n    \"ENG-4821\",\n    \"ENG-4823\"\n  ],\n  \"sub_issues\": [\n    \"ENG-4828\",\n    \"ENG-4829\",\n    \"ENG-4831\"\n  ],\n  \"description\": \"Context\\nWe currently have multiple cost definitions floating around (Console aggregation, billing hooks, Optimize prototypes). This ticket defines the canonical schema for Standard Cost Model v1 so that:\\n- Console cost breakdowns and Optimize ROI/what-if both call the same API and interpret the same fields.\\n- Telemetry + runtime exported metrics can be normalized into stable cost primitives.\\n- Finance can rely on the same breakdown categories for reporting windows.\\n\\nScope\\nDefine schema package v1:\\n1) Request-level inputs (what the cost model needs to compute cost)\\n2) Request-level outputs (canonical breakdown + totals)\\n3) Aggregation output shapes (bounded, queryable)\\n4) What-if input/output shapes (guardrailed)\\n5) Versioning + compatibility policy (major/minor/patch)\\n6) Codegen strategy and repo/package layout\\n\\nNon-goals\\n- Not implementing the service endpoints (see ENG-4821 / ENG-4824).\\n- Not replacing billing system of record; these are standardized primitives.\\n\\nProposed schema package layout (monorepo)\\n- package: redwood.costmodel.schema\\n- versions: v1 (frozen once shipped), v1alpha (if needed for iteration behind flags)\\n- generated targets: Go (server + client), TypeScript (Console/Optimize), JSON schema for validation + docs\\n\\nSchema v1: key concepts\\nA) Determinism and boundedness\\n- For identical inputs, the model should produce identical outputs (no dependence on wall clock, random sampling, or unbounded lookups).\\n- Bounded response size: breakdown taxonomy is fixed; any per-dimension breakdown must be top-K with \\\"other\\\" bucket.\\n\\nB) Versioning and negotiation\\n- version string is explicit in requests/outputs: schema_version = \\\"cost-model/v1\\\".\\n- Backward compatibility:\\n  - Additive fields allowed in minor updates; consumers must ignore unknown fields.\\n  - Semantics changes require major version bump.\\n  - Field removals only via deprecation window (>= 2 releases) and major bump.\\n- Service supports a \\\"min_version\\\"/\\\"max_version\\\" negotiation header in client library (implemented in ENG-4830), but schema package defines the canonical strings and behavior.\\n\\nC) Canonical identifiers\\n- model_id: stable Redwood model catalog ID (e.g., \\\"rwqwen2.5-72b-instruct\\\")\\n- model_revision: immutable revision hash / semver (ties to weights + runtime profile)\\n- quant_profile_id: stable profile ID from model catalog (ENG-4829)\\n- deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private\\n- tenant_id, project_id, environment: used for tenancy + routing, not for breakdown grouping by default\\n- compute_sku: normalized GPU SKU identifier (e.g., \\\"h100-sxm-80gb\\\")\\n\\nSchema v1: Inputs (RequestCostInput)\\nRequired (v1 must-have)\\n- request_id: UUID (caller-generated OK)\\n- timestamp_ms: event time of the request (for joining to telemetry windows; not used for nondeterministic pricing)\\n- tenant_id, project_id\\n- deployment_mode\\n- region\\n- model_id, model_revision\\n- quant_profile_id (\\\"fp16\\\" / \\\"int8\\\" / \\\"w4a16\\\" etc. as stable IDs, not free-form)\\n- token_accounting:\\n  - prompt_tokens\\n  - generated_tokens\\n  - prefill_tokens (if available; otherwise = prompt_tokens)\\n  - decode_tokens (if available; otherwise = generated_tokens)\\n  - tokenizer_id (optional; for diagnostics)\\n- runtime_observations (all optional-but-highly-recommended; if omitted we fall back to default profiles):\\n  - batch_size_effective_avg\\n  - queue_time_ms\\n  - kv_cache_hit_rate (0..1) and kv_cache_bytes_read/write (if available)\\n  - stage_time_ms_prefill / stage_time_ms_decode (optional; used for sanity checks)\\n  - fallback_taken: true/false + fallback_reason (if request served by compatible variant)\\n- routing_context:\\n  - route_id (Console uses this dimension heavily)\\n  - policy_id (routing policy version)\\n\\nExplicitly out of v1 inputs\\n- No per-layer kernel counters; too high-cardinality and unstable.\\n- No raw GPU telemetry join keys; those stay in telemetry store, not request payload.\\n\\nSchema v1: Outputs (RequestCostOutput)\\n- schema_version\\n- request_id\\n- currency: \\\"USD\\\" (v1 fixed; multi-currency later)\\n- total_cost_usd: decimal string (avoid float; clients must parse)\\n- breakdown_usd: fixed taxonomy with explicit semantics:\\n  - compute_prefill_usd\\n  - compute_decode_usd\\n  - kv_cache_read_usd\\n  - kv_cache_write_usd\\n  - network_egress_usd (0 unless known; v1 can be stubbed)\\n  - overhead_allocated_usd (allocated platform overhead; see ADR-022 + finance policy)\\n  - discounts_credits_usd (must be 0 for internal cost; billing can apply separately)\\n- attribution:\\n  - cost_basis: \\\"estimated\\\" | \\\"observed\\\" (v1 mostly \\\"estimated\\\"; \\\"observed\\\" allowed for replay/backfill pipelines)\\n  - confidence: \\\"high\\\" | \\\"medium\\\" | \\\"low\\\" (for Optimize what-if and incomplete runtime observations)\\n  - warnings: list of warning codes (e.g., \\\"MISSING_KV_CACHE_METRICS\\\", \\\"DEFAULT_BATCH_EFFICIENCY_ASSUMED\\\")\\n\\nSchema v1: Aggregation (bounded)\\n- Query shapes live in the API design spec, but schema must include canonical response types:\\n  - AggregatedCostBreakdown: totals + breakdown by fixed dimensions (route_id, model_id, deployment_mode) with top-K semantics.\\n  - Always include \\\"other\\\" bucket when top-K is used.\\n  - Include sample_count and token totals to support dashboard normalization.\\n\\nSchema v1: What-if inputs/outputs\\n- WhatIfCostInput:\\n  - baseline_workload_summary: {prompt_tokens_p50/p95, decode_tokens_p50/p95, qps_avg, concurrency_avg} (encoded as flat fields in schema; avoid nested maps)\\n  - baseline_config: {batching_enabled, caching_enabled, quant_profile_id}\\n  - proposed_config: same fields\\n  - constraints: {max_p95_latency_ms, min_quality_tier}\\n- WhatIfCostOutput:\\n  - baseline_total_cost_usd\\n  - proposed_total_cost_usd\\n  - delta_usd\\n  - delta_percent\\n  - confidence and assumptions: list of assumption codes (e.g., \\\"CACHE_WARM_RATE_ASSUMED_0P7\\\")\\n\\nNotes on overhead allocation (v1)\\n- Overhead is explicitly shown as overhead_allocated_usd.\\n- v1 policy: allocate overhead proportionally to request-attributable compute (prefill+decode) within a reporting window; exact policy parameters are not embedded in schema, but output must carry an overhead_policy_id string for auditability.\\n\\nCodegen + validation\\n- Generate:\\n  - Go types + JSON marshal/unmarshal with strict validation (unknown fields allowed, but required fields enforced)\\n  - TypeScript types for Console/Optimize\\n  - JSON Schema artifact for docs and conformance tests\\n- Validation rules (examples):\\n  - token counts >= 0\\n  - confidence enum constrained\\n  - kv_cache_hit_rate in [0,1]\\n  - cost fields are decimal strings with max 6 fractional digits\\n\\nReviewers / sign-off\\n- Console: Chloe Martin, Jada Williams (confirm required fields for breakdown pages; ensure response shapes support top-K and \\\"other\\\")\\n- Optimize: Aditya Rao, Jonas Weber (confirm what-if fields and confidence/assumptions model)\\n- Telemetry: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman (confirm availability of runtime_observations and token splits)\\n- Finance: Laura Bennett/Rishi Malhotra (confirm overhead representation and auditability)\\n\\nAcceptance criteria\\n- Schema v1 types merged as a versioned package with docs comments describing semantics (especially overhead_allocated_usd, prefill vs decode, cache read/write).\\n- Codegen outputs present for Go + TS, and serialization tests pass.\\n- Conformance tests include at least 5 golden examples covering: cache hit, cache miss, batching effect, quant profile change, fallback route.\\n- Review approvals recorded from Console + Optimize.\\n\\nLinks\\n- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/standard-cost-model-prd.json\\n- API design spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/cost-model-api-v1-design-spec.json\\n- ADR-021: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-021-standardize-cost-model-interfaces.json\\n- ADR-022: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-022-cost-breakdown-taxonomy.json\\n- Proto outline (early): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/cost-model-api-proto-outline.json\\n\\nImplementation notes / decisions made in this ticket\\n- Use decimal strings for money fields to avoid float drift across languages.\\n- Keep taxonomy fields explicit (no map<string, number>) to ensure boundedness and stable dashboards.\\n- Prefer stable IDs (quant_profile_id, compute_sku) rather than free-form strings for long-lived analytics.\\n\\nFollow-ups\\n- If runtime cannot provide prefill/decode split reliably, v1 must define fallback semantics (prefill=prompt_tokens, decode=generated_tokens) and surface warning code.\\n- If network egress cannot be measured per request, keep network_egress_usd at 0 in v1 and document it as \\\"not modeled\\\".\\n\",\n Please include sample_count and token totals in aggregated response types so we can normalize per 1k tokens.\",\n    \"2026-01-15 (Aditya Rao): For Optimize what-if, we need a place to express confidence + assumptions. document.title: Define Standard Cost Model schema v1 (inputs/outputs), versioning rules, and codegen
document.content:
{
  "key": "ENG-4822",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Define Standard Cost Model schema v1 (inputs/outputs), versioning rules, and codegen",
  "status": "Done",
  "priority": "P0",
  "created_at": "2026-01-08",
  "updated_at": "2026-02-18",
  "creator": "Ethan Park",
  "assignee": "Benji Okafor",
  "project": "Standard Cost Model Spec + API",
  "cycle": "2026-W03",
  "estimate": "5",
  "due_date": "2026-02-14",
  "customer_impact": "medium",
  "release": "platform-2026.02",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "labels": [
    "cost-model",
    "schema",
    "versioning",
    "codegen",
    "api-contract",
    "console",
    "optimize"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "PM-1482",
    "ENG-4821",
    "ENG-4823"
  ],
  "sub_issues": [
    "ENG-4828",
    "ENG-4829",
    "ENG-4831"
  ],
  "description": "Context
We currently have multiple cost definitions floating around (Console aggregation, billing hooks, Optimize prototypes). This ticket defines the canonical schema for Standard Cost Model v1 so that:
- Console cost breakdowns and Optimize ROI/what-if both call the same API and interpret the same fields.
- Telemetry + runtime exported metrics can be normalized into stable cost primitives.
- Finance can rely on the same breakdown categories for reporting windows.

Scope
Define schema package v1:
1) Request-level inputs (what the cost model needs to compute cost)
2) Request-level outputs (canonical breakdown + totals)
3) Aggregation output shapes (bounded, queryable)
4) What-if input/output shapes (guardrailed)
5) Versioning + compatibility policy (major/minor/patch)
6) Codegen strategy and repo/package layout

Non-goals
- Not implementing the service endpoints (see ENG-4821 / ENG-4824).
- Not replacing billing system of record; these are standardized primitives.

Proposed schema package layout (monorepo)
- package: redwood.costmodel.schema
- versions: v1 (frozen once shipped), v1alpha (if needed for iteration behind flags)
- generated targets: Go (server + client), TypeScript (Console/Optimize), JSON schema for validation + docs

Schema v1: key concepts
A) Determinism and boundedness
- For identical inputs, the model should produce identical outputs (no dependence on wall clock, random sampling, or unbounded lookups).
- Bounded response size: breakdown taxonomy is fixed; any per-dimension breakdown must be top-K with "other" bucket.

B) Versioning and negotiation
- version string is explicit in requests/outputs: schema_version = "cost-model/v1".
- Backward compatibility:
  - Additive fields allowed in minor updates; consumers must ignore unknown fields.
  - Semantics changes require major version bump.
  - Field removals only via deprecation window (>= 2 releases) and major bump.
- Service supports a "min_version"/"max_version" negotiation header in client library (implemented in ENG-4830), but schema package defines the canonical strings and behavior.

C) Canonical identifiers
- model_id: stable Redwood model catalog ID (e.g., "rwqwen2.5-72b-instruct")
- model_revision: immutable revision hash / semver (ties to weights + runtime profile)
- quant_profile_id: stable profile ID from model catalog (ENG-4829)
- deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private
- tenant_id, project_id, environment: used for tenancy + routing, not for breakdown grouping by default
- compute_sku: normalized GPU SKU identifier (e.g., "h100-sxm-80gb")

Schema v1: Inputs (RequestCostInput)
Required (v1 must-have)
- request_id: UUID (caller-generated OK)
- timestamp_ms: event time of the request (for joining to telemetry windows; not used for nondeterministic pricing)
- tenant_id, project_id
- deployment_mode
- region
- model_id, model_revision
- quant_profile_id ("fp16" / "int8" / "w4a16" etc. as stable IDs, not free-form)
- token_accounting:
  - prompt_tokens
  - generated_tokens
  - prefill_tokens (if available; otherwise = prompt_tokens)
  - decode_tokens (if available; otherwise = generated_tokens)
  - tokenizer_id (optional; for diagnostics)
- runtime_observations (all optional-but-highly-recommended; if omitted we fall back to default profiles):
  - batch_size_effective_avg
  - queue_time_ms
  - kv_cache_hit_rate (0..1) and kv_cache_bytes_read/write (if available)
  - stage_time_ms_prefill / stage_time_ms_decode (optional; used for sanity checks)
  - fallback_taken: true/false + fallback_reason (if request served by compatible variant)
- routing_context:
  - route_id (Console uses this dimension heavily)
  - policy_id (routing policy version)

Explicitly out of v1 inputs
- No per-layer kernel counters; too high-cardinality and unstable.
- No raw GPU telemetry join keys; those stay in telemetry store, not request payload.

Schema v1: Outputs (RequestCostOutput)
- schema_version
- request_id
- currency: "USD" (v1 fixed; multi-currency later)
- total_cost_usd: decimal string (avoid float; clients must parse)
- breakdown_usd: fixed taxonomy with explicit semantics:
  - compute_prefill_usd
  - compute_decode_usd
  - kv_cache_read_usd
  - kv_cache_write_usd
  - network_egress_usd (0 unless known; v1 can be stubbed)
  - overhead_allocated_usd (allocated platform overhead; see ADR-022 + finance policy)
  - discounts_credits_usd (must be 0 for internal cost; billing can apply separately)
- attribution:
  - cost_basis: "estimated" | "observed" (v1 mostly "estimated"; "observed" allowed for replay/backfill pipelines)
  - confidence: "high" | "medium" | "low" (for Optimize what-if and incomplete runtime observations)
  - warnings: list of warning codes (e.g., "MISSING_KV_CACHE_METRICS", "DEFAULT_BATCH_EFFICIENCY_ASSUMED")

Schema v1: Aggregation (bounded)
- Query shapes live in the API design spec, but schema must include canonical response types:
  - AggregatedCostBreakdown: totals + breakdown by fixed dimensions (route_id, model_id, deployment_mode) with top-K semantics.
  - Always include "other" bucket when top-K is used.
  - Include sample_count and token totals to support dashboard normalization.

Schema v1: What-if inputs/outputs
- WhatIfCostInput:
  - baseline_workload_summary: {prompt_tokens_p50/p95, decode_tokens_p50/p95, qps_avg, concurrency_avg} (encoded as flat fields in schema; avoid nested maps)
  - baseline_config: {batching_enabled, caching_enabled, quant_profile_id}
  - proposed_config: same fields
  - constraints: {max_p95_latency_ms, min_quality_tier}
- WhatIfCostOutput:
  - baseline_total_cost_usd
  - proposed_total_cost_usd
  - delta_usd
  - delta_percent
  - confidence and assumptions: list of assumption codes (e.g., "CACHE_WARM_RATE_ASSUMED_0P7")

Notes on overhead allocation (v1)
- Overhead is explicitly shown as overhead_allocated_usd.
- v1 policy: allocate overhead proportionally to request-attributable compute (prefill+decode) within a reporting window; exact policy parameters are not embedded in schema, but output must carry an overhead_policy_id string for auditability.

Codegen + validation
- Generate:
  - Go types + JSON marshal/unmarshal with strict validation (unknown fields allowed, but required fields enforced)
  - TypeScript types for Console/Optimize
  - JSON Schema artifact for docs and conformance tests
- Validation rules (examples):
  - token counts >= 0
  - confidence enum constrained
  - kv_cache_hit_rate in [0,1]
  - cost fields are decimal strings with max 6 fractional digits

Reviewers / sign-off
- Console: Chloe Martin, Jada Williams (confirm required fields for breakdown pages; ensure response shapes support top-K and "other")
- Optimize: Aditya Rao, Jonas Weber (confirm what-if fields and confidence/assumptions model)
- Telemetry: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman (confirm availability of runtime_observations and token splits)
- Finance: Laura Bennett/Rishi Malhotra (confirm overhead representation and auditability)

Acceptance criteria
- Schema v1 types merged as a versioned package with docs comments describing semantics (especially overhead_allocated_usd, prefill vs decode, cache read/write).
- Codegen outputs present for Go + TS, and serialization tests pass.
- Conformance tests include at least 5 golden examples covering: cache hit, cache miss, batching effect, quant profile change, fallback route.
- Review approvals recorded from Console + Optimize.

Links
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/standard-cost-model-prd.json
- API design spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/cost-model-api-v1-design-spec.json
- ADR-021: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-021-standardize-cost-model-interfaces.json
- ADR-022: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-022-cost-breakdown-taxonomy.json
- Proto outline (early): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/cost-model-api-proto-outline.json

Implementation notes / decisions made in this ticket
- Use decimal strings for money fields to avoid float drift across languages.
- Keep taxonomy fields explicit (no map<string, number>) to ensure boundedness and stable dashboards.
- Prefer stable IDs (quant_profile_id, compute_sku) rather than free-form strings for long-lived analytics.

Follow-ups
- If runtime cannot provide prefill/decode split reliably, v1 must define fallback semantics (prefill=prompt_tokens, decode=generated_tokens) and surface warning code.
- If network egress cannot be measured per request, keep network_egress_usd at 0 in v1 and document it as "not modeled".
",
  "comments": [
    "2026-01-10 (Ethan Park): Kicking off schema work. Please keep fields explicit; we got bitten before by map-based breakdowns blowing up cardinality and dashboards.",
    "2026-01-13 (Chloe Martin): Console needs (1) route_id always present, (2) top-K breakdown by model_id within a time range, (3) explicit prefill vs decode numbers. Please include sample_count and token totals in aggregated response types so we can normalize per 1k tokens.",
    "2026-01-15 (Aditya Rao): For Optimize what-if, we need a place to express confidence + assumptions. Not every projection is equally reliable; please include a structured list of assumption codes, even if it’s just strings in v1.",
    "2026-01-18 (Nadia Rahman): Token split availability: prompt_tokens and generated_tokens are reliable; prefill/decode split depends on runtime export (ENG-4828/PR-28509). Suggest schema marks prefill/decode optional but defines fallback semantics + warning code.",
    "2026-01-22 (Laura Bennett): Finance requirement: overhead must be explicit and auditable. Add overhead_policy_id and make sure discounts/credits are not mixed into internal cost; billing can overlay later.",
    "2026-02-03 (Benji Okafor): Drafted schema comments + validation rules. Using decimal strings for costs, enums for confidence/cost_basis, and stable IDs for model/quant. Will send for final review once codegen is wired.",
    "2026-02-12 (Jada Williams): Please document that overhead_allocated_usd may not sum perfectly at the single-request level due to windowed allocation, but aggregates should reconcile within tolerance. Add note to docs comments.",
    "2026-02-18 (Ethan Park): Marking done after merge of schema package + serialization tests. Next: service wiring + client library version negotiation."
  ],
  "attachments": [
    "GitHub PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-28451-add-cost-model-schema-package-v1.json"
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "comments"
  ],

}

document.title: Console cost breakdown: switch to Cost Model API behind feature flag
document.content:
{
  "key": "ENG-4825",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Console cost breakdown: switch to Cost Model API behind feature flag",
  "status": "In Review",
  "priority": "P0",
  "created_at": "2026-01-15",
  "updated_at": "2026-02-22",
  "creator": "Talia Benson",
  "assignee": "Chloe Martin",
  "project": "Standard Cost Model Spec + API",
  "cycle": "2026-W07",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2026-02-27",
  "labels": [
    "console",
    "cost-model",
    "feature-flag",
    "observability",
    "migration"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-4821",
    "ENG-4822",
    "ENG-4823",
    "ENG-4830"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "console-2026.03",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Console cost breakdown pages currently compute/request cost fields using a mix of legacy telemetry aggregations + inline heuristics, which do not always match billing hooks and have drift/definition mismatches (prefill vs decode, cache hits, overhead allocation, etc.).

This ticket migrates Console backend cost breakdown to call the internal Cost Model API v1 and render the canonical, versioned breakdown (and per-request estimate where needed), behind a feature flag with safe fallback to the legacy path.

Primary goals:
- Replace Console’s legacy cost breakdown computation with Cost Model API v1 responses for supported views.
- Ensure breakdown taxonomy matches ADR-022 (prefill/decode, cache, batching, overhead allocation, quantization deltas as applicable).
- Ship behind feature flag with staged rollout (dev -> staging -> prod small %) and clear rollback.
- Add metrics to compare legacy vs new output and track drift, latency impact, and error rates.

Non-goals:
- Changing customer-facing pricing or invoice calculations.
- Building new UI experiences; this is a backend data source swap + minimal response mapping.

References:
- Confluence PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/standard-cost-model-prd.json
- Design spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/cost-model-api-v1-design-spec.json
- API guidelines: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/cost-model-api-guidelines.json
- ADRs: adr-021-standardize-cost-model-interfaces, adr-022-cost-breakdown-taxonomy
- Console mock payloads: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts/console-cost-breakdown-mock-data.json

Implementation notes (current plan):
1) Console backend calls cost-model-service using the shared client library (ENG-4830) with:
   - schema version negotiation (pin to v1 for initial rollout)
   - timeouts (<= 250ms per request on hot path; fall back if exceeded)
   - retries only for safe/idempotent endpoints and only if under request budget
2) Feature flag:
   - Flag name: console.cost_breakdown.use_cost_model_api
   - Default: off
   - Per-tenant allowlist + per-environment overrides
3) Fallback behavior:
   - If Cost Model API is unavailable, times out, or returns non-retryable errors, fallback to legacy breakdown (existing behavior) and emit a metric with error code.
   - If response is partial (bounded results) still render but annotate internal debug logs; do not break UI.
4) Caching:
   - Apply short-lived caching (e.g., 30–60s) for dashboard aggregate breakdown queries where request parameters are stable and cardinality is bounded.
   - No caching for per-request drilldowns where IDs are unique; rely on cost-model-service internal memoization.
5) Bounds/pagination:
   - Ensure Console requests remain within cost-model API bounding rules (time range limits, top-N dimensions, etc.).
   - Avoid “group-by everything” patterns that explode cardinality.

Scope: Console backend endpoints
- cost breakdown summary panels (by model, route, deployment mode)
- time series breakdown charts (bounded buckets)
- drilldown table for top contributors (bounded top-N)

Out of scope for v1 in Console:
- what-if projections (Optimize only)
- cost breakdown by arbitrary user-defined tags beyond the standard dimension set (needs v2 taxonomy + API support)

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Flagged path returns breakdown values populated from Cost Model API v1 for staging + prod.
- [ ] Console renders without regressions (no missing columns, stable totals) for supported views.
- [ ] Legacy vs new totals differ by <= 3% at p50 and <= 8% at p95 on the validation dataset/time windows, excluding known exceptions documented below.
- [ ] Added metrics:
      - cost_breakdown_source (legacy vs cost_model_api)
      - fallback_reason (timeout, 5xx, 4xx, schema_mismatch)
      - latency impact (p50/p95/p99 on Console endpoint)
      - “diff metrics” comparing legacy vs cost-model totals in shadow mode
- [ ] Rollout playbook documented in ticket + linked in release notes.

Known exceptions / intentional differences (must be documented as they come up):
- Overhead allocation: Console legacy path does not include certain shared overhead components; Cost Model v1 may include a request-attributable overhead line item depending on deployment mode and policy window.
- Telemetry lag: cost-model computations may differ from near-real-time legacy views when upstream token metering is delayed.

Risks:
- Latency regression for Console hot routes if cost-model calls are synchronous and uncached.
- Cardinality explosion if Console requests unbounded group-bys.
- Schema mismatches during early adoption (unknown fields / version negotiation).

Test plan:
- Unit tests: response mapping from Cost Model API -> Console DTOs (including missing optional fields).
- Integration tests: staging fixtures from golden datasets; verify deterministic output.
- Shadow mode: in prod, compute both legacy and cost-model outputs for a small % and emit diffs without changing UI (or internal-only headers/logs).
- Load test: exercise dashboard endpoints over typical query patterns; confirm overhead is within performance budget.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: dev/staging only, flag on by default in staging for internal tenants.
- Phase 1: prod allowlist (Redwood internal + 1–2 friendly customers) with shadow diffs enabled.
- Phase 2: ramp to 10% tenants, monitor latency/errors/drift dashboards.
- Phase 3: ramp to 50% then 100% after 1 week stable; keep legacy fallback for one full release cycle.

Links to related work:
- Client library: ENG-4830
- Drift SLI/alerts: ENG-4827
- Billing hooks alignment: ENG-4832
- GitHub PR (expected): pr-28470-console-cost-breakdown-switch-to-cost-model-api.json",
  "comments": [
    "2026-01-16 - Chloe Martin: Kicked off. Met w/ Jada + Felix to enumerate Console endpoints that currently compute cost breakdown.     "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-4827\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Define drift SLI and configure monitoring + alerts for Cost Model API\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P0\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-17\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-02-20\",\n  \"creator\": \"Ethan Park\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Rafael Mendes\",\n  \"project\": \"Standard Cost Model Spec + API\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W07\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-02-28\",\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"cost-model\",\n    \"observability\",\n    \"sre\",\n    \"sli-slo\",\n    \"finance-alignment\",\n    \"telemetry\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-4823\",\n    \"ENG-4821\",\n    \"ENG-4828\",\n    \"ENG-4831\"\n  ],\n  \"related_links\": [\n    \"Confluence: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/cost-model-api-observability.json\",\n    \"Confluence: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/cost-model-api-slo.json\",\n    \"Confluence: sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/cost-model-api-incident-runbook.json\",\n    \"Drive: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/observability/cost-drift-analysis-notes.json\",\n    \"Slack incident thread: sources/slack/incidents/1769032199.json\",\n    \"Slack SRE thread: sources/slack/eng-sre/1768793301.json\",\n    \"GitHub: sources/github/redwood/pr-28490-cost-model-drift-monitoring-job.json\",\n    \"GitHub: sources/github/observability-pack/pr-391-add-cost-model-api-dashboards.json\"\n  ],\n  \"description\": \"We need a single, auditable drift SLI definition for the Standard Cost Model initiative, plus a monitoring pipeline that continuously compares predicted (cost-model outputs) vs observed (infra spend / GPU-seconds-derived cost) and alerts when drift exceeds thresholds. This is required before Console flips cost breakdowns broadly and before Finance treats standard cost outputs as a reliable unit-econ primitive.\\n\\nContext: We already saw a drift alert fire due to telemetry lag (see incidents thread 1769032199). This ticket formalizes drift semantics, adds lag-awareness + volume guardrails, and ships actionable dashboards + paging rules.\\n\\nDeliverables:\\n- Drift SLI definition (v1) with explicit formulae, inclusion/exclusion rules, and windowing/lag policy.\\n- Scheduled drift monitoring job/pipeline emitting Prometheus metrics (bounded cardinality).\\n- Grafana dashboard + alert rules (warn/page) with runbook links and clear next steps.\\n\\nNon-goals:\\n- Perfect cost reconciliation to invoices (billing system of record remains separate).\\n- Per-customer drift alerts at high cardinality (we will do top-K / aggregate-first in v1).\\n\\nPrimary stakeholders: Rafael Mendes (SRE), Logan Wright / Mei Lin (Telemetry), Ethan Park (API), Laura Bennett / Rishi Malhotra (FP&A).\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": \"- Drift SLI v1 is documented and reviewed by SRE + Telemetry + Finance (written definition + examples).\\n- Drift pipeline runs on schedule in prod and emits:\\n  - drift_ratio metrics for 1h/6h/24h windows\\n  - telemetry_lag_seconds + data_freshness indicators\\n  - sample sizes (request_count / token_count / gpu_seconds) for gating\\n- Alerting:\\n  - P0 page when sustained high drift and volume gate is met\\n  - P1 warning when drift elevated but below page threshold\\n  - Separate alert for telemetry lag (to avoid false positives)\\n- Dashboard provides drill-down to top contributors with bounded series (top-N + \\u201cother\\u201d).\\n- Runbook section updated with \\u201cdrift\\u201d triage steps + common causes (telemetry lag, schema mismatch, runtime metric regression, overhead allocation changes).\\n- Backtest on last 14 days shows alert thresholds don\\u2019t flap (documented).\",\n  \"sli_definition_v1\": \"Name: cost_model.drift (v1)\\n\\nGoal: quantify how far Cost Model predicted cost deviates from observed infrastructure-derived cost over a fixed reporting window, after applying the same allocation policy.\\n\\nDefinitions:\\n- Predicted cost (P): Sum of cost-model \\u2018request_attributable_total_usd\\u2019 over the window, computed from cost-model primitives (prefill/decode, cache, batch efficiency, quantization profile) using schema version pinned per environment.\\n- Observed cost (O): Infra-derived cost over the same window, mapped to the same attribution scope:\\n  - v1 uses GPU-seconds * effective_usd_per_gpu_second by cluster/SKU/region/deployment_mode\\n  - excludes non-GPU line items and one-time credits\\n  - includes request-attributable overhead per the agreed overhead allocation policy (see Finance thread/email; implemented as overhead_multiplier or overhead_usd bucket)\\n\\nDrift ratio:\\n- drift_ratio = (P - O) / max(O, O_floor)\\n- O_floor is to avoid division noise; v1 O_floor = $50 per window (configurable).\\n\\nWindowing & freshness:\\n- Compute over rolling windows: 1h, 6h, 24h.\\n- Apply a data-lag offset: exclude the most recent 2 hours from both P and O when computing drift (configurable) unless telemetry freshness guarantees improve.\\n\\nGating (to reduce noise):\\n- Only emit window-level drift alerts when:\\n  - request_count >= 10,000 OR token_count >= 50M OR observed_cost >= $200 for that window (thresholds configurable by env)\\n\\nDimensions (bounded):\\n- Always emit global (no dimensions) drift.\\n- Emit limited breakdown by:\\n  - deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private)\\n  - region\\n  - hardware_sku\\n  - model_id (top 10 by observed_cost in the window) + \\u201cother\\u201d\\n- No per-tenant/customer dimension in v1.\\n\\nInterpretation guidelines:\\n- Positive drift_ratio means predicted > observed (we are over-attributing).\\n- Negative drift_ratio means predicted < observed (we are under-attributing).\",\n  \"implementation_plan\": \"1) Finalize SLI semantics + Finance alignment (owners: Rafael, Laura, Rishi)\\n- Confirm overhead allocation treatment in O vs P so we\\u2019re not comparing apples to oranges.\\n- Document what is excluded (CPU, storage, credits) for v1.\\n\\n2) Data sources + joins (owners: Mei, Logan, Thomas)\\n- Predicted P: use telemetry-derived request aggregates produced by cost-model drift job (not live request path).\\n- Observed O: consume daily/hourly infra cost export or GPU-seconds accounting table (whichever is already used for internal unit econ).\\n- Add freshness checks + telemetry lag metric.\\n\\n3) Job + metrics emission (owners: Rafael)\\n- Implement scheduled job (hourly) that computes drift for windows ending at T-2h.\\n- Emit Prometheus metrics:\\n  - cost_model_drift_ratio{window=\\\"1h\\\",...}\\n  - cost_model_observed_cost_usd{window,...}\\n  - cost_model_predicted_cost_usd{window,...}\\n  - cost_model_drift_gated{reason=\\\"low_volume\\\"|\\\"stale_data\\\"|\\\"ok\\\"}\\n  - cost_model_telemetry_lag_seconds\\n- Enforce series limits: topK selection, aggregate remainder into \\u201cother\\u201d.\\n\\n4) Dashboard + alerts (owners: Allison + Rafael)\\n- Add Grafana dashboard panels:\\n  - Global drift time series (1h/6h/24h)\\n  - Telemetry lag + job success\\n  - Top       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Define drift SLI and configure monitoring + alerts for Cost Model API\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4827-cost-model-drift-sli-and-alerts.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: Standard Cost Model Spec + API\nTeam: engineering\n\ndescription : we need a single, auditable drift sli definition for the standard cost model initiative, plus a monitoring pipeline that continuously compares predicted ( cost - model outputs ) vs observed ( infra spend / gpu - seconds - derived cost ) and alerts when drift exceeds thresholds. this is required before console flips cost breakdowns broadly and before finance treats standard cost outputs as a reliable unit - econ primitive. context : we already saw a drift alert fire due to telemetry lag ( see incidents thread 1769032199 ). this ticket formalizes drift semantics, adds lag - awareness + volume guardrails, and ships actionable dashboards + paging rules.",

  "description": "We need a single, auditable drift SLI definition for the Standard Cost Model initiative, plus a monitoring pipeline that continuously compares predicted (cost-model outputs) vs observed (infra spend / GPU-seconds-derived cost) and alerts when drift exceeds thresholds. This is required before Console flips cost breakdowns broadly and before Finance treats standard cost outputs as a reliable unit-econ primitive.

Context: We already saw a drift alert fire due to telemetry lag (see incidents thread 1769032199). This ticket formalizes drift semantics, adds lag-awareness + volume guardrails, and ships actionable dashboards + paging rules.

Deliverables:
- Drift SLI definition (v1) with explicit formulae, inclusion/exclusion rules, and windowing/lag policy.
- Scheduled drift monitoring job/pipeline emitting Prometheus metrics (bounded cardinality).
- Grafana dashboard + alert rules (warn/page) with runbook links and clear next steps.

Non-goals:
- Perfect cost reconciliation to invoices (billing system of record remains separate).
- Per-customer drift alerts at high cardinality (we will do top-K / aggregate-first in v1).

Primary stakeholders: Rafael Mendes (SRE), Logan Wright / Mei Lin (Telemetry), Ethan Park (API), Laura Bennett / Rishi Malhotra (FP&A).",
  "acceptance_criteria": "- Drift SLI v1 is documented and reviewed by SRE + Telemetry + Finance (written definition + examples).
- Drift pipeline runs on schedule in prod and emits:
  - drift_ratio metrics for 1h/6h/24h windows
  - telemetry_lag_seconds + data_freshness indicators
  - sample sizes (request_count / token_count / gpu_seconds) for gating
- Alerting:
  - P0 page when sustained high drift and volume gate is met
  - P1 warning when drift elevated but below page threshold
  - Separate alert for telemetry lag (to avoid false positives)
- Dashboard provides drill-down to top contributors with bounded series (top-N + “other”).
- Runbook section updated with “drift” triage steps + common causes (telemetry lag, schema mismatch, runtime metric regression, overhead allocation changes).
- Backtest on last 14 days shows alert thresholds don’t flap (documented).",
  "sli_definition_v1": "Name: cost_model.drift (v1)

Goal: quantify how far Cost Model predicted cost deviates from observed infrastructure-derived cost over a fixed reporting window, after applying the same allocation policy.

Definitions:
- Predicted cost (P): Sum of cost-model ‘request_attributable_total_usd’ over the window, computed from cost-model primitives (prefill/decode, cache, batch efficiency, quantization profile) using schema version pinned per environment.
- Observed cost (O): Infra-derived cost over the same window, mapped to the same attribution scope:
  - v1 uses GPU-seconds * effective_usd_per_gpu_second by cluster/SKU/region/deployment_mode
  - excludes non-GPU line items and one-time credits
  - includes request-attributable overhead per the agreed overhead allocation policy (see Finance thread/email; implemented as overhead_multiplier or overhead_usd bucket)

Drift ratio:
- drift_ratio = (P - O) / max(O, O_floor)
- O_floor is to avoid division noise; v1 O_floor = $50 per window (configurable).

Windowing & freshness:
- Compute over rolling windows: 1h, 6h, 24h.
- Apply a data-lag offset: exclude the most recent 2 hours from both P and O when computing drift (configurable) unless telemetry freshness guarantees improve.

Gating (to reduce noise):
- Only emit window-level drift alerts when:
  - request_count >= 10,000 OR token_count >= 50M OR observed_cost >= $200 for that window (thresholds configurable by env)

Dimensions (bounded):
- Always emit global (no dimensions) drift.
- Emit limited breakdown by:
  - deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private)
  - region
  - hardware_sku
  - model_id (top 10 by observed_cost in the window) + “other”
- No per-tenant/customer dimension in v1.

Interpretation guidelines:
- Positive drift_ratio means predicted > observed (we are over-attributing).
- Negative drift_ratio means predicted < observed (we are under-attributing).",
  "implementation_plan": "1) Finalize SLI semantics + Finance alignment (owners: Rafael, Laura, Rishi)
- Confirm overhead allocation treatment in O vs P so we’re not comparing apples to oranges.
- Document what is excluded (CPU, storage, credits) for v1.

2) Data sources + joins (owners: Mei, Logan, Thomas)
- Predicted P: use telemetry-derived request aggregates produced by cost-model drift job (not live request path).
- Observed O: consume daily/hourly infra cost export or GPU-seconds accounting table (whichever is already used for internal unit econ).
- Add freshness checks + telemetry lag metric.

3) Job + metrics emission (owners: Rafael)
- Implement scheduled job (hourly) that computes drift for windows ending at T-2h.
- Emit Prometheus metrics:
  - cost_model_drift_ratio{window="1h",...}
  - cost_model_observed_cost_usd{window,...}
  - cost_model_predicted_cost_usd{window,...}
  - cost_model_drift_gated{reason="low_volume"|"stale_data"|"ok"}
  - cost_model_telemetry_lag_seconds
- Enforce series limits: topK selection, aggregate remainder into “other”.

4) Dashboard + alerts (owners: Allison + Rafael)
- Add Grafana dashboard panels:
  - Global drift time series (1h/6h/24h)
  - Telemetry lag + job success
  - Top contributors table for model_id/hardware_sku/region
  - Correlate with cost-model API error rate + schema version distribution
- Alerting rules:
  - Page: |drift_ratio| > 0.10 for 2 consecutive 1h windows AND volume gate met AND telemetry fresh
  - Warn: |drift_ratio| > 0.05 for 3 consecutive 1h windows (same gates)
  - Telemetry lag page: telemetry_lag_seconds > 3h for 2 consecutive evaluations

5) Backtest & threshold tuning (owners: Rafael + Logan)
- Run job in shadow for ~1 week, compare alert firing to known changes (runtime deploys, schema changes).
- Tune O_floor and volume gates if needed.

6) Runbook updates + handoff (owners: Rafael)
- Update incident runbook with drift triage steps and links to dashboard.
- Confirm oncall rotation + escalation to Telemetry/Runtime/Platform depending on root cause.",
  "risks_and_mitigations": "Risk: false positives due to telemetry lag or partial backfills.
Mitigation: explicit lag offset (T-2h), freshness metric, and gating so drift alerts require fresh data.

Risk: cardinality explosion (model_id x region x sku).
Mitigation: topK + other bucketing; hard caps in job; no per-tenant dimension v1.

Risk: comparing predicted request-attributable cost to observed spend that includes unrelated overhead.
Mitigation: implement the same overhead allocation policy in both P and O (or emit both ‘request_attributable’ and ‘allocated_total’ drift; v1 is allocated_total drift).

Risk: silent drift masked by gates.
Mitigation: always emit ungated global metrics for dashboard visibility, but only page on gated conditions; add a weekly report for low-volume dims.

Risk: schema version migrations cause step changes.
Mitigation: include schema_version label in drift job output at global level; add alert suppression during planned migrations; coordinate with release train (Connor).",
  "notes_for_oncall": "When drift alert fires:
1) Check telemetry freshness + drift job success.
2) Check if a recent deploy occurred (runtime instrumentation, cost-model schema/service) and whether schema_version distribution changed.
3) Compare dimensions: is drift isolated to one hardware_sku, region, or model_id?
4) If drift aligns with a single model_id, validate runtime-exported prefill/decode split + KV cache metrics (known source of regressions).
5) If drift is broad across all dims, check infra cost export delay or allocation policy changes.
6) Use runbook section ‘Cost drift SLI’ and escalate:
- Telemetry lag / ingestion: Logan Wright / Mei Lin
- Runtime metrics regression: Sofia Ivanova / Omar El-Sayed
- Cost-model logic/schema change: Ethan Park
- Allocation policy / reporting window questions: Laura Bennett / Rishi Malhotra",

    "2026-01-20 — Rafael Mendes: Drafted initial drift formula proposal. Key open question: do we compare against GPU-seconds-derived cost or cloud billing export (billing export has 24h latency). Leaning GPU-seconds for v1 to get 1h/6h windows; Finance ok as long as the USD rate table is versioned and auditable.",
    "2026-01-23 — Laura Bennett: Confirmed Finance wants drift measured against allocated cost (includes request-attributable overhead per policy), not bare GPU cost. Also requested that we always expose both components in the dashboard to explain deltas during month-end close.",
    "2026-01-29 — Logan Wright: Telemetry lag is still ~60–120m at p95 during peak. Please bake in a fixed offset (2h) and a freshness check; otherwise we will page on ‘missing data’ again like the 1769032199 incident.",
    "2026-02-03 — Allison Grant: For alert hygiene, gate on both $ and volume; use an O_floor so we don’t page on a $5 window. Also please add a ‘job last success timestamp’ metric so oncall can quickly distinguish ‘pipeline down’ vs ‘real drift’.",
    "2026-02-11 — Ethan Park: Noted that schema migrations can shift P. Suggest adding schema_version label at least at global level, and annotate the Grafana dashboard via deploy markers during planned rollouts (Connor coordinating).",
    "2026-02-18 — Rafael Mendes: Implemented job in staging with top-10 model bucketing + other. Next: wire to prod metrics and create alert rules behind a disabled-by-default toggle until we backtest 7 days."

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/github",
    "content": "{\n  \"repo\": \"redwood\",\n  \"pr_number\": \"28462\",\n  \"title\": \"Add shared Cost Model API client library (timeouts, retries, schema negotiation)\",\n  \"author\": \"Benji Okafor\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-04\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-02-11\",\n  \"merged_at\": \"2026-02-11\",\n  \"state\": \"merged\",\n  \"base_branch\": \"main\",\n  \"head_branch\": \"feature/cost-model-client-library\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"platform\",\n    \"cost-model\",\n    \"api\",\n    \"observability\",\n    \"reliability\"\n  ],\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Ethan Park\",\n    \"Kaitlyn Nguyen\",\n    \"Chloe Martin\",\n    \"Rafael Mendes\",\n    \"Allison Grant\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_linear\": [\n    \"ENG-4830\",\n    \"ENG-4821\",\n    \"ENG-4822\"\n  ],\n  \"ci_status\": \"pass\",\n  \"files_changed_count\": \"18\",\n  \"additions\": \"742\",\n  \"deletions\": \"86\",\n  \"description\": \"Context\\nConsole and Optimize are both adopting the Cost Model API (see ENG-4821/4822). We need a single, opinionated client that standardizes:\\n- request timeouts (hot path safety for Console)\\n- retries (bounded + only when safe)\\n- schema version negotiation (so callers can be forward-compatible and we can roll schema changes safely)\\n- consistent auth/tenancy + tracing/metrics\\n\\nWhat this PR does\\n- Adds a shared client library for service-to-service calls to Cost Model API:\\n  - package: //go/platform/costmodel/client (Go)\\n  - exported type: costmodel.Client\\n  - supports endpoints: EstimateCost, GetCostBreakdown, WhatIf\\n- Timeouts\\n  - default request timeout: 250ms (overridable per-call)\\n  - default connect timeout: 50ms\\n  - caller can pass a context with deadline; client will respect the stricter of (ctx deadline, configured timeout)\\n- Retries\\n  - retries are bounded: max 2 retries, exponential backoff + full jitter\\n  - only retries on: 502/503/504, connection reset/timeouts, and explicit server retryable errors\\n  - never retries on: 4xx (except 429), schema/version errors, validation errors\\n  - idempotency: for POST requests we attach X-Redwood-Request-Id; server can safely dedupe if it chooses (client side still assumes retries may result in duplicate work)\\n  - 429 behavior: honor Retry-After (bounded by a per-call max budget)\\n- Schema version negotiation\\n  - client sends:\\n    - X-Redwood-Cost-Model-Schema-Version: <preferred_version>\\n    - X-Redwood-Cost-Model-Schema-Versions-Accepted: <csv of supported versions>\\n  - server responds with:\\n    - X-Redwood-Cost-Model-Schema-Version-Applied: <applied_version>\\n  - client surfaces applied version in response metadata and emits a metric when fallback occurs (preferred != applied)\\n  - unknown response fields are ignored by default (forward compatibility); strict mode is available for conformance tests\\n- Auth/tenancy plumbing\\n  - client requires tenant context (tenant_id) and propagates:\\n    - X-Redwood-Tenant-Id\\n    - X-Redwood-Caller-Service (for attribution)\\n  - supports standard internal service auth transport (mTLS) and attaches per-service auth token when available via ctx\\n- Observability\\n  - OpenTelemetry spans: costmodel.client.<method>\\n  - metrics:\\n    - costmodel_client_requests_total{method,status,retried}\\n    - costmodel_client_latency_ms_bucket{method}\\n    - costmodel_client_schema_applied_total{preferred,applied}\\n    - costmodel_client_retry_total{method,reason}\\n  - adds log fields (structured): request_id, tenant_id, schema_preferred, schema_applied\\n\\nWhy now\\nWe have multiple in-flight integrations (Console + Optimize) and we\\u2019ve already seen early endpoint performance discussions in eng-platform threads. Centralizing client behavior prevents each consumer from inventing its own timeouts/retry logic and makes schema rollouts measurable.\\n\\nNot in scope\\n- circuit breaking (we\\u2019ll rely on existing service mesh / caller-side fail-open behavior per integration)\\n- client-side caching (Console caching guidance will live in the integration how-to)\\n- non-Go clients (we can port the semantics to TS later; this PR establishes the canonical behavior)\\n\\nTest plan\\n- Unit tests for:\\n  - retry policy (retryable vs non-retryable statuses)\\n  - 429 Retry-After handling\\n  - schema negotiation header behavior + strict mode\\n  - context deadline behavior\\n- Integration-style tests with httptest server verifying:\\n  - headers for tenant/auth/version negotiation\\n  - metrics/spans are emitted\\n\\nRollout\\n- Library is additive.\\n- Console/Optimize adoption will be done in separate PRs behind feature flags.\\n\\nFollow-ups\\n- Add conformance tests that run against staging Cost Model API to validate negotiation behavior end-to-end (ENG-4831)\\n- Evaluate lowering default timeout for Console once we have p95 data in the new dashboards\\n\",\n  \"commits\": [\n    \"costmodel/client: initial client interface + request/response structs\",\n    \"costmodel/client: implement retry policy + backoff w/ jitter\",\n    \"costmodel/client: add schema negotiation headers + response metadata\",\n    \"obs: add OTel spans + client metrics helpers\",\n    \"tests: add httptest-based client integration tests\"\n  ],\n  \"changed_files\": [\n    \"go/platform/costmodel/client/client.go\",\n    \"go/platform/costmodel/client/options.go\",\n    \"go/platform/costmodel/client/retry.go\",\n    \"go/platform/costmodel/client/version_negotiation.go\",\n    \"go/platform/costmodel/client/errors.go\",\n    \"go/platform/costmodel/client/metrics.go\",\n    \"go/platform/costmodel/client/otel.go\",\n    \"go/platform/costmodel/client/README.md\",\n    \"go/platform/costmodel/client/client_test.go\",\n    \"go/platform/costmodel/client/retry_test.go\",\n    \"go/platform/costmodel/client/version_negotiation_test.go\",\n    \"go/platform/http/headers/headers.go\",\n    \"go/platform/observability/metrics/registry.go\",\n    \"go.mod\",\n    \"go.sum\",\n    \"tools/lint/lintconfig.yaml\",\n    \"go/platform/costmodel/client/internal/testserver/testserver.go\",\n    \"go/platform/costmodel/client/internal/testserver/testserver_test.go\"\n  ],\n  \"ci_checks\": [\n    \"build-and-unit-tests (go test ./...)\",\n    \"lint (golangci-lint)\",\n    \"api-compat (schema package compile)\",\n    \"license-scan\",\n    \"security-sast\"\n  ],\n  \"review_conversation\": [\n    \"Chloe Martin (Console): Default 250ms seems high for Console hot paths. Can we make it 150ms? We\\u2019ll have pages calling this per-route per-model and we want failures to fail fast and fall back to cached/approx numbers.\",\n    \"Benji Okafor (author): Agree on failing fast. I set 250ms to start because staging p95 for estimate endpoint isn\\u2019t stable yet. I added per-call override + documented recommended 150ms for Console in README. We can drop the default after we get a week of p95/p99 data from dashboards.\",\n    \"Rafael Mendes (SRE): Please ensure retry budget is bounded and doesn\\u2019t amplify outages. Also: avoid retrying on validation/version errors. Can you add a metric for retries + a label with retry reason?\",\n    \"Benji Okafor (author): Done. Retries capped at 2, only on 502/503/504 + transport timeouts, and 429 honoring Retry-After (bounded). Added costmodel_client_retry_total{reason} and a retried=true label on requests_total.\",\n    \"Kaitlyn Nguyen (Auth/Tenancy): Tenant propagation: can we enforce tenant_id required? Also please make sure we don\\u2019t accidentally log auth tokens.\",\n    \"Benji Okafor (author): Tenant is required in ClientOptions; constructor returns error if missing. Logging is only request_id/tenant_id/schema fields/status; no auth material. Added a unit test ensuring headers don\\u2019t get dumped in error strings.\",\n    \"Allison Grant (Observability): Span naming looks good. Please add an attribute for schema_applied and schema_preferred so we can correlate fallback rates. Also avoid high-cardinality attributes (tenant id) on spans.\",\n    \"Benji Okafor (author): Added span attrs schema.preferred/schema.applied and omitted tenant_id from span attrs. Tenant remains in structured logs (already standard in platform services).\",\n    \"Ethan Park (API lead): Version negotiation headers: can we align names with the API standards doc? Also strict mode is great\\u2014please ensure default behavior is permissive (unknown fields ignored) for forward-compat.\",\n    \"Benji Okafor (author): Renamed headers to the X-Redwood-Cost-Model-* set we agreed on in the design review. Default is permissive; strict mode only enabled in tests via option WithStrictDecoding(true).\",\n    \"Ethan Park: Approved after header rename + docs update.\",\n    \"Rafael Mendes: Approved after retry metrics landed.\"\n  ],\n  \"notable_ci_events\": [\n    \"2026-02-08: lint failed (unused error wrapper in retry.go); fixed in follow-up commit\",\n    \"2026-02-10: unit tests flaky due to time-based backoff assertion; updated test to use deterministic backoff clock\"\n  ],\n  \"merge_outcome\": \"Merged via squash into main\",\n  \"release_notes\": \"Internal: Added shared Cost Model API client library with standardized timeouts, bounded retries, schema version negotiation, and OTel/metrics instrumentation.\",\n  \"breaking_change\": \"false\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"review_conversation\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_e0d2abc35e20447881e78682340a919e\"\n}",

document.title: Add shared Cost Model API client library (timeouts, retries, schema negotiation)
document.content:
{
  "repo": "redwood",
  "pr_number": "28462",
  "title": "Add shared Cost Model API client library (timeouts, retries, schema negotiation)",
  "author": "Benji Okafor",
  "created_at": "2026-02-04",
  "updated_at": "2026-02-11",
  "merged_at": "2026-02-11",
  "state": "merged",
  "base_branch": "main",
  "head_branch": "feature/cost-model-client-library",
  "labels": [
    "platform",
    "cost-model",
    "api",
    "observability",
    "reliability"
  ],
  "reviewers": [
    "Ethan Park",
    "Kaitlyn Nguyen",
    "Chloe Martin",
    "Rafael Mendes",
    "Allison Grant"
  ],
  "linked_linear": [
    "ENG-4830",
    "ENG-4821",
    "ENG-4822"
  ],
  "ci_status": "pass",
  "files_changed_count": "18",
  "additions": "742",
  "deletions": "86",
  "description": "Context\nConsole and Optimize are both adopting the Cost Model API (see ENG-4821/4822). We need a single, opinionated client that standardizes:\n- request timeouts (hot path safety for Console)\n- retries (bounded + only when safe)\n- schema version negotiation (so callers can be forward-compatible and we can roll schema changes safely)\n- consistent auth/tenancy + tracing/metrics\n\nWhat this PR does\n- Adds a shared client library for service-to-service calls to Cost Model API:\n  - package: //go/platform/costmodel/client (Go)\n  - exported type: costmodel.Client\n  - supports endpoints: EstimateCost, GetCostBreakdown, WhatIf\n- Timeouts\n  - default request timeout: 250ms (overridable per-call)\n  - default connect timeout: 50ms\n  - caller can pass a context with deadline; client will respect the stricter of (ctx deadline, configured timeout)\n- Retries\n  - retries are bounded: max 2 retries, exponential backoff + full jitter\n  - only retries on: 502/503/504, connection reset/timeouts, and explicit server retryable errors\n  - never retries on: 4xx (except 429), schema/version errors, validation errors\n  - idempotency: for POST requests we attach X-Redwood-Request-Id; server can safely dedupe if it chooses (client side still assumes retries may result in duplicate work)\n  - 429 behavior: honor Retry-After (bounded by a per-call max budget)\n- Schema version negotiation\n  - client sends:\n    - X-Redwood-Cost-Model-Schema-Version: <preferred_version>\n    - X-Redwood-Cost-Model-Schema-Versions-Accepted: <csv of supported versions>\n  - server responds with:\n    - X-Redwood-Cost-Model-Schema-Version-Applied: <applied_version>\n  - client surfaces applied version in response metadata and emits a metric when fallback occurs (preferred != applied)\n  - unknown response fields are ignored by default (forward compatibility); strict mode is available for conformance tests\n- Auth/tenancy plumbing\n  - client requires tenant context (tenant_id) and propagates:\n    - X-Redwood-Tenant-Id\n    - X-Redwood-Caller-Service (for attribution)\n  - supports standard internal service auth transport (mTLS) and attaches per-service auth token when available via ctx\n- Observability\n  - OpenTelemetry spans: costmodel.client.<method>\n  - metrics:\n    - costmodel_client_requests_total{method,status,retried}\n    - costmodel_client_latency_ms_bucket{method}\n    - costmodel_client_schema_applied_total{preferred,applied}\n    - costmodel_client_retry_total{method,reason}\n  - adds log fields (structured): request_id, tenant_id, schema_preferred, schema_applied\n\nWhy now\nWe have multiple in-flight integrations (Console + Optimize) and we\u2019ve already seen early endpoint performance discussions in eng-platform threads. Centralizing client behavior prevents each consumer from inventing its own timeouts/retry logic and makes schema rollouts measurable.\n\nNot in scope\n- circuit breaking (we\u2019ll rely on existing service mesh / caller-side fail-open behavior per integration)\n- client-side caching (Console caching guidance will live in the integration how-to)\n- non-Go clients (we can port the semantics to TS later; this PR establishes the canonical behavior)\n\nTest plan\n- Unit tests for:\n  - retry policy (retryable vs non-retryable statuses)\n  - 429 Retry-After handling\n  - schema negotiation header behavior + strict mode\n  - context deadline behavior\n- Integration-style tests with httptest server verifying:\n  - headers for tenant/auth/version negotiation\n  - metrics/spans are emitted\n\nRollout\n- Library is additive.\n- Console/Optimize adoption will be done in separate PRs behind feature flags.\n\nFollow-ups\n- Add conformance tests that run against staging Cost Model API to validate negotiation behavior end-to-end (ENG-4831)\n- Evaluate lowering default timeout for Console once we have p95 data in the new dashboards\n",
  "commits": [
    "costmodel/client: initial client interface + request/response structs",
    "costmodel/client: implement retry policy + backoff w/ jitter",
    "costmodel/client: add schema negotiation headers + response metadata",
    "obs: add OTel spans + client metrics helpers",
    "tests: add httptest-based client integration tests"
  ],
  "changed_files": [
    "go/platform/costmodel/client/client.go",
    "go/platform/costmodel/client/options.go",
    "go/platform/costmodel/client/retry.go",
    "go/platform/costmodel/client/version_negotiation.go",
    "go/platform/costmodel/client/errors.go",
    "go/platform/costmodel/client/metrics.go",
    "go/platform/costmodel/client/otel.go",
    "go/platform/costmodel/client/README.md",
    "go/platform/costmodel/client/client_test.go",
    "go/platform/costmodel/client/retry_test.go",
    "go/platform/costmodel/client/version_negotiation_test.go",
    "go/platform/http/headers/headers.go",
    "go/platform/observability/metrics/registry.go",
    "go.mod",
    "go.sum",
    "tools/lint/lintconfig.yaml",
    "go/platform/costmodel/client/internal/testserver/testserver.go",
    "go/platform/costmodel/client/internal/testserver/testserver_test.go"
  ],
  "ci_checks": [
    "build-and-unit-tests (go test ./...)",
    "lint (golangci-lint)",
    "api-compat (schema package compile)",
    "license-scan",
    "security-sast"
  ],
  "review_conversation": [
    "Chloe Martin (Console): Default 250ms seems high for Console hot paths. Can we make it 150ms? We\u2019ll have pages calling this per-route per-model and we want failures to fail fast and fall back to cached/approx numbers.",
    "Benji Okafor (author): Agree on failing fast. I set 250ms to start because staging p95 for estimate endpoint isn\u2019t stable yet. I added per-call override + documented recommended 150ms for Console in README. We can drop the default after we get a week of p95/p99 data from dashboards.",
    "Rafael Mendes (SRE): Please ensure retry budget is bounded and doesn\u2019t amplify outages. Also: avoid retrying on validation/version errors. Can you add a metric for retries + a label with retry reason?",
    "Benji Okafor (author): Done. Retries capped at 2, only on 502/503/504 + transport timeouts, and 429 honoring Retry-After (bounded). Added costmodel_client_retry_total{reason} and a retried=true label on requests_total.",
    "Kaitlyn Nguyen (Auth/Tenancy): Tenant propagation: can we enforce tenant_id required? Also please make sure we don\u2019t accidentally log auth tokens.",
    "Benji Okafor (author): Tenant is required in ClientOptions; constructor returns error if missing. Logging is only request_id/tenant_id/schema fields/status; no auth material. Added a unit test ensuring headers don\u2019t get dumped in error strings.",
    "Allison Grant (Observability): Span naming looks good. Please add an attribute for schema_applied and schema_preferred so we can correlate fallback rates. Also avoid high-cardinality attributes (tenant id) on spans.",
    "Benji Okafor (author): Added span attrs schema.preferred/schema.applied and omitted tenant_id from span attrs. Tenant remains in structured logs (already standard in platform services).",
    "Ethan Park (API lead): Version negotiation headers: can we align names with the API standards doc? Also strict mode is great\u2014please ensure default behavior is permissive (unknown fields ignored) for forward-compat.",
    "Benji Okafor (author): Renamed headers to the X-Redwood-Cost-Model-* set we agreed on in the design review. Default is permissive; strict mode only enabled in tests via option WithStrictDecoding(true).",
    "Ethan Park: Approved after header rename + docs update.",
    "Rafael Mendes: Approved after retry metrics landed."
  ],
  "notable_ci_events": [
    "2026-02-08: lint failed (unused error wrapper in retry.go); fixed in follow-up commit",
    "2026-02-10: unit tests flaky due to time-based backoff assertion; updated test to use deterministic backoff clock"
  ],
  "merge_outcome": "Merged via squash into main",
  "release_notes": "Internal: Added shared Cost Model API client library with standardized timeouts, bounded retries, schema version negotiation, and OTel/metrics instrumentation.",
  "breaking_change": "false",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "review_conversation"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_e0d2abc35e20447881e78682340a919e"
}
