{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_51987b4d7d154048be2b0efc91a08bea",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/cost-model-performance-budget.json",
    "title": "Cost Model API v1 — Performance Budget Worksheet (latency, caching, cardinality)",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/google_drive",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Cost Model API v1 \\u2014 Performance Budget Worksheet (latency, caching, cardinality)\",\n  \"owner\": \"Thomas Baird\",\n  \"collaborators\": [\n    \"Ethan Park\",\n    \"Benji Okafor\",\n    \"Logan Wright\",\n    \"Chloe Martin\",\n    \"Rafael Mendes\"\n  ],\n  \"drive_area\": \"shared_drives\",\n  \"path\": \"shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/cost-model-performance-budget.json\",\n  \"doc_type\": \"sheet\",\n  \"team\": \"eng-platform\",\n  \"status\": \"in_review\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-22\",\n  \"last_modified\": \"2026-02-18\",\n  \"tags\": [\n    \"cost-model\",\n    \"performance\",\n    \"latency\",\n    \"cardinality\",\n    \"caching\",\n    \"slo\",\n    \"console\",\n    \"optimize\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_artifacts\": [\n    \"Linear:ENG-4821\",\n    \"Linear:ENG-4822\",\n    \"Linear:ENG-4824\",\n    \"Linear:ENG-4825\",\n    \"Linear:ENG-4826\",\n    \"Linear:ENG-4827\",\n    \"Confluence:cost-model-api-v1-design-spec\",\n    \"Confluence:cost-model-api-guidelines\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"Owner: Thomas Baird (Perf/Cardinality)\\nLast review: 2026-02-18\\nAudience: Platform (Cost Model service), Console backend, Optimize backend, Telemetry/Analytics, SRE\\n\\nPurpose\\n- Define the performance budget for Cost Model API v1 so Console (hot-path dashboards) and Optimize (what-if projections) have predictable latency and bounded responses.\\n- Translate \\u201cdon\\u2019t explode cardinality\\u201d into concrete request bounds + caching rules + query patterns.\\n- Establish default timeouts and fallback behavior expectations for callers.\\n\\nScope (v1 endpoints)\\n- /v1/cost:estimate (single request estimate; used in request traces + inline views)\\n- /v1/cost:breakdown (aggregated breakdown for a time window; used for dashboard tables)\\n- /v1/cost:what_if (scenario projection; used by Optimize)\\n\\nNon-goals\\n- This is not the billing system of record.\\n- This does not define pricing; only compute budgets and bounds.\\n\\n\\nA) Latency + availability targets (service-level)\\n\\nAssumptions\\n- Cost Model API is called by internal services (Console, Optimize). Some calls are on a user-facing path.\\n- We must tolerate telemetry lag. When inputs are missing/stale, return partial results with explicit status flags (see \\u201cDegraded modes\\u201d).\\n\\nTargets by endpoint (prod, steady state)\\n\\n| Endpoint | Typical caller | Expected QPS (steady) | p50 target | p95 target | Hard timeout (server) | Caller timeout recommendation |\\n|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\\n| estimate | Console trace drilldown, debugging tools | 150\\u2013400 | 25 ms | 80 ms | 200 ms | 250 ms |\\n| breakdown | Console dashboards | 30\\u201380 | 120 ms | 450 ms | 1200 ms | 1500 ms |\\n| what_if | Optimize | 5\\u201325 | 300 ms | 1200 ms | 2500 ms | 3000 ms |\\n\\nNotes\\n- estimate must be \\u201cfast and boring\\u201d: memory-local computation + cached model/runtime parameters; no large fan-out.\\n- breakdown is allowed to hit pre-aggregated telemetry tables (or cached aggregates), but must have bounded result cardinality.\\n- what_if is explicitly slower; it may run multiple candidate computations but must still be bounded.\\n\\nAvailability / error budget (draft)\\n- Availability: 99.9% monthly for estimate + breakdown (internal).\\n- what_if: 99.5% monthly acceptable due to non-hot-path nature.\\n\\n\\nB) Compute budget + caching strategy\\n\\nKey principle\\n- All endpoints must have a \\u201ccacheable core\\u201d keyed by stable inputs. Anything high-cardinality must be caller-provided or pre-aggregated upstream.\\n\\nCaches in play\\n1) Model Catalog + runtime metadata cache (L1 in-process)\\n- Contents: model_id -> (arch, param_count_bucket, context_len, quant_profile_id defaults, kernel_path_id mapping), hardware_sku -> $/sec, throughput baselines\\n- TTL: 15 minutes\\n- Warmup: on deploy + periodic refresh\\n- Expected hit rate: > 99% after warm\\n\\n2) Telemetry aggregate cache (L2 shared, e.g., redis/memcache) \\u2014 for breakdown\\n- Key: (org_id, project_id?, env, model_id, route_id?, region, time_bucket, schema_version, group_by_set)\\n- TTL: 2\\u20135 minutes for \\u201ctoday\\u201d buckets; 30\\u201360 minutes for historical buckets\\n- Eviction: LRU; cap by per-tenant quota (to avoid a single org dominating)\\n\\n3) What-if memoization (L1 + optional L2)\\n- Key: (org_id, base_workload_summary_hash, scenario_hash, schema_version)\\n- TTL: 10 minutes\\n- Guardrail: only memoize if the scenario passes \\u201ccheap to reuse\\u201d predicate (scenario is common and response size is small)\\n\\nCacheability rules (caller-visible)\\n- estimate responses include cache_status: HIT/MISS (internal header), and \\u201cinputs_resolved_at\\u201d timestamp.\\n- breakdown responses include \\u201ccomputed_from\\u201d: [cache, preagg_table, raw_rollup] and a \\u201ctime_range_truncated\\u201d boolean.\\n- what_if responses include \\u201cconfidence\\u201d and \\u201cassumption_profile_id\\u201d (not a cache signal, but used to interpret results).\\n\\nRecommended caller behavior\\n- Console: for dashboards, prefer breakdown requests with (a) coarse time_bucket (>= 5m) and (b) small group_by sets.\\n- Optimize: batch what_if calls by workload_summary and dedupe scenarios client-side.\\n\\n\\nC) Cardinality constraints (hard bounds)\\n\\nWhy this exists\\n- We saw early prototypes produce \\u201cgroup_by everything\\u201d breakdowns that explode in both runtime and response size (and create unbounded cache keys).\\n\\nHard request bounds (enforced server-side)\\n- Max time range per request:\\n  - breakdown: 31 days (hard), 7 days recommended for interactive\\n  - estimate: single request only (no ranges)\\n  - what_if: max 24 hours of workload summary input (summarized, not raw)\\n- Max group_by dimensions per breakdown request: 3\\n- Max distinct groups returned: 200 (top-K + \\u201cother\\u201d bucket required)\\n- Max models per request: 10\\n- Max routes per request: 50 (but only if route_id is NOT in group_by)\\n- Max regions per request: 10\\n- Max quant_profile_ids per request: 5\\n- Max response size (serialized): 512 KB (reject or truncate with explicit \\u201ctruncated\\u201d flag)\\n\\nAllowed group_by dimensions (v1)\\n- org_id (implicit; never group_by)\\n- project_id (optional; not recommended unless customer is small)\\n- env (prod/staging)\\n- model_id\\n- route_id\\n- region\\n- deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private)\\n- quant_profile_id\\n- cache_status_bucket (HIT/MISS/PARTIAL; only if derived from rollups)\\n\\nExplicitly disallowed as group_by (v1)\\n- request_id, user_id, api_key_id, prompt_hash, tool_name, function_name\\n- any free-form tag keys (e.g., \\u201cmetadata.*\\u201d)\\nReason: unbounded, high-entropy.\\n\\nTop-K semantics\\n- When group cardinality > 200:\\n  - Return top 199 by total_cost, plus one \\u201cother\\u201d bucket.\\n  - Provide dropped_group_count.\\n  - Provide ordering metric (total_cost) and stable tie-breaking (lexicographic) for determinism.\\n\\n\\nD) Budget by computation stage (internal breakdown)\\n\\nFor estimate endpoint (target p95 <= 80 ms)\\n- Request validation + auth/tenancy: 5\\u201310 ms\\n- Resolve model + hardware + pricing primitives (cached): 5\\u201315 ms\\n- Compute prefill/decode token accounting + kv cache attribution: 10\\u201325 ms\\n- Overhead allocation (simple rule): 5\\u201315 ms\\n- Serialization: 2\\u20138 ms\\n\\nFor breakdown endpoint (target p95 <= 450 ms)\\n- Auth + bounds validation: 10\\u201320 ms\\n- Aggregate fetch (pre-aggregated telemetry): 60\\u2013250 ms\\n- Post-processing (top-K, other bucket, normalization): 30\\u2013120 ms\\n- Optional joins (model metadata for display names): 5\\u201330 ms\\n\\nFor what_if endpoint (target p95 <= 1200 ms)\\n- Validate scenario + guardrails: 10\\u201340 ms\\n- Workload summary normalization: 20\\u201380 ms\\n- Scenario compute (batching/caching/quant deltas): 150\\u2013900 ms\\n- Confidence + assumption stamping: 10\\u201360 ms\\n\\n\\nE) Degraded modes + fallback behavior\\n\\nDegraded modes we expect\\n1) Telemetry lag / missing bucket\\n- behavior: return partial with status=PARTIAL_INPUTS and missing_ranges list (bounded to 20 entries)\\n- do NOT block waiting for telemetry catch-up\\n\\n2) Cache backend unhealthy\\n- estimate: continue (L1 only); never depend on L2\\n- breakdown: fall back to direct pre-agg query path; tighten bounds (max groups 100) and set status=DEGRADED_CACHE\\n- what_if: continue; skip L2 memoization; tighten scenario max_candidates\\n\\n3) Downstream model catalog slowdown\\n- behavior: use stale cache up to 60 minutes; stamp \\u201cmetadata_stale=true\\u201d\\n\\nCaller fallback expectations (important for Console)\\n- Console must have a feature-flagged fallback to existing (legacy) cost breakdown for 30 days post-launch.\\n- If Cost Model API p95 > 800 ms for breakdown over 10 min window, Console should reduce refresh frequency + use cached UI data.\\n\\n\\nF) Request shaping guidance (to prevent expensive patterns)\\n\\nConsole dashboard recommended query patterns\\n- Time bucket: 5m for last 24h; 1h for 7d; 1d for 31d\\n- group_by: model_id + route_id (avoid adding region unless the user explicitly filters)\\n- Always pass filters when available (model_id, route_id, region) rather than using group_by to discover everything.\\n\\nOptimize what_if recommended patterns\\n- Provide workload summary, not raw request samples.\\n- Cap scenario count per request to 5.\\n- Prefer one scenario per call if you need low latency; batch scenarios if you accept p95 ~1.2s.\\n\\n\\nG) Open questions / decisions needed (as of 2026-02-18)\\n1) Do we need a separate \\u201casync breakdown job\\u201d endpoint for heavy dashboard loads?\\n- Proposed: not for v1; revisit if breakdown QPS > 150 sustained.\\n\\n2) Should route_id be allowed in group_by by default?\\n- Console wants it; perf risk if customers have high route cardinality.\\n- Proposal: allow route_id group_by only when time_range <= 7d OR time_bucket >= 1h.\\n\\n3) Response truncation semantics\\n- Decision needed: reject vs truncate.\\n- Proposal: truncate with \\u201cother\\u201d bucket, plus explicit flags. Reject only if response would exceed 2 MB.\\n\\n\\nH) Action items (next 2\\u20133 weeks)\\n- [Ethan Park] Confirm endpoint timeouts + default server limits in cost-model service config. (ENG-4821)\\n- [Thomas Baird] Add request bounds + top-K enforcement to breakdown endpoint; include deterministic ordering tests. (ENG-4822)\\n- [Logan Wright] Ensure pre-aggregated telemetry tables support required group_by sets with bounded scan. (ENG-4823)\\n- [Chloe Martin] Update Console integration to use recommended time buckets + filters; avoid \\u201cgroup_by region\\u201d by default. (ENG-4825)\\n- [Rafael Mendes] Draft SLO + alert thresholds aligned with p95 targets and degraded-mode behavior. (ENG-4827)\\n\\nAppendix: Quick checklist for PR reviews\\n- Does the change add a new group_by dimension? If yes, is it bounded and documented?\\n- Does the change increase response size risk? If yes, confirm truncation behavior + tests.\\n- Does the change add new cache keys? If yes, confirm key includes schema_version and has bounded cardinality.\\n- Does the change affect p95? If yes, include benchmark results (staging load test or microbench).\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_51987b4d7d154048be2b0efc91a08bea\"\n}",

  "title": "Cost Model API v1 — Performance Budget Worksheet (latency, caching, cardinality)",
  "owner": "Thomas Baird",
  "collaborators": [

  "created_at": "2026-01-22",
  "last_modified": "2026-02-18",
  "tags": [
    "cost-model",
    "performance",
    "latency",
    "cardinality",
    "caching",
    "slo",
    "console",
    "optimize"
  ],
  "linked_artifacts": [
    "Linear:ENG-4821",

    "Confluence:cost-model-api-guidelines"
  ],
  "content": "Owner: Thomas Baird (Perf/Cardinality)
Last review: 2026-02-18
Audience: Platform (Cost Model service), Console backend, Optimize backend, Telemetry/Analytics, SRE

Purpose
- Define the performance budget for Cost Model API v1 so Console (hot-path dashboards) and Optimize (what-if projections) have predictable latency and bounded responses.
- Translate “don’t explode cardinality” into concrete request bounds + caching rules + query patterns.
- Establish default timeouts and fallback behavior expectations for callers.

Scope (v1 endpoints)
- /v1/cost:estimate (single request estimate; used in request traces + inline views)
- /v1/cost:breakdown (aggregated breakdown for a time window; used for dashboard tables)
- /v1/cost:what_if (scenario projection; used by Optimize)

Non-goals
- This is not the billing system of record.
- This does not define pricing; only compute budgets and bounds.


A) Latency + availability targets (service-level)

Assumptions
- Cost Model API is called by internal services (Console, Optimize). Some calls are on a user-facing path.
- We must tolerate telemetry lag. When inputs are missing/stale, return partial results with explicit status flags (see “Degraded modes”).

Targets by endpoint (prod, steady state)

| Endpoint | Typical caller | Expected QPS (steady) | p50 target | p95 target | Hard timeout (server) | Caller timeout recommendation |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| estimate | Console trace drilldown, debugging tools | 150–400 | 25 ms | 80 ms | 200 ms | 250 ms |
| breakdown | Console dashboards | 30–80 | 120 ms | 450 ms | 1200 ms | 1500 ms |
| what_if | Optimize | 5–25 | 300 ms | 1200 ms | 2500 ms | 3000 ms |

Notes
- estimate must be “fast and boring”: memory-local computation + cached model/runtime parameters; no large fan-out.
- breakdown is allowed to hit pre-aggregated telemetry tables (or cached aggregates), but must have bounded result cardinality.
- what_if is explicitly slower; it may run multiple candidate computations but must still be bounded.

Availability / error budget (draft)
- Availability: 99.9% monthly for estimate + breakdown (internal).
- what_if: 99.5% monthly acceptable due to non-hot-path nature.


B) Compute budget + caching strategy

Key principle
- All endpoints must have a “cacheable core” keyed by stable inputs. Anything high-cardinality must be caller-provided or pre-aggregated upstream.

Caches in play
1) Model Catalog + runtime metadata cache (L1 in-process)
- Contents: model_id -> (arch, param_count_bucket, context_len, quant_profile_id defaults, kernel_path_id mapping), hardware_sku -> $/sec, throughput baselines
- TTL: 15 minutes
- Warmup: on deploy + periodic refresh
- Expected hit rate: > 99% after warm

2) Telemetry aggregate cache (L2 shared, e.g., redis/memcache) — for breakdown
- Key: (org_id, project_id?, env, model_id, route_id?, region, time_bucket, schema_version, group_by_set)
- TTL: 2–5 minutes for “today” buckets; 30–60 minutes for historical buckets
- Eviction: LRU; cap by per-tenant quota (to avoid a single org dominating)

3) What-if memoization (L1 + optional L2)
- Key: (org_id, base_workload_summary_hash, scenario_hash, schema_version)
- TTL: 10 minutes
- Guardrail: only memoize if the scenario passes “cheap to reuse” predicate (scenario is common and response size is small)

Cacheability rules (caller-visible)
- estimate responses include cache_status: HIT/MISS (internal header), and “inputs_resolved_at” timestamp.
- breakdown responses include “computed_from”: [cache, preagg_table, raw_rollup] and a “time_range_truncated” boolean.
- what_if responses include “confidence” and “assumption_profile_id” (not a cache signal, but used to interpret results).

Recommended caller behavior
- Console: for dashboards, prefer breakdown requests with (a) coarse time_bucket (>= 5m) and (b) small group_by sets.
- Optimize: batch what_if calls by workload_summary and dedupe scenarios client-side.


C) Cardinality constraints (hard bounds)

Why this exists
- We saw early prototypes produce “group_by everything” breakdowns that explode in both runtime and response size (and create unbounded cache keys).

Hard request bounds (enforced server-side)
- Max time range per request:
  - breakdown: 31 days (hard), 7 days recommended for interactive
  - estimate: single request only (no ranges)
  - what_if: max 24 hours of workload summary input (summarized, not raw)
- Max group_by dimensions per breakdown request: 3
- Max distinct groups returned: 200 (top-K + “other” bucket required)
- Max models per request: 10
- Max routes per request: 50 (but only if route_id is NOT in group_by)
- Max regions per request: 10
- Max quant_profile_ids per request: 5
- Max response size (serialized): 512 KB (reject or truncate with explicit “truncated” flag)

Allowed group_by dimensions (v1)
- org_id (implicit; never group_by)
- project_id (optional; not recommended unless customer is small)
- env (prod/staging)
- model_id
- route_id
- region
- deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private)
- quant_profile_id
- cache_status_bucket (HIT/MISS/PARTIAL; only if derived from rollups)

Explicitly disallowed as group_by (v1)
- request_id, user_id, api_key_id, prompt_hash, tool_name, function_name
- any free-form tag keys (e.g., “metadata.*”)
Reason: unbounded, high-entropy.

Top-K semantics
- When group cardinality > 200:
  - Return top 199 by total_cost, plus one “other” bucket.
  - Provide dropped_group_count.
  - Provide ordering metric (total_cost) and stable tie-breaking (lexicographic) for determinism.


D) Budget by computation stage (internal breakdown)

For estimate endpoint (target p95 <= 80 ms)
- Request validation + auth/tenancy: 5–10 ms
- Resolve model + hardware + pricing primitives (cached): 5–15 ms
- Compute prefill/decode token accounting + kv cache attribution: 10–25 ms
- Overhead allocation (simple rule): 5–15 ms
- Serialization: 2–8 ms

For breakdown endpoint (target p95 <= 450 ms)
- Auth + bounds validation: 10–20 ms
- Aggregate fetch (pre-aggregated telemetry): 60–250 ms
- Post-processing (top-K, other bucket, normalization): 30–120 ms
- Optional joins (model metadata for display names): 5–30 ms

For what_if endpoint (target p95 <= 1200 ms)
- Validate scenario + guardrails: 10–40 ms
- Workload summary normalization: 20–80 ms
- Scenario compute (batching/caching/quant deltas): 150–900 ms
- Confidence + assumption stamping: 10–60 ms


E) Degraded modes + fallback behavior

Degraded modes we expect
1) Telemetry lag / missing bucket
- behavior: return partial with status=PARTIAL_INPUTS and missing_ranges list (bounded to 20 entries)
- do NOT block waiting for telemetry catch-up

2) Cache backend unhealthy
- estimate: continue (L1 only); never depend on L2
- breakdown: fall back to direct pre-agg query path; tighten bounds (max groups 100) and set status=DEGRADED_CACHE
- what_if: continue; skip L2 memoization; tighten scenario max_candidates

3) Downstream model catalog slowdown
- behavior: use stale cache up to 60 minutes; stamp “metadata_stale=true”

Caller fallback expectations (important for Console)
- Console must have a feature-flagged fallback to existing (legacy) cost breakdown for 30 days post-launch.
- If Cost Model API p95 > 800 ms for breakdown over 10 min window, Console should reduce refresh frequency + use cached UI data.


F) Request shaping guidance (to prevent expensive patterns)

Console dashboard recommended query patterns
- Time bucket: 5m for last 24h; 1h for 7d; 1d for 31d
- group_by: model_id + route_id (avoid adding region unless the user explicitly filters)
- Always pass filters when available (model_id, route_id, region) rather than using group_by to discover everything.

Optimize what_if recommended patterns
- Provide workload summary, not raw request samples.
- Cap scenario count per request to 5.
- Prefer one scenario per call if you need low latency; batch scenarios if you accept p95 ~1.2s.


G) Open questions / decisions needed (as of 2026-02-18)
1) Do we need a separate “async breakdown job” endpoint for heavy dashboard loads?
- Proposed: not for v1; revisit if breakdown QPS > 150 sustained.

2) Should route_id be allowed in group_by by default?
- Console wants it; perf risk if customers have high route cardinality.
- Proposal: allow route_id group_by only when time_range <= 7d OR time_bucket >= 1h.

3) Response truncation semantics
- Decision needed: reject vs truncate.
- Proposal: truncate with “other” bucket, plus explicit flags. Reject only if response would exceed 2 MB.


H) Action items (next 2–3 weeks)
- [Ethan Park] Confirm endpoint timeouts + default server limits in cost-model service config. (ENG-4821)
- [Thomas Baird] Add request bounds + top-K enforcement to breakdown endpoint; include deterministic ordering tests. (ENG-4822)
- [Logan Wright] Ensure pre-aggregated telemetry tables support required group_by sets with bounded scan. (ENG-4823)
- [Chloe Martin] Update Console integration to use recommended time buckets + filters; avoid “group_by region” by default. (ENG-4825)
- [Rafael Mendes] Draft SLO + alert thresholds aligned with p95 targets and degraded-mode behavior. (ENG-4827)

Appendix: Quick checklist for PR reviews
- Does the change add a new group_by dimension? If yes, is it bounded and documented?
- Does the change increase response size risk? If yes, confirm truncation behavior + tests.
- Does the change add new cache keys? If yes, confirm key includes schema_version and has bounded cardinality.
- Does the change affect p95? If yes, include benchmark results (staging load test or microbench).

    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"SUP-31905\",\n  \"project\": \"customer-support\",\n  \"issue_type\": \"Incident\",\n  \"summary\": \"Latency spike on internal Cost Model API endpoint causing slow Console cost breakdown loads\",\n  \"status\": \"Closed\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"severity\": \"Sev2\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-18\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-02-20\",\n  \"reporter\": \"Chloe Martin\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Rafael Mendes\",\n  \"customer_company\": \"Northbridge Security Labs\",\n  \"customer_tier\": \"enterprise\",\n  \"components\": [\n    \"console\",\n    \"telemetry\",\n    \"cost-model-service\",\n    \"api-gateway\",\n    \"observability\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"latency\",\n    \"cost-model\",\n    \"console-regression\",\n    \"needs-caching\",\n    \"feature-flag\",\n    \"prod\"\n  ],\n  \"environment\": \"prod (us-east primary; spillover eu-west)\",\n  \"affected_regions\": [\n    \"us-east\",\n    \"eu-west\"\n  ],\n  \"affected_models\": [\n    \"N/A (cost-model endpoint; model-agnostic)\"\n  ],\n  \"first_response_due_at\": \"2026-02-18\",\n  \"sla_due_at\": \"2026-02-19\",\n  \"related_incident_id\": \"INC-2026-02-18-cost-model-latency\",\n  \"linked_issues\": [\n    \"SUP-31844\",\n    \"ENG-4827\",\n    \"ENG-4830\"\n  ],\n  \"related_github_prs\": [\n    \"sources/github/redwood/pr-28457-cost-model-service-internal-endpoints.json\",\n    \"sources/github/redwood/pr-28462-add-cost-model-client-library.json\",\n    \"sources/github/observability-pack/pr-391-add-cost-model-api-dashboards.json\"\n  ],\n  \"related_confluence_pages\": [\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/cost-model-api-incident-runbook.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/cost-model-api-observability.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/cost-model-api-slo.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/cost-model-api-guidelines.json\"\n  ],\n  \"description\": \"Issue summary:\\n- Customer reports Console cost breakdown pages intermittently taking 20\\u201360s to load or timing out.\\n- Root symptom appears to be elevated p95 latency on internal Cost Model API (estimate/breakdown endpoints), which Console backend calls on-demand.\\n\\nCustomer impact:\\n- Northbridge Security Labs (enterprise) cannot reliably load Console cost breakdown for the last 24h; internal finance review blocked.\\n- Console UI shows partial data or \\\"Something went wrong\\\" after ~30s.\\n\\nScope / suspected:\\n- Internal Cost Model API p95 latency spike and occasional 504s between Console backend and cost-model-service.\\n- Possible regression due to higher request volume and cache-miss heavy query patterns (high-cardinality breakdown dimensions).\\n\\nNotes:\\n- This is not a customer calling the Cost Model API directly; it is Console calling internal endpoints on the hot path.\\n- Console is behind a feature flag for cost-model-backed breakdown; fallback is legacy aggregation if enabled.\\n\\nRequested outcome:\\n- Immediate mitigation to restore Console responsiveness.\\n- Follow-up work: add server-side caching/memoization and enforce tighter request bounding for Console hot paths.\",\n  \"steps_to_reproduce\": \"1) In prod Console, navigate to Usage \\u2192 Cost breakdown.\\n2) Select: Time range = Last 24 hours; Group by = model + route + region (or other multi-dimension view).\\n3) Observe: UI spinner persists >20s; often times out.\\n\\nInternal reproduction:\\n- Hit Console backend endpoint that requests cost-model breakdown for the same range; observe cost-model-service p95 > 8s and occasional gateway timeouts.\",\n  \"expected_result\": \"Console cost breakdown loads in <5s for Last 24 hours views; Cost Model API p95 within SLO.\",\n  \"actual_result\": \"Cost Model API p95 spikes to 8\\u201315s (with tail up to ~30s) leading to Console timeouts/partial results; sporadic 504s.\",\n  \"investigation_notes\": \"Timeline (UTC):\\n- 2026-02-18 16:40: Support intake from CSM: Northbridge reports Console cost pages timing out.\\n- 2026-02-18 17:05: Console team confirms elevated latency calling cost-model-service; opens SUP-31905.\\n- 2026-02-18 17:20: SRE reviews Grafana dashboard (cost-model API). p95 latency jump coincides with increased request volume after enabling breakdown feature flag for additional orgs.\\n- 2026-02-18 17:40: Noted many requests with high-cardinality breakdown configs (multiple group_by dimensions) and large time windows returning large intermediate aggregates.\\n- 2026-02-18 18:05: Checked telemetry/analytics dependency health: ingestion lag within normal bounds; not the primary driver.\\n- 2026-02-18 18:15: Cost-model-service CPU saturation observed; GC pressure increased; request concurrency spikes.\\n- 2026-02-18 18:30: Identified Console backend retry behavior amplifying load during slow responses.\\n\\nHypotheses evaluated:\\n- Telemetry lag / backfill causing slow queries: ruled out (lag normal; queries still slow with fresh data).\\n- Schema negotiation issues causing retries: not primary (version distribution stable; errors not concentrated).\\n- Cardinality explosion from unbounded breakdown dimensions: likely contributor.\\n- Missing caching layer for identical repeated queries (Console refresh/polling): confirmed (cache hit rate near zero).\\n\\nSlack coordination:\\n- Referenced #incidents thread about cost drift alert/telemetry lag earlier in the week; not directly related but informed mitigation approach.\\n\\nCustomer comms:\\n- Acknowledged incident, shared mitigation plan: temporarily reduce breakdown complexity and/or fall back to legacy aggregation while performance improvements roll out.\",\n  \"resolution\": \"Mitigation applied (2026-02-18 19:05 UTC):\\n- Console: temporarily reduced feature-flag exposure for cost-model-backed breakdown for affected org(s) and enabled legacy fallback for high-latency scenarios.\\n- Cost-model-service: applied a temporary config to enforce stricter request bounds for breakdown requests coming from Console (max group_by dimensions and max time buckets) per API guidelines.\\n- Infra: increased service replicas and tightened timeouts to reduce queued tail latency; added circuit-breaker behavior in Console backend to avoid retry amplification.\\n\\nResult:\\n- Cost-model-service p95 returned to ~2.1s; 504s stopped.\\n- Console load times improved to <6s for Northbridge on standard views; advanced high-cardinality view now shows a \\\"refine filters\\\" message rather than timing out.\\n\\nCustomer confirmation:\\n- 2026-02-19: Northbridge confirmed Console is usable again for finance review; requested ETA for permanent fix/caching improvements.\",\n  \"next_steps\": \"1) Implement server-side caching/memoization for common Console queries (time-window + org + breakdown config) with bounded TTL and cache-size guards.\\n2) Add explicit Console guidance and guardrails: default group_by set, maximum dimensions, and proactive UI validation.\\n3) Update Console backend client usage: backoff + jitter; reduce automatic retries on timeouts; introduce request coalescing.\\n4) Add alert for cache hit rate and high-cardinality request share; ensure dashboards include request-shape distribution.\\n5) Post-incident follow-up: document the temporary bounds change and ensure it is captured in cost-model API guidelines as a Console-specific profile.\\n\\nOwners:\\n- SRE: Rafael Mendes (monitoring + rollout safety)\\n- Cost Model API: Ethan Park (caching + bounds)\\n- Console: Jada Williams / Felix Schneider (client behavior + UI guardrails)\",\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2026-02-18 16:47 (Chloe Martin): Getting reports from Northbridge that cost breakdown pages are timing out. We see a spike in calls to cost-model-service when loading Usage/Cost pages. Can SRE help triage p95? Customer impact: finance review today.\",\n    \"2026-02-18 17:12 (Rafael Mendes): On it. Looking at cost-model API dashboard now. p95 is ~12s over last hour; error rate low but timeouts at gateway are rising. Will dig into request patterns and saturation.\",\n    \"2026-02-18 17:33 (Felix Schneider): Console backend logs show long tail from /internal/cost-model/v1/breakdown. We also retry on timeout (2x). Might be amplifying traffic. We can hotfix to reduce retries if needed.\",\n    \"2026-02-18 18:02 (Ethan Park): Seeing many breakdown requests with 3\\u20134 group_by dimensions + fine-grained buckets. This is worst-case for aggregation. We don\\u2019t have caching yet; identical queries repeat on refresh and navigation.\",\n    \"2026-02-18 18:41 (Rafael Mendes): Proposed mitigation: (1) shrink feature-flag exposure for cost-model breakdown; (2) enforce stricter bounds for Console caller; (3) scale replicas. Chloe/Felix please confirm legacy fallback still acceptable for customer until caching ships.\",\n    \"2026-02-18 18:55 (Chloe Martin): Confirmed. We can route Northbridge to legacy breakdown (with a banner) as an interim. Proceed with bounds + scaling now.\",\n    \"2026-02-18 19:18 (Rafael Mendes): Mitigation deployed. p95 trending down to ~2\\u20133s; no new 504s observed. Monitoring for 30 minutes before declaring stable.\",\n    \"2026-02-19 09:10 (Chloe Martin): Northbridge confirmed pages load again. They asked if we can avoid removing advanced group_by options long-term; told them we\\u2019re adding caching + performance work.\",\n    \"2026-02-20 14:05 (Rafael Mendes): Closing as mitigated and stable. Follow-ups tracked with platform team; recommend adding cache hit-rate panel and request-shape guardrail metrics to dashboards.\"\n  ],\n  \"attachments\": [\n    \"Grafana: cost-model API latency panel screenshot (internal link)\",\n    \"Console backend log excerpt showing timeout + retry amplification (internal link)\"\n  ],\n  \"original_location\": \"jira/customer-support/SUP-31905-latency-spike-on-cost-model-endpoint.json\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"summary\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"steps_to_reproduce\",\n    \"expected_result\",\n    \"actual_result\",\n    \"investigation_notes\",\n    \"resolution\",\n    \"next_steps\",\n    \"comments\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_5ffe28c9feb14e5c9c6bf4534a9ed862\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Latency spike on internal Cost Model API endpoint causing slow Console cost breakdown loads\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/jira\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/jira/internal-support/SUP-31905-latency-spike-on-cost-model-endpoint.json\nConnector: jira\nWorkspace: internal-support\nProject: customer-support\n\nshared mitigation plan : temporarily reduce breakdown complexity and / or fall back to legacy aggregation while performance improvements roll out. resolution : mitigation applied ( 2026 - 02 - 18 19 : 05 utc ) : - console : temporarily reduced feature - flag exposure for cost - model - backed breakdown for affected org ( s ) and enabled legacy fallback for high - latency scenarios. - cost - model - service : applied a temporary config to enforce stricter request bounds for breakdown requests coming from console ( max group _ by dimensions and max time buckets ) per api guidelines. - infra : increased service replicas and tightened timeouts to reduce queued tail latency ; added circuit - breaker behavior in console backend to avoid retry amplification.",

{
  "key": "SUP-31905",
  "project": "customer-support",
  "issue_type": "Incident",
  "summary": "Latency spike on internal Cost Model API endpoint causing slow Console cost breakdown loads",
  "status": "Closed",
  "priority": "P1",
  "severity": "Sev2",
  "created_at": "2026-02-18",
  "updated_at": "2026-02-20",
  "reporter": "Chloe Martin",
  "assignee": "Rafael Mendes",
  "customer_company": "Northbridge Security Labs",
  "customer_tier": "enterprise",
  "components": [
    "console",
    "telemetry",
    "cost-model-service",
    "api-gateway",
    "observability"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "latency",
    "cost-model",
    "console-regression",
    "needs-caching",
    "feature-flag",
    "prod"
  ],
  "environment": "prod (us-east primary; spillover eu-west)",
  "affected_regions": [
    "us-east",
    "eu-west"
  ],
  "affected_models": [
    "N/A (cost-model endpoint; model-agnostic)"
  ],
  "first_response_due_at": "2026-02-18",
  "sla_due_at": "2026-02-19",
  "related_incident_id": "INC-2026-02-18-cost-model-latency",
  "linked_issues": [
    "SUP-31844",
    "ENG-4827",
    "ENG-4830"
  ],
  "related_github_prs": [
    "sources/github/redwood/pr-28457-cost-model-service-internal-endpoints.json",
    "sources/github/redwood/pr-28462-add-cost-model-client-library.json",
    "sources/github/observability-pack/pr-391-add-cost-model-api-dashboards.json"
  ],
  "related_confluence_pages": [
    "sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/cost-model-api-incident-runbook.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/cost-model-api-observability.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/cost-model-api-slo.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/cost-model-api-guidelines.json"
  ],
  "description": "Issue summary:\n- Customer reports Console cost breakdown pages intermittently taking 20\u201360s to load or timing out.\n- Root symptom appears to be elevated p95 latency on internal Cost Model API (estimate/breakdown endpoints), which Console backend calls on-demand.\n\nCustomer impact:\n- Northbridge Security Labs (enterprise) cannot reliably load Console cost breakdown for the last 24h; internal finance review blocked.\n- Console UI shows partial data or \"Something went wrong\" after ~30s.\n\nScope / suspected:\n- Internal Cost Model API p95 latency spike and occasional 504s between Console backend and cost-model-service.\n- Possible regression due to higher request volume and cache-miss heavy query patterns (high-cardinality breakdown dimensions).\n\nNotes:\n- This is not a customer calling the Cost Model API directly; it is Console calling internal endpoints on the hot path.\n- Console is behind a feature flag for cost-model-backed breakdown; fallback is legacy aggregation if enabled.\n\nRequested outcome:\n- Immediate mitigation to restore Console responsiveness.\n- Follow-up work: add server-side caching/memoization and enforce tighter request bounding for Console hot paths.",
  "steps_to_reproduce": "1) In prod Console, navigate to Usage \u2192 Cost breakdown.\n2) Select: Time range = Last 24 hours; Group by = model + route + region (or other multi-dimension view).\n3) Observe: UI spinner persists >20s; often times out.\n\nInternal reproduction:\n- Hit Console backend endpoint that requests cost-model breakdown for the same range; observe cost-model-service p95 > 8s and occasional gateway timeouts.",
  "expected_result": "Console cost breakdown loads in <5s for Last 24 hours views; Cost Model API p95 within SLO.",
  "actual_result": "Cost Model API p95 spikes to 8\u201315s (with tail up to ~30s) leading to Console timeouts/partial results; sporadic 504s.",
  "investigation_notes": "Timeline (UTC):\n- 2026-02-18 16:40: Support intake from CSM: Northbridge reports Console cost pages timing out.\n- 2026-02-18 17:05: Console team confirms elevated latency calling cost-model-service; opens SUP-31905.\n- 2026-02-18 17:20: SRE reviews Grafana dashboard (cost-model API). p95 latency jump coincides with increased request volume after enabling breakdown feature flag for additional orgs.\n- 2026-02-18 17:40: Noted many requests with high-cardinality breakdown configs (multiple group_by dimensions) and large time windows returning large intermediate aggregates.\n- 2026-02-18 18:05: Checked telemetry/analytics dependency health: ingestion lag within normal bounds; not the primary driver.\n- 2026-02-18 18:15: Cost-model-service CPU saturation observed; GC pressure increased; request concurrency spikes.\n- 2026-02-18 18:30: Identified Console backend retry behavior amplifying load during slow responses.\n\nHypotheses evaluated:\n- Telemetry lag / backfill causing slow queries: ruled out (lag normal; queries still slow with fresh data).\n- Schema negotiation issues causing retries: not primary (version distribution stable; errors not concentrated).\n- Cardinality explosion from unbounded breakdown dimensions: likely contributor.\n- Missing caching layer for identical repeated queries (Console refresh/polling): confirmed (cache hit rate near zero).\n\nSlack coordination:\n- Referenced #incidents thread about cost drift alert/telemetry lag earlier in the week; not directly related but informed mitigation approach.\n\nCustomer comms:\n- Acknowledged incident, shared mitigation plan: temporarily reduce breakdown complexity and/or fall back to legacy aggregation while performance improvements roll out.",
  "resolution": "Mitigation applied (2026-02-18 19:05 UTC):\n- Console: temporarily reduced feature-flag exposure for cost-model-backed breakdown for affected org(s) and enabled legacy fallback for high-latency scenarios.\n- Cost-model-service: applied a temporary config to enforce stricter request bounds for breakdown requests coming from Console (max group_by dimensions and max time buckets) per API guidelines.\n- Infra: increased service replicas and tightened timeouts to reduce queued tail latency; added circuit-breaker behavior in Console backend to avoid retry amplification.\n\nResult:\n- Cost-model-service p95 returned to ~2.1s; 504s stopped.\n- Console load times improved to <6s for Northbridge on standard views; advanced high-cardinality view now shows a \"refine filters\" message rather than timing out.\n\nCustomer confirmation:\n- 2026-02-19: Northbridge confirmed Console is usable again for finance review; requested ETA for permanent fix/caching improvements.",
  "next_steps": "1) Implement server-side caching/memoization for common Console queries (time-window + org + breakdown config) with bounded TTL and cache-size guards.\n2) Add explicit Console guidance and guardrails: default group_by set, maximum dimensions, and proactive UI validation.\n3) Update Console backend client usage: backoff + jitter; reduce automatic retries on timeouts; introduce request coalescing.\n4) Add alert for cache hit rate and high-cardinality request share; ensure dashboards include request-shape distribution.\n5) Post-incident follow-up: document the temporary bounds change and ensure it is captured in cost-model API guidelines as a Console-specific profile.\n\nOwners:\n- SRE: Rafael Mendes (monitoring + rollout safety)\n- Cost Model API: Ethan Park (caching + bounds)\n- Console: Jada Williams / Felix Schneider (client behavior + UI guardrails)",
  "comments": [
    "2026-02-18 16:47 (Chloe Martin): Getting reports from Northbridge that cost breakdown pages are timing out. We see a spike in calls to cost-model-service when loading Usage/Cost pages. Can SRE help triage p95? Customer impact: finance review today.",
    "2026-02-18 17:12 (Rafael Mendes): On it. Looking at cost-model API dashboard now. p95 is ~12s over last hour; error rate low but timeouts at gateway are rising. Will dig into request patterns and saturation.",
    "2026-02-18 17:33 (Felix Schneider): Console backend logs show long tail from /internal/cost-model/v1/breakdown. We also retry on timeout (2x). Might be amplifying traffic. We can hotfix to reduce retries if needed.",
    "2026-02-18 18:02 (Ethan Park): Seeing many breakdown requests with 3\u20134 group_by dimensions + fine-grained buckets. This is worst-case for aggregation. We don\u2019t have caching yet; identical queries repeat on refresh and navigation.",
    "2026-02-18 18:41 (Rafael Mendes): Proposed mitigation: (1) shrink feature-flag exposure for cost-model breakdown; (2) enforce stricter bounds for Console caller; (3) scale replicas. Chloe/Felix please confirm legacy fallback still acceptable for customer until caching ships.",
    "2026-02-18 18:55 (Chloe Martin): Confirmed. We can route Northbridge to legacy breakdown (with a banner) as an interim. Proceed with bounds + scaling now.",
    "2026-02-18 19:18 (Rafael Mendes): Mitigation deployed. p95 trending down to ~2\u20133s; no new 504s observed. Monitoring for 30 minutes before declaring stable.",
    "2026-02-19 09:10 (Chloe Martin): Northbridge confirmed pages load again. They asked if we can avoid removing advanced group_by options long-term; told them we\u2019re adding caching + performance work.",
    "2026-02-20 14:05 (Rafael Mendes): Closing as mitigated and stable. Follow-ups tracked with platform team; recommend adding cache hit-rate panel and request-shape guardrail metrics to dashboards."
  ],

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{
  "title": "PRD: Standard Cost Model Spec + Internal Cost Model API (v1)",
  "space": "product-docs",
  "author": "Marissa Cole",
  "owner_team": "product",
  "status": "in_review",
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "created_at": "2026-01-10",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-18",
  "reviewers": [
    "Priya Natarajan",
    "Ethan Park",
    "Logan Wright",
    "Chloe Martin",
    "Aditya Rao",
    "Laura Bennett",
    "Rafael Mendes"

  "related_pages": [

    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-022-cost-breakdown-taxonomy.json",
    "sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/cost-model-api-v1-design-spec.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/cost-model-api-guidelines.json"
  ],
  "body": "h1. Summary\n\nRedwood Inference currently computes and displays \u201ccost\u201d in multiple places (Console dashboards, billing hooks, Optimize prototypes, finance reporting). Each path uses slightly different definitions and inputs (prefill vs decode accounting, KV cache attribution, batching efficiency, quantization effects, overhead allocation, and handling of telemetry lag). This results in mismatched dashboards vs invoices, inconsistent ROI estimates, and friction during enterprise/security/finance reviews.\n\nThis PRD defines a single, versioned Standard Cost Model Spec and an internal Cost Model API (service + shared client library) that produces canonical cost primitives used by:\n- Redwood Console: consistent, explorable cost breakdown views\n- Redwood Optimize: defensible \u201cwhat-if\u201d projections for batching/caching/quantization recommendations\n- Finance/FP&A: stable unit-economics reporting primitives and auditability\n- Platform/Billing: aligned request attribution inputs and shared taxonomy\n\nh1. Problem statement\n\nh2. User pain\n\n1) Console cost breakdown inconsistencies\n- Engineers and customer admins see a cost breakdown in Console that may not match invoice totals.\n- During incidents or telemetry gaps, Console can show partial or misleading cost attribution.\n\n2) Optimize ROI trust gap\n- Optimize \u201cwhat-if\u201d savings can be too optimistic if assumptions (e.g., cache warm-rate) aren\u2019t explicit or bounded.\n- Recommendations are hard to explain to customers because they lack a canonical breakdown taxonomy and confidence/assumptions.\n\n3) Internal misalignment and slow iteration\n- Telemetry, billing, and product teams do not share a single \u201csource of truth\u201d for cost definitions.\n- Each team re-implements cost logic, making changes risky and increasing regressions.\n\nh2. Business impact\n- Reduced customer trust in cost transparency and \u201csavings\u201d claims.\n- Increased support burden (cost mismatch tickets) and slower sales cycles for Dedicated/Private.\n- Harder to manage unit economics and to reason about cost drivers across hardware SKUs and model versions.\n\nh1. Goals and non-goals\n\nh2. Goals (v1)\n\n- Standardize cost representation and semantics across Console, Optimize, billing hooks, and finance reporting.\n- Publish a versioned Standard Cost Model Spec (schemas + definitions) that is backwards compatible.\n- Provide an internal Cost Model API that returns:\n  - Per-request cost estimates (request-attributable)\n  - Cost breakdown taxonomy (prefill/decode, cache hits/misses, batching efficiency, overhead allocation)\n  - Aggregated breakdowns with bounded response sizes\n  - \u201cWhat-if\u201d projections for batching/caching/quantization changes with guardrails and confidence fields\n- Align telemetry and billing inputs to produce consistent primitives.\n- Establish governance: ownership, review process, compatibility guarantees, and deprecation policy.\n\nh2. Non-goals (v1)\n\n- Replace billing/RevRec systems. The cost model provides standardized primitives but does not become the billing system of record.\n- Provide a customer-facing pricing calculator or pricing policy engine.\n- Perfect \u201ctrue cost\u201d in all cases; v1 prioritizes consistency, explainability, and bounded error with monitoring.\n\nh1. Primary users and personas\n\n- Console users (Engineering managers, platform engineers, FinOps-like roles at customers): need reliable, drill-down cost breakdowns to understand drivers and anomalies.\n- Optimize users (ML engineers, platform teams): need credible \u201cwhat-if\u201d ROI numbers with explicit assumptions and confidence.\n- Internal stakeholders:\n  - Telemetry & Analytics (Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman): need clear contracts and data quality rules.\n  - Platform Control Plane (Ethan Park, Benji Okafor, Kaitlyn Nguyen): need stable APIs, tenancy/auth, rate limits.\n  - Finance/FP&A (Laura Bennett, Rishi Malhotra): need stable categories and overhead allocation rules for reporting windows.\n\nh1. Key use-cases\n\nh2. Console use-cases (must support v1)\n\n1) Request breakdown view\n- Show request-attributable cost for a single request (or small set) with a clear split of:\n  - Prefill tokens vs decode tokens\n  - Cache hit vs miss attribution (where applicable)\n  - Queue/scheduler overhead classification (as overhead vs request-attributable per policy)\n\n2) Time-series breakdown for a route/model\n- Show cost per 1K tokens and absolute cost over time.\n- Drill down by model, model version, deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), region, and quantization profile.\n- Bounded cardinality: must support top-K breakdowns and \u201cother\u201d.\n\n3) Consistency with invoices (explainable deltas)\n- Console must not diverge due to definitional drift.\n- If invoice differs due to billing policy (rounding, minimums, credits), Console must be able to explain \u201ccost primitives\u201d vs \u201cbilling totals\u201d.\n\nh2. Optimize use-cases (must support v1)\n\n1) ROI estimates for recommendations\n- Given a workload summary (token distribution, cache behavior summary, current batching/quant profile), return projected cost delta for:\n  - Increased batch size / improved batching efficiency\n  - Increased cache hit rate (within guardrails)\n  - Switching quantization profile (supported profiles)\n\n2) Explainability and safety\n- Optimize must surface: assumptions, constraints, and confidence indicators (e.g., bounded interval or qualitative confidence).\n- Guardrails: reject/clip unrealistic what-if parameters (e.g., cache hit rate > 95% without evidence).\n\nh2. Finance/FP&A use-cases (must support v1)\n\n- Map cost breakdown taxonomy to unit economics reporting.\n- Provide stable categories over reporting windows, with versioned specs and deprecation policies.\n\nh1. Scope and product requirements\n\nh2. In scope (v1)\n\n1) Standard Cost Model Spec (schema + semantics)\n- A versioned schema package that defines:\n  - Inputs (what the cost model requires)\n  - Outputs (what the cost model guarantees)\n  - Breakdown taxonomy and definitions\n  - Determinism requirements and rounding rules\n\n2) Cost Model API (internal)\n- Service endpoints used by Console and Optimize.\n- Shared client library with timeouts, retries, and schema version negotiation.\n\n3) Telemetry input contracts + validation\n- Token metering and attribution fields required by spec.\n- Required runtime-exported metrics (KV cache stats, prefill/decode split, batch efficiency measures).\n- Data quality checks and drift monitoring.\n\n4) Governance\n- Documented ownership, review process, and a migration/deprecation policy.\n\nh2. Out of scope (v1)\n\n- Customer-facing public API for cost model results.\n- Pricing policy changes.\n- Full historical backfills beyond what is needed for validation and confidence-building.\n\nh1. Functional requirements\n\nh2. Canonical taxonomy (required)\n\nThe cost model must expose a stable breakdown taxonomy aligned to ADR-022. v1 requires these top-level categories:\n- compute.prefill\n- compute.decode\n- memory.kv_cache (if modeled as separate line item; otherwise attribute via compute and expose cache metrics)\n- overhead.request_attributable (e.g., per-request control-plane overhead if policy includes it)\n- overhead.shared_allocated (allocated overhead per policy; must include policy_id/version)\n\nEach category must have clear semantics:\n- Prefill: prompt processing tokens (including system/user/tool messages) counted as prefill tokens.\n- Decode: generated tokens counted as decode tokens.\n- Cache: if prefix/KV cache prevents prefill compute, the model must attribute savings explicitly and expose cache hit-rate.\n- Batching: model must account for batch efficiency, exposing the effective batch factor used.\n- Quantization: model must expose quantization profile identifiers and any modeled delta assumptions.\n\nh2. Required outputs (v1)\n\nPer request:\n- total_cost_usd (request-attributable + allocated overhead per selected policy)\n- cost_breakdown (by taxonomy keys; bounded number of keys)\n- token_counts (prefill_tokens, decode_tokens)\n- cache_metrics_summary (cache_hit_rate or hit/miss counts, with clear definition)\n- batch_metrics_summary (effective_batch_size or batch_efficiency)\n- model_identity (model_id, model_version, quant_profile_id)\n- deployment_context (hosted/dedicated/private, region, hardware_sku)\n- spec_version + policy_version\n\nAggregations:\n- ability to request time-bucketed aggregates with filters and top-K dimensions.\n- response bounding rules (top-K + other, max dimensions, max buckets).\n\nWhat-if:\n- projected_total_cost_usd\n- projected_cost_breakdown\n- delta_usd and delta_percent vs baseline\n- assumptions (human-readable strings)\n- guardrails_applied (human-readable strings)\n- confidence indicator (qualitative or interval; exact representation is defined in the design spec)\n\nh2. Required inputs (v1)\n\nMinimum telemetry and catalog inputs required:\n- Token accounting: prefill_tokens, decode_tokens, total_tokens (with precise definitions)\n- Cache: prefix/KV cache hits/misses (or hit rate) with consistent units\n- Scheduler/batching: batch size distribution summary or effective batch factor\n- Runtime path identifiers: quantization execution path/profile\n- Deployment context: environment, region, hardware SKU, capacity mode\n- Cost rates: GPU $/hr (or internal normalized rate) and overhead allocation policy inputs\n\nh1. Non-functional requirements\n\nh2. Performance and bounds\n- P95 latency targets (internal):\n  - Single-request estimate: p95 <= 50ms in-region\n  - Aggregation query (bounded): p95 <= 250ms for typical Console dashboard queries\n- Hard bounds:\n  - Max time range per query (e.g., 7 days for high-cardinality breakdown endpoints; longer ranges require pre-aggregation)\n  - Max buckets (e.g., 2,000)\n  - Max dimension values returned per request (top-K + other)\n\nh2. Correctness and determinism\n- Same inputs + same spec version + same policy version must produce identical outputs.\n- Document rounding and precision (e.g., USD precision to 1e-6, display rounding handled by callers).\n- Drift SLI: track predicted vs observed spend within agreed tolerances and with lag awareness.\n\nh2. Reliability\n- API must degrade safely:\n  - If cost-model API is degraded, Console should fall back to existing computation for a limited window (behind feature flag).\n  - Optimize must fail closed (no recommendation) if confidence is too low or request is outside guardrails.\n\nh2. Security and tenancy\n- Enforce tenant isolation (org_id/project_id).\n- Auth: service-to-service auth with scoped permissions.\n- Audit logs for access to finance-adjacent aggregations.\n\nh1. Success metrics\n\nh2. Adoption metrics\n- >= 90% of Console cost breakdown traffic uses Cost Model API within 4 weeks of GA (excluding explicitly exempt routes).\n- >= 80% of Optimize recommendation ROI computations use Cost Model API within 4 weeks of GA.\n\nh2. Quality metrics\n- Cost mismatch support tickets (Console vs invoice) reduced by 50% within 8 weeks (measured via Support/Jira tags).\n- Drift SLI:\n  - Median monthly drift (modeled cost vs observed spend) within +/- 5% for Hosted and Dedicated (after lag correction)\n  - Alerts on sustained drift > 10% over 24 hours (with telemetry lag gating)\n\nh2. Performance metrics\n- Meet p95 latency targets for top Console queries.\n- Error budget compliance per SLO doc.\n\nh2. Trust/Explainability metrics\n- Optimize ROI \u201ctoo optimistic\u201d escalations reduced by 30% within 8 weeks.\n- At least one customer-facing narrative (via CS) validated: ability to explain cost drivers using standard taxonomy.\n\nh1. UX / Product requirements (Console + Optimize)\n\nh2. Console requirements\n- Console must display:\n  - Spec version and policy version (at least in \u201cdetails\u201d view)\n  - A consistent breakdown table that matches taxonomy keys\n  - A note when results are estimated vs observed, and when telemetry lag applies\n\nh2. Optimize requirements\n- Optimize must display:\n  - Baseline cost assumptions and inputs\n  - What-if parameters and any guardrails applied\n  - Confidence indicator and rationale\n\nh1. Dependencies\n\n- Runtime metrics exports (KV cache stats, prefill/decode token split, batching metrics) owned by Runtime Scheduling/Kernels (Sofia Ivanova, Omar El-Sayed, Grace Kim).\n- Telemetry normalization and contracts owned by Telemetry & Analytics (Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman).\n- Model catalog must expose stable quant_profile_id and metadata.\n- Finance approval of overhead allocation policy and reporting windows.\n- SRE SLOs, dashboards, and incident runbooks.\n\nh1. Risks and mitigations\n\n1) Cardinality explosion in aggregation endpoints\n- Risk: high-cardinality dimensions (route, customer, model version, region) create slow/expensive queries.\n- Mitigation: strict request bounds, top-K + other, pre-aggregation for common dashboards, caching.\n\n2) Telemetry lag and missing fields\n- Risk: drift alerts or incorrect dashboard values due to delayed ingestion or schema mismatch.\n- Mitigation: lag-aware correctness SLI, explicit \u201cdata freshness\u201d fields, fallback paths, conformance tests.\n\n3) Mismatch between \u201ccost primitives\u201d and \u201cinvoice totals\u201d\n- Risk: customers expect exact match; billing includes credits, rounding, minimums.\n- Mitigation: document difference; add \u201cbilling_adjustments\u201d as a separate concept (not rolled into primitives) and ensure Console messaging is clear.\n\n4) Overfitting what-if projections\n- Risk: Optimize projects savings that cannot be realized operationally.\n- Mitigation: guardrails; require evidence-based constraints; confidence gating; track realized vs projected where possible.\n\nh1. Phased rollout plan (Q1 2026 target)\n\nh2. Phase 0: Discovery (Weeks 1\u20132)\nOwner: Talia Benson (program), Marissa Cole (product)\n- Inventory existing cost definitions (Console, billing, Optimize prototypes)\n- Confirm must-have v1 fields and taxonomy\n- Produce v1 spec outline + open questions list\n\nh2. Phase 1: Spec + ADRs (Weeks 3\u20135)\nOwner: Ethan Park (API), Logan Wright (telemetry)\n- Publish Standard Cost Model Spec v1 (schema + semantics)\n- Approve ADR-021/022 alignment\n- Define compatibility rules and deprecation policy\n\nh2. Phase 2: Implementation (Weeks 6\u20139)\nOwner: Ethan Park, Benji Okafor, Kaitlyn Nguyen\n- Implement internal Cost Model API v1 endpoints\n- Add shared client library with version negotiation\n- Add conformance tests and golden fixtures\n\nh2. Phase 3: Integration + Validation (Weeks 10\u201312)\nOwners: Chloe Martin (Console), Aditya Rao (Optimize)\n- Console integration behind feature flag (route-by-route enablement)\n- Optimize integration for top recommendation types\n- Backtesting vs observed spend and validation dashboards\n\nh2. Phase 4: GA + Governance (Week 13+)\nOwners: Marissa Cole (product), Rafael Mendes (SRE)\n- Remove \u201cpreview\u201d labeling once SLOs and drift SLIs are met\n- Establish ongoing review cadence for spec changes\n- Publish runbooks and oncall rotation details\n\nh1. Launch checklist\n\nh2. Spec readiness\n- [ ] Spec v1 published with definitions for all required fields\n- [ ] Taxonomy keys finalized and documented\n- [ ] Backward compatibility rules documented (unknown fields tolerated by clients; additive changes allowed; breaking changes require new major version)\n\nh2. API readiness\n- [ ] Endpoints implemented with request bounding and pagination/top-K\n- [ ] Auth/tenancy enforced (org_id/project_id)\n- [ ] Rate limits and timeouts documented\n- [ ] Client library available and used by Console and Optimize\n\nh2. Data readiness\n- [ ] Runtime metrics exporting required fields\n- [ ] Telemetry pipeline normalizes/validates fields\n- [ ] Data quality dashboards in place (missing fields, lag, schema version distribution)\n\nh2. Reliability readiness\n- [ ] SLO document approved and oncall ownership assigned\n- [ ] Dashboards and alerts configured (latency, error rate, drift)\n- [ ] Incident runbook published\n\nh2. Product readiness\n- [ ] Console: feature flag rollout plan, fallback behavior, user messaging on freshness/estimates\n- [ ] Optimize: guardrails and confidence gating; user-visible assumptions\n- [ ] Support enablement: internal guide for explaining Console vs invoice and what-if assumptions\n\nh2. Finance alignment\n- [ ] Overhead allocation policy approved and versioned\n- [ ] Mapping of taxonomy to FP&A reporting confirmed\n\nh1. Open questions (as of 2026-02-18)\n\n1) Overhead allocation presentation\n- Should allocated overhead be shown as a separate line item by default in Console, or only in \u201cdetails\u201d?\n\n2) Cache modeling representation\n- Do we attribute cache as negative cost (savings) or as separate metrics with compute already netted? (Preference: compute netted + explicit cache metrics and optional savings line item.)\n\n3) Confidence representation for what-if\n- v1 decision: qualitative (HIGH/MED/LOW) vs numeric interval. Optimize prefers an interval; platform prefers bounded size and simplicity.\n\n4) Multi-region and fallback routing\n- How should a single request that routes across regions/capacity tiers be represented? (Candidate: primary execution context + optional \u201cfallback_events\u201d summarized as strings; keep bounded.)\n\nh1. Appendix: Example (illustrative; not normative)\n\n{code}\nCost Model API - estimate (illustrative)\nRequest inputs: org_id, project_id, request_id OR request_summary\nResponse:\n- total_cost_usd: 0.002341\n- breakdown:\n  - compute.prefill: 0.000812\n  - compute.decode: 0.001329\n  - overhead.shared_allocated: 0.000200\n- token_counts: prefill=512, decode=214\n- cache_metrics: kv_hit_rate=0.37 (definition: fraction of prefill tokens served from cache)\n- batch_metrics: effective_batch_factor=1.8\n- model: redwood/llama-3.1-70b, version=2026-02-01, quant_profile_id=int8-kv\n- spec_version: 1.0\n- overhead_policy_version: 2026-02\n{code}\n\nh1. Owners\n\n- Product (PRD owner): Marissa Cole (Console)\n- Program management: Talia Benson\n- API/service lead: Ethan Park\n- Telemetry lead: Logan Wright\n- Optimize product owner: Aditya Rao\n- Finance stakeholders: Laura Bennett, Rishi Malhotra\n- SRE reliability lead: Rafael Mendes\n",
