{
  "title": "PRD: Standard Cost Model Spec + Internal Cost Model API (v1)",
  "space": "product-docs",
  "author": "Marissa Cole",
  "owner_team": "product",
  "status": "in_review",
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "created_at": "2026-01-10",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-18",
  "reviewers": [
    "Priya Natarajan",
    "Ethan Park",
    "Logan Wright",
    "Chloe Martin",
    "Aditya Rao",
    "Laura Bennett",
    "Rafael Mendes"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "cost-model",
    "prd",
    "console",
    "optimize",
    "telemetry",
    "billing",
    "api",
    "versioning"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-021-standardize-cost-model-interfaces.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-022-cost-breakdown-taxonomy.json",
    "sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/cost-model-api-v1-design-spec.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/cost-model-api-guidelines.json"
  ],
  "body": "h1. Summary

Redwood Inference currently computes and displays “cost” in multiple places (Console dashboards, billing hooks, Optimize prototypes, finance reporting). Each path uses slightly different definitions and inputs (prefill vs decode accounting, KV cache attribution, batching efficiency, quantization effects, overhead allocation, and handling of telemetry lag). This results in mismatched dashboards vs invoices, inconsistent ROI estimates, and friction during enterprise/security/finance reviews.

This PRD defines a single, versioned Standard Cost Model Spec and an internal Cost Model API (service + shared client library) that produces canonical cost primitives used by:
- Redwood Console: consistent, explorable cost breakdown views
- Redwood Optimize: defensible “what-if” projections for batching/caching/quantization recommendations
- Finance/FP&A: stable unit-economics reporting primitives and auditability
- Platform/Billing: aligned request attribution inputs and shared taxonomy

h1. Problem statement

h2. User pain

1) Console cost breakdown inconsistencies
- Engineers and customer admins see a cost breakdown in Console that may not match invoice totals.
- During incidents or telemetry gaps, Console can show partial or misleading cost attribution.

2) Optimize ROI trust gap
- Optimize “what-if” savings can be too optimistic if assumptions (e.g., cache warm-rate) aren’t explicit or bounded.
- Recommendations are hard to explain to customers because they lack a canonical breakdown taxonomy and confidence/assumptions.

3) Internal misalignment and slow iteration
- Telemetry, billing, and product teams do not share a single “source of truth” for cost definitions.
- Each team re-implements cost logic, making changes risky and increasing regressions.

h2. Business impact
- Reduced customer trust in cost transparency and “savings” claims.
- Increased support burden (cost mismatch tickets) and slower sales cycles for Dedicated/Private.
- Harder to manage unit economics and to reason about cost drivers across hardware SKUs and model versions.

h1. Goals and non-goals

h2. Goals (v1)

- Standardize cost representation and semantics across Console, Optimize, billing hooks, and finance reporting.
- Publish a versioned Standard Cost Model Spec (schemas + definitions) that is backwards compatible.
- Provide an internal Cost Model API that returns:
  - Per-request cost estimates (request-attributable)
  - Cost breakdown taxonomy (prefill/decode, cache hits/misses, batching efficiency, overhead allocation)
  - Aggregated breakdowns with bounded response sizes
  - “What-if” projections for batching/caching/quantization changes with guardrails and confidence fields
- Align telemetry and billing inputs to produce consistent primitives.
- Establish governance: ownership, review process, compatibility guarantees, and deprecation policy.

h2. Non-goals (v1)

- Replace billing/RevRec systems. The cost model provides standardized primitives but does not become the billing system of record.
- Provide a customer-facing pricing calculator or pricing policy engine.
- Perfect “true cost” in all cases; v1 prioritizes consistency, explainability, and bounded error with monitoring.

h1. Primary users and personas

- Console users (Engineering managers, platform engineers, FinOps-like roles at customers): need reliable, drill-down cost breakdowns to understand drivers and anomalies.
- Optimize users (ML engineers, platform teams): need credible “what-if” ROI numbers with explicit assumptions and confidence.
- Internal stakeholders:
  - Telemetry & Analytics (Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman): need clear contracts and data quality rules.
  - Platform Control Plane (Ethan Park, Benji Okafor, Kaitlyn Nguyen): need stable APIs, tenancy/auth, rate limits.
  - Finance/FP&A (Laura Bennett, Rishi Malhotra): need stable categories and overhead allocation rules for reporting windows.

h1. Key use-cases

h2. Console use-cases (must support v1)

1) Request breakdown view
- Show request-attributable cost for a single request (or small set) with a clear split of:
  - Prefill tokens vs decode tokens
  - Cache hit vs miss attribution (where applicable)
  - Queue/scheduler overhead classification (as overhead vs request-attributable per policy)

2) Time-series breakdown for a route/model
- Show cost per 1K tokens and absolute cost over time.
- Drill down by model, model version, deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), region, and quantization profile.
- Bounded cardinality: must support top-K breakdowns and “other”.

3) Consistency with invoices (explainable deltas)
- Console must not diverge due to definitional drift.
- If invoice differs due to billing policy (rounding, minimums, credits), Console must be able to explain “cost primitives” vs “billing totals”.

h2. Optimize use-cases (must support v1)

1) ROI estimates for recommendations
- Given a workload summary (token distribution, cache behavior summary, current batching/quant profile), return projected cost delta for:
  - Increased batch size / improved batching efficiency
  - Increased cache hit rate (within guardrails)
  - Switching quantization profile (supported profiles)

2) Explainability and safety
- Optimize must surface: assumptions, constraints, and confidence indicators (e.g., bounded interval or qualitative confidence).
- Guardrails: reject/clip unrealistic what-if parameters (e.g., cache hit rate > 95% without evidence).

h2. Finance/FP&A use-cases (must support v1)

- Map cost breakdown taxonomy to unit economics reporting.
- Provide stable categories over reporting windows, with versioned specs and deprecation policies.

h1. Scope and product requirements

h2. In scope (v1)

1) Standard Cost Model Spec (schema + semantics)
- A versioned schema package that defines:
  - Inputs (what the cost model requires)
  - Outputs (what the cost model guarantees)
  - Breakdown taxonomy and definitions
  - Determinism requirements and rounding rules

2) Cost Model API (internal)
- Service endpoints used by Console and Optimize.
- Shared client library with timeouts, retries, and schema version negotiation.

3) Telemetry input contracts + validation
- Token metering and attribution fields required by spec.
- Required runtime-exported metrics (KV cache stats, prefill/decode split, batch efficiency measures).
- Data quality checks and drift monitoring.

4) Governance
- Documented ownership, review process, and a migration/deprecation policy.

h2. Out of scope (v1)

- Customer-facing public API for cost model results.
- Pricing policy changes.
- Full historical backfills beyond what is needed for validation and confidence-building.

h1. Functional requirements

h2. Canonical taxonomy (required)

The cost model must expose a stable breakdown taxonomy aligned to ADR-022. v1 requires these top-level categories:
- compute.prefill
- compute.decode
- memory.kv_cache (if modeled as separate line item; otherwise attribute via compute and expose cache metrics)
- overhead.request_attributable (e.g., per-request control-plane overhead if policy includes it)
- overhead.shared_allocated (allocated overhead per policy; must include policy_id/version)

Each category must have clear semantics:
- Prefill: prompt processing tokens (including system/user/tool messages) counted as prefill tokens.
- Decode: generated tokens counted as decode tokens.
- Cache: if prefix/KV cache prevents prefill compute, the model must attribute savings explicitly and expose cache hit-rate.
- Batching: model must account for batch efficiency, exposing the effective batch factor used.
- Quantization: model must expose quantization profile identifiers and any modeled delta assumptions.

h2. Required outputs (v1)

Per request:
- total_cost_usd (request-attributable + allocated overhead per selected policy)
- cost_breakdown (by taxonomy keys; bounded number of keys)
- token_counts (prefill_tokens, decode_tokens)
- cache_metrics_summary (cache_hit_rate or hit/miss counts, with clear definition)
- batch_metrics_summary (effective_batch_size or batch_efficiency)
- model_identity (model_id, model_version, quant_profile_id)
- deployment_context (hosted/dedicated/private, region, hardware_sku)
- spec_version + policy_version

Aggregations:
- ability to request time-bucketed aggregates with filters and top-K dimensions.
- response bounding rules (top-K + other, max dimensions, max buckets).

What-if:
- projected_total_cost_usd
- projected_cost_breakdown
- delta_usd and delta_percent vs baseline
- assumptions (human-readable strings)
- guardrails_applied (human-readable strings)
- confidence indicator (qualitative or interval; exact representation is defined in the design spec)

h2. Required inputs (v1)

Minimum telemetry and catalog inputs required:
- Token accounting: prefill_tokens, decode_tokens, total_tokens (with precise definitions)
- Cache: prefix/KV cache hits/misses (or hit rate) with consistent units
- Scheduler/batching: batch size distribution summary or effective batch factor
- Runtime path identifiers: quantization execution path/profile
- Deployment context: environment, region, hardware SKU, capacity mode
- Cost rates: GPU $/hr (or internal normalized rate) and overhead allocation policy inputs

h1. Non-functional requirements

h2. Performance and bounds
- P95 latency targets (internal):
  - Single-request estimate: p95 <= 50ms in-region
  - Aggregation query (bounded): p95 <= 250ms for typical Console dashboard queries
- Hard bounds:
  - Max time range per query (e.g., 7 days for high-cardinality breakdown endpoints; longer ranges require pre-aggregation)
  - Max buckets (e.g., 2,000)
  - Max dimension values returned per request (top-K + other)

h2. Correctness and determinism
- Same inputs + same spec version + same policy version must produce identical outputs.
- Document rounding and precision (e.g., USD precision to 1e-6, display rounding handled by callers).
- Drift SLI: track predicted vs observed spend within agreed tolerances and with lag awareness.

h2. Reliability
- API must degrade safely:
  - If cost-model API is degraded, Console should fall back to existing computation for a limited window (behind feature flag).
  - Optimize must fail closed (no recommendation) if confidence is too low or request is outside guardrails.

h2. Security and tenancy
- Enforce tenant isolation (org_id/project_id).
- Auth: service-to-service auth with scoped permissions.
- Audit logs for access to finance-adjacent aggregations.

h1. Success metrics

h2. Adoption metrics
- >= 90% of Console cost breakdown traffic uses Cost Model API within 4 weeks of GA (excluding explicitly exempt routes).
- >= 80% of Optimize recommendation ROI computations use Cost Model API within 4 weeks of GA.

h2. Quality metrics
- Cost mismatch support tickets (Console vs invoice) reduced by 50% within 8 weeks (measured via Support/Jira tags).
- Drift SLI:
  - Median monthly drift (modeled cost vs observed spend) within +/- 5% for Hosted and Dedicated (after lag correction)
  - Alerts on sustained drift > 10% over 24 hours (with telemetry lag gating)

h2. Performance metrics
- Meet p95 latency targets for top Console queries.
- Error budget compliance per SLO doc.

h2. Trust/Explainability metrics
- Optimize ROI “too optimistic” escalations reduced by 30% within 8 weeks.
- At least one customer-facing narrative (via CS) validated: ability to explain cost drivers using standard taxonomy.

h1. UX / Product requirements (Console + Optimize)

h2. Console requirements
- Console must display:
  - Spec version and policy version (at least in “details” view)
  - A consistent breakdown table that matches taxonomy keys
  - A note when results are estimated vs observed, and when telemetry lag applies

h2. Optimize requirements
- Optimize must display:
  - Baseline cost assumptions and inputs
  - What-if parameters and any guardrails applied
  - Confidence indicator and rationale

h1. Dependencies

- Runtime metrics exports (KV cache stats, prefill/decode token split, batching metrics) owned by Runtime Scheduling/Kernels (Sofia Ivanova, Omar El-Sayed, Grace Kim).
- Telemetry normalization and contracts owned by Telemetry & Analytics (Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman).
- Model catalog must expose stable quant_profile_id and metadata.
- Finance approval of overhead allocation policy and reporting windows.
- SRE SLOs, dashboards, and incident runbooks.

h1. Risks and mitigations

1) Cardinality explosion in aggregation endpoints
- Risk: high-cardinality dimensions (route, customer, model version, region) create slow/expensive queries.
- Mitigation: strict request bounds, top-K + other, pre-aggregation for common dashboards, caching.

2) Telemetry lag and missing fields
- Risk: drift alerts or incorrect dashboard values due to delayed ingestion or schema mismatch.
- Mitigation: lag-aware correctness SLI, explicit “data freshness” fields, fallback paths, conformance tests.

3) Mismatch between “cost primitives” and “invoice totals”
- Risk: customers expect exact match; billing includes credits, rounding, minimums.
- Mitigation: document difference; add “billing_adjustments” as a separate concept (not rolled into primitives) and ensure Console messaging is clear.

4) Overfitting what-if projections
- Risk: Optimize projects savings that cannot be realized operationally.
- Mitigation: guardrails; require evidence-based constraints; confidence gating; track realized vs projected where possible.

h1. Phased rollout plan (Q1 2026 target)

h2. Phase 0: Discovery (Weeks 1–2)
Owner: Talia Benson (program), Marissa Cole (product)
- Inventory existing cost definitions (Console, billing, Optimize prototypes)
- Confirm must-have v1 fields and taxonomy
- Produce v1 spec outline + open questions list

h2. Phase 1: Spec + ADRs (Weeks 3–5)
Owner: Ethan Park (API), Logan Wright (telemetry)
- Publish Standard Cost Model Spec v1 (schema + semantics)
- Approve ADR-021/022 alignment
- Define compatibility rules and deprecation policy

h2. Phase 2: Implementation (Weeks 6–9)
Owner: Ethan Park, Benji Okafor, Kaitlyn Nguyen
- Implement internal Cost Model API v1 endpoints
- Add shared client library with version negotiation
- Add conformance tests and golden fixtures

h2. Phase 3: Integration + Validation (Weeks 10–12)
Owners: Chloe Martin (Console), Aditya Rao (Optimize)
- Console integration behind feature flag (route-by-route enablement)
- Optimize integration for top recommendation types
- Backtesting vs observed spend and validation dashboards

h2. Phase 4: GA + Governance (Week 13+)
Owners: Marissa Cole (product), Rafael Mendes (SRE)
- Remove “preview” labeling once SLOs and drift SLIs are met
- Establish ongoing review cadence for spec changes
- Publish runbooks and oncall rotation details

h1. Launch checklist

h2. Spec readiness
- [ ] Spec v1 published with definitions for all required fields
- [ ] Taxonomy keys finalized and documented
- [ ] Backward compatibility rules documented (unknown fields tolerated by clients; additive changes allowed; breaking changes require new major version)

h2. API readiness
- [ ] Endpoints implemented with request bounding and pagination/top-K
- [ ] Auth/tenancy enforced (org_id/project_id)
- [ ] Rate limits and timeouts documented
- [ ] Client library available and used by Console and Optimize

h2. Data readiness
- [ ] Runtime metrics exporting required fields
- [ ] Telemetry pipeline normalizes/validates fields
- [ ] Data quality dashboards in place (missing fields, lag, schema version distribution)

h2. Reliability readiness
- [ ] SLO document approved and oncall ownership assigned
- [ ] Dashboards and alerts configured (latency, error rate, drift)
- [ ] Incident runbook published

h2. Product readiness
- [ ] Console: feature flag rollout plan, fallback behavior, user messaging on freshness/estimates
- [ ] Optimize: guardrails and confidence gating; user-visible assumptions
- [ ] Support enablement: internal guide for explaining Console vs invoice and what-if assumptions

h2. Finance alignment
- [ ] Overhead allocation policy approved and versioned
- [ ] Mapping of taxonomy to FP&A reporting confirmed

h1. Open questions (as of 2026-02-18)

1) Overhead allocation presentation
- Should allocated overhead be shown as a separate line item by default in Console, or only in “details”?

2) Cache modeling representation
- Do we attribute cache as negative cost (savings) or as separate metrics with compute already netted? (Preference: compute netted + explicit cache metrics and optional savings line item.)

3) Confidence representation for what-if
- v1 decision: qualitative (HIGH/MED/LOW) vs numeric interval. Optimize prefers an interval; platform prefers bounded size and simplicity.

4) Multi-region and fallback routing
- How should a single request that routes across regions/capacity tiers be represented? (Candidate: primary execution context + optional “fallback_events” summarized as strings; keep bounded.)

h1. Appendix: Example (illustrative; not normative)

{code}
Cost Model API - estimate (illustrative)
Request inputs: org_id, project_id, request_id OR request_summary
Response:
- total_cost_usd: 0.002341
- breakdown:
  - compute.prefill: 0.000812
  - compute.decode: 0.001329
  - overhead.shared_allocated: 0.000200
- token_counts: prefill=512, decode=214
- cache_metrics: kv_hit_rate=0.37 (definition: fraction of prefill tokens served from cache)
- batch_metrics: effective_batch_factor=1.8
- model: redwood/llama-3.1-70b, version=2026-02-01, quant_profile_id=int8-kv
- spec_version: 1.0
- overhead_policy_version: 2026-02

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Cost Model Service (cost-model-api) \\u2014 Service Overview\",\n  \"space\": \"eng-platform\",\n  \"author\": \"Ethan Park\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-16\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-02-21\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Rafael Mendes\",\n    \"Logan Wright\",\n    \"Chloe Martin\",\n    \"Laura Bennett\",\n    \"Allison Grant\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"cost-model\",\n    \"internal-api\",\n    \"observability\",\n    \"billing-hooks\",\n    \"telemetry\",\n    \"slo\",\n    \"versioning\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"confluence://eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/cost-model-api-slo\",\n    \"confluence://product-docs/design-specs/cost-model-api-v1-design-spec\",\n    \"confluence://architecture-and-standards/api-standards/cost-model-api-guidelines\",\n    \"confluence://architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-021-standardize-cost-model-interfaces\",\n    \"confluence://architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-022-cost-breakdown-taxonomy\",\n    \"confluence://eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/cost-model-api-observability\",\n    \"confluence://eng-sre/runbooks/cost-model-api-incident-runbook\"\n  ],\n  \"body\": \"## Summary\\nCost Model Service (service name: **cost-model-api**) provides a single, versioned implementation for inference cost estimation and cost breakdowns across Redwood products.\\n\\nIt is the canonical source for:\\n- **Per-request cost estimates** and standardized breakdown taxonomy (prefill/decode, cache, batch efficiency, overhead allocation, quantization deltas)\\n- **Aggregated cost breakdowns** for Console dashboards (bounded-cardinality responses)\\n- **What-if projections** used by Optimize to quantify ROI from configuration changes (batching/caching/quantization)\\n\\nThis document describes architecture, dependencies, SLOs, ownership/on-call, and rollout strategy.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Service owners\\n**Primary owner team:** Platform Control Plane\\n- Service/API lead: Ethan Park\\n- Control plane integration: Benji Okafor, Cole Summers\\n- Auth/tenancy: Kaitlyn Nguyen\\n\\n**Reliability partner:** SRE\\n- Reliability lead: Rafael Mendes\\n\\n**Key dependencies owners:**\\n- Telemetry & Analytics: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman\\n- Runtime metrics/instrumentation: Sofia Ivanova, Omar El-Sayed, Grace Kim\\n- Finance alignment: Laura Bennett, Rishi Malhotra\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Where this service sits\\nThe Cost Model Service is an internal service + shared library that standardizes cost calculations. It is intentionally *not* the billing system of record.\\n\\n### Primary callers\\n- **Redwood Console backend** (hot path for cost breakdown pages; calls are cacheable)\\n- **Redwood Optimize backend** (what-if projections; heavier compute but guarded and bounded)\\n- **Finance/analytics pipelines** (offline reconciliations and reporting windows; typically via batch exports or aggregated endpoints)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## High-level architecture (text diagram)\\n\\n```\\n            +-----------------------+\\n            |  Redwood Console BE   |\\n            |  (dashboards, APIs)   |\\n            +-----------+-----------+\\n                        |\\n                        | (internal, mTLS)\\n                        v\\n+-----------------------+-----------------------+\\n|                cost-model-api                 |\\n|----------------------------------------------|\\n|  1) Request validation + tenancy/authz        |\\n|  2) Version negotiation (schema + semantics)  |\\n|  3) Cost computation engine                   |\\n|     - cost breakdown taxonomy                 |\\n|     - overhead allocation policy              |\\n|     - quantization profile deltas             |\\n|  4) Response bounding + aggregation guards    |\\n|  5) Cache (read-through) for hot keys         |\\n+-----------+-------------------+---------------+\\n            |                   |\\n            |                   |\\n            v                   v\\n  +------------------+   +---------------------+\\n  | Telemetry Store  |   | Model Catalog       |\\n  | (token + runtime |   | (model + quant      |\\n  |  metrics, lag)   |   |  profile metadata)  |\\n  +------------------+   +---------------------+\\n            |\\n            v\\n  +------------------+\\n  | Drift Monitor Job|\\n  | (scheduled; SLI) |\\n  +------------------+\\n            |\\n            v\\n  +------------------+\\n  | Observed Spend / |\\n  | Billing Primitives|\\n  +------------------+\\n\\n            +-----------------------+\\n            |   Redwood Optimize    |\\n            | (recommendations/ROI) |\\n            +-----------+-----------+\\n                        |\\n                        v\\n                 (what-if endpoints)\\n```\\n\\nNotes:\\n- **Console** calls are latency-sensitive; the service is designed to be cache-friendly and returns bounded responses.\\n- **Optimize** calls can be more compute-heavy, but are constrained by request guardrails (limits on parameter ranges, cardinality, and time horizon).\\n- A **drift monitoring job** compares predicted vs observed spend to produce a correctness/drift SLI.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Dependencies\\n\\n### Required upstream data\\n1) **Telemetry Store** (authoritative inputs for per-request and aggregated cost)\\n- Token accounting: prompt/prefill tokens, decode tokens, output tokens\\n- Cache metrics: KV cache hit/miss rates and bytes (when available), cache eligibility flags\\n- Scheduling metrics: effective batch size, queue time, batching window outcomes\\n- Runtime stage breakdown: prefill vs decode wall time and/or token accounting split\\n\\nOwners: Telemetry & Analytics (Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman)\\n\\n2) **Model Catalog**\\n- Model identifiers, versions, architecture class\\n- Hardware compatibility metadata\\n- **Quantization profile IDs** and relevant metadata used by the cost model\\n\\nOwner: Platform / Model Catalog maintainers (in coordination with Applied ML)\\n\\n3) **Overhead allocation policy**\\n- Finance-approved policy to allocate shared costs to request-attributable vs overhead buckets\\n- Reporting windows and reconciliation rules\\n\\nOwners: Finance/FP&A (Laura Bennett, Rishi Malhotra) + Platform\\n\\n### Downstream integrations\\n- Console cost breakdown views (feature flag gated)\\n- Optimize ROI estimates and recommendation guardrails\\n- Billing hooks alignment (shared primitives; may intentionally differ for invoicing semantics; see ADRs)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Data flow & request types\\n\\n### Request types supported (v1)\\n- **Estimate**: Per-request estimated cost + breakdown (for request detail / tracing contexts)\\n- **Breakdown**: Aggregated cost breakdown over a bounded query window (for dashboards)\\n- **What-if**: Projected deltas based on configuration changes (for Optimize)\\n\\n### Query bounding (hard requirements)\\nTo prevent cardinality and latency blowups, the service enforces:\\n- Maximum time window per request (e.g., dashboard query windows must be bounded; long-range queries require pre-aggregation)\\n- Maximum number of group-by dimensions\\n- Maximum response size (rows and bytes)\\n- Allowed parameter ranges for what-if (e.g., batch size multipliers, cache warm-rate assumptions, quantization profile sets)\\n\\nThe exact limits are maintained in the API standards addendum and service config.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Cost computation model (implementation overview)\\nThe cost-model-api combines three layers:\\n\\n1) **Standard Cost Spec (schema + semantics)**\\n- Versioned schemas for inputs/outputs (e.g., cost_model_spec v1)\\n- Explicit semantics for:\\n  - Prefill vs decode attribution\\n  - Cache hits vs misses vs ineligible requests\\n  - Batch efficiency and queue-time effects\\n  - Quantization profile deltas (throughput/memory impacts; quality guardrails)\\n  - Overhead allocation buckets\\n\\n2) **Deterministic computation engine**\\n- Pure functions over canonical inputs where possible\\n- Stable rounding rules and currency/unit conventions\\n- Explicit \\u201cunknown/unavailable\\u201d handling for missing telemetry fields (no silent backfill that changes semantics)\\n\\n3) **Confidence/uncertainty for projections (What-if only)**\\n- What-if returns a point estimate plus a confidence indicator when driven by empirically learned parameters\\n- Guardrails prevent projections when input uncertainty is too high or when inputs are out of policy bounds\\n\\n---\\n\\n## SLAs / SLOs (service-level)\\nDetailed SLO definitions live in the SLO page (see related pages). This section summarizes the operational targets used by Platform + SRE.\\n\\n### Availability SLO\\n- **99.9%** monthly availability for core endpoints used by Console\\n- Degraded-mode behavior is allowed (see \\u201cFallbacks\\u201d)\\n\\n### Latency SLO (p95)\\n- Estimate/Breakdown endpoints (Console path): **p95 < 250ms** for cache-hit and **p95 < 600ms** for cache-miss under typical dashboard query bounds\\n- What-if endpoint (Optimize path): **p95 < 2.0s** for bounded scenarios\\n\\n### Correctness / Drift SLI\\n- A scheduled drift job compares predicted costs (from cost-model primitives) to observed spend attribution over an agreed reporting window.\\n- Alerting is based on drift thresholds that account for telemetry lag and overhead allocation windows.\\n\\n### Error budget policy\\n- If latency or errors threaten Console UX, the Console integration must automatically fall back to the legacy breakdown path (flag-controlled), and SRE may request a rollout pause.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Reliability: fallbacks and failure modes\\n\\n### Client fallbacks (required)\\n- Console must implement:\\n  - Timeouts (short)\\n  - Retries (bounded)\\n  - Fallback behavior (legacy cost breakdown implementation) behind a feature flag\\n\\n- Optimize must implement:\\n  - Timeouts (longer)\\n  - No unbounded retries\\n  - Safe default behavior (suppress recommendation / show \\u201cinsufficient confidence\\u201d) when the what-if endpoint is unavailable\\n\\n### Common failure modes\\n- **Telemetry lag / partial ingestion** \\u2192 drift alerts, missing fields, inconsistent breakdowns\\n- **Schema mismatch / version negotiation errors** \\u2192 4xx from service; clients should downgrade gracefully\\n- **Cardinality explosion** from overly broad group-bys \\u2192 request rejected with explicit error code\\n- **Cache stampede** on common dashboard keys \\u2192 mitigated via request coalescing + short TTL caching\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Deployment & environments\\n- Environments: dev, staging, prod\\n- Deployed as a standard internal control-plane service with:\\n  - mTLS service-to-service auth\\n  - Tenant-aware authorization checks\\n  - Per-route rate limits (stricter for what-if)\\n\\nConfig highlights:\\n- Cache TTLs are endpoint-specific\\n- Feature flags control:\\n  - Console adoption percentage\\n  - Optimize what-if enablement\\n  - Strictness of schema enforcement (e.g., rejecting vs warning on unknown fields)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## On-call & escalation\\n\\n### On-call rotation\\n- **Primary:** Platform Control Plane on-call (cost-model-api)\\n- **Secondary:** SRE on-call (platform services)\\n\\n### Escalation\\n- Telemetry ingestion incidents: page Telemetry & Analytics on-call\\n- Runtime instrumentation regressions: page Runtime Scheduling/Kernels on-call\\n- Finance reconciliation concerns (non-urgent): route to FP&A partner (Rishi Malhotra) via ticket\\n\\n### Operational readiness requirements\\nBefore enabling Console in production beyond initial canary:\\n- Dashboards exist for latency, error rates, request volume, version distribution, and drift\\n- Runbook is current and linked in service alerts\\n- Client fallback is verified in staging with forced fault injection\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Observability\\nMetrics emitted by cost-model-api:\\n- Request volume by endpoint + tenant tier (bounded cardinality)\\n- Latency (p50/p95/p99) by endpoint\\n- Error rates by error class (validation, auth, upstream dependency, compute timeout)\\n- Cache hit ratio (endpoint-level)\\n- Schema version distribution (requested vs served)\\n- Drift metrics (from scheduled job) and telemetry lag indicators\\n\\nLogging/tracing:\\n- Trace IDs propagated from Console/Optimize\\n- Logs must not include raw prompts or customer content; only derived counts and stable identifiers\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Rollout strategy\\n\\n### Phase 0 \\u2014 Service bootstrap (completed)\\n- Ship service skeleton, auth/tenancy, and schema package\\n- Implement bounded endpoints with deterministic behavior\\n\\n### Phase 1 \\u2014 Staging integrations\\n- Console integration behind flag with fallback enabled\\n- Optimize integration behind flag for internal tenants only\\n- Validate schema version negotiation behavior\\n\\n### Phase 2 \\u2014 Production canary\\n- Enable for a small set of internal tenants and low-risk customers\\n- Monitor: latency, errors, schema version distribution, and drift SLI\\n- Compare Console breakdowns vs legacy for a sample of dashboard queries\\n\\n### Phase 3 \\u2014 Expand adoption\\n- Increase Console coverage gradually (e.g., 5% \\u2192 25% \\u2192 50% \\u2192 100%)\\n- Expand Optimize what-if access with strict guardrails\\n- Align billing hooks to consume the same primitives (document intentional differences)\\n\\n### Rollback plan\\n- Immediate rollback via feature flag to legacy breakdowns (Console)\\n- Disable what-if endpoint exposure (Optimize) and freeze new recommendation rollouts\\n- If drift alerts are driven by telemetry lag: widen lag tolerance window temporarily and open follow-up work with Telemetry\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Open items / follow-ups\\n- Finalize drift thresholds by deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private)\\n- Reduce dependency on high-cardinality telemetry dimensions for dashboard queries (prefer pre-aggregations)\\n- Document a clear customer-support explanation template for \\u201cConsole vs invoice differences\\u201d rooted in the standard taxonomy and reporting windows\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Appendix: operational checklist (quick)\\n- [ ] Pager routes to Platform Control Plane on-call\\n- [ ] Dashboards present in Grafana (latency/errors/version/drift)\\n- [ ] Alerts link to runbook\\n- [ ] Client timeouts + fallback verified\\n- [ ] Request bounds tested (reject oversized queries)\\n- [ ] Schema version negotiation tested across Console/Optimize client library versions\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_b70ef35a4bbc433081fdda277f9c0fe8\"\n}",

{
  "title": "Cost Model Service (cost-model-api) — Service Overview",
  "space": "eng-platform",
  "author": "Ethan Park",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-01-16",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-21",
  "reviewers": [
    "Rafael Mendes",
    "Logan Wright",
    "Chloe Martin",
    "Laura Bennett",
    "Allison Grant"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "cost-model",
    "internal-api",
    "observability",
    "billing-hooks",
    "telemetry",
    "slo",
    "versioning"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "related_pages": [
    "confluence://eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/cost-model-api-slo",
    "confluence://product-docs/design-specs/cost-model-api-v1-design-spec",
    "confluence://architecture-and-standards/api-standards/cost-model-api-guidelines",
    "confluence://architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-021-standardize-cost-model-interfaces",
    "confluence://architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-022-cost-breakdown-taxonomy",
    "confluence://eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/cost-model-api-observability",
    "confluence://eng-sre/runbooks/cost-model-api-incident-runbook"
  ],
  "body": "## Summary
Cost Model Service (service name: **cost-model-api**) provides a single, versioned implementation for inference cost estimation and cost breakdowns across Redwood products.

It is the canonical source for:
- **Per-request cost estimates** and standardized breakdown taxonomy (prefill/decode, cache, batch efficiency, overhead allocation, quantization deltas)
- **Aggregated cost breakdowns** for Console dashboards (bounded-cardinality responses)
- **What-if projections** used by Optimize to quantify ROI from configuration changes (batching/caching/quantization)

This document describes architecture, dependencies, SLOs, ownership/on-call, and rollout strategy.

---

## Service owners
**Primary owner team:** Platform Control Plane
- Service/API lead: Ethan Park
- Control plane integration: Benji Okafor, Cole Summers
- Auth/tenancy: Kaitlyn Nguyen

**Reliability partner:** SRE
- Reliability lead: Rafael Mendes

**Key dependencies owners:**
- Telemetry & Analytics: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman
- Runtime metrics/instrumentation: Sofia Ivanova, Omar El-Sayed, Grace Kim
- Finance alignment: Laura Bennett, Rishi Malhotra

---

## Where this service sits
The Cost Model Service is an internal service + shared library that standardizes cost calculations. It is intentionally *not* the billing system of record.

### Primary callers
- **Redwood Console backend** (hot path for cost breakdown pages; calls are cacheable)
- **Redwood Optimize backend** (what-if projections; heavier compute but guarded and bounded)
- **Finance/analytics pipelines** (offline reconciliations and reporting windows; typically via batch exports or aggregated endpoints)

---

## High-level architecture (text diagram)

```
            +-----------------------+
            |  Redwood Console BE   |
            |  (dashboards, APIs)   |
            +-----------+-----------+
                        |
                        | (internal, mTLS)
                        v
+-----------------------+-----------------------+
|                cost-model-api                 |
|----------------------------------------------|
|  1) Request validation + tenancy/authz        |
|  2) Version negotiation (schema + semantics)  |
|  3) Cost computation engine                   |
|     - cost breakdown taxonomy                 |
|     - overhead allocation policy              |
|     - quantization profile deltas             |
|  4) Response bounding + aggregation guards    |
|  5) Cache (read-through) for hot keys         |
+-----------+-------------------+---------------+
            |                   |
            |                   |
            v                   v
  +------------------+   +---------------------+
  | Telemetry Store  |   | Model Catalog       |
  | (token + runtime |   | (model + quant      |
  |  metrics, lag)   |   |  profile metadata)  |
  +------------------+   +---------------------+
            |
            v
  +------------------+
  | Drift Monitor Job|
  | (scheduled; SLI) |
  +------------------+
            |
            v
  +------------------+
  | Observed Spend / |
  | Billing Primitives|
  +------------------+

            +-----------------------+
            |   Redwood Optimize    |
            | (recommendations/ROI) |
            +-----------+-----------+
                        |
                        v
                 (what-if endpoints)
```

Notes:
- **Console** calls are latency-sensitive; the service is designed to be cache-friendly and returns bounded responses.
- **Optimize** calls can be more compute-heavy, but are constrained by request guardrails (limits on parameter ranges, cardinality, and time horizon).
- A **drift monitoring job** compares predicted vs observed spend to produce a correctness/drift SLI.

---

## Dependencies

### Required upstream data
1) **Telemetry Store** (authoritative inputs for per-request and aggregated cost)
- Token accounting: prompt/prefill tokens, decode tokens, output tokens
- Cache metrics: KV cache hit/miss rates and bytes (when available), cache eligibility flags
- Scheduling metrics: effective batch size, queue time, batching window outcomes
- Runtime stage breakdown: prefill vs decode wall time and/or token accounting split

Owners: Telemetry & Analytics (Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman)

2) **Model Catalog**
- Model identifiers, versions, architecture class
- Hardware compatibility metadata
- **Quantization profile IDs** and relevant metadata used by the cost model

Owner: Platform / Model Catalog maintainers (in coordination with Applied ML)

3) **Overhead allocation policy**
- Finance-approved policy to allocate shared costs to request-attributable vs overhead buckets
- Reporting windows and reconciliation rules

Owners: Finance/FP&A (Laura Bennett, Rishi Malhotra) + Platform

### Downstream integrations
- Console cost breakdown views (feature flag gated)
- Optimize ROI estimates and recommendation guardrails
- Billing hooks alignment (shared primitives; may intentionally differ for invoicing semantics; see ADRs)

---

## Data flow & request types

### Request types supported (v1)
- **Estimate**: Per-request estimated cost + breakdown (for request detail / tracing contexts)
- **Breakdown**: Aggregated cost breakdown over a bounded query window (for dashboards)
- **What-if**: Projected deltas based on configuration changes (for Optimize)

### Query bounding (hard requirements)
To prevent cardinality and latency blowups, the service enforces:
- Maximum time window per request (e.g., dashboard query windows must be bounded; long-range queries require pre-aggregation)
- Maximum number of group-by dimensions
- Maximum response size (rows and bytes)
- Allowed parameter ranges for what-if (e.g., batch size multipliers, cache warm-rate assumptions, quantization profile sets)

The exact limits are maintained in the API standards addendum and service config.

---

## Cost computation model (implementation overview)
The cost-model-api combines three layers:

1) **Standard Cost Spec (schema + semantics)**
- Versioned schemas for inputs/outputs (e.g., cost_model_spec v1)
- Explicit semantics for:
  - Prefill vs decode attribution
  - Cache hits vs misses vs ineligible requests
  - Batch efficiency and queue-time effects
  - Quantization profile deltas (throughput/memory impacts; quality guardrails)
  - Overhead allocation buckets

2) **Deterministic computation engine**
- Pure functions over canonical inputs where possible
- Stable rounding rules and currency/unit conventions
- Explicit “unknown/unavailable” handling for missing telemetry fields (no silent backfill that changes semantics)

3) **Confidence/uncertainty for projections (What-if only)**
- What-if returns a point estimate plus a confidence indicator when driven by empirically learned parameters
- Guardrails prevent projections when input uncertainty is too high or when inputs are out of policy bounds

---

## SLAs / SLOs (service-level)
Detailed SLO definitions live in the SLO page (see related pages). This section summarizes the operational targets used by Platform + SRE.

### Availability SLO
- **99.9%** monthly availability for core endpoints used by Console
- Degraded-mode behavior is allowed (see “Fallbacks”)

### Latency SLO (p95)
- Estimate/Breakdown endpoints (Console path): **p95 < 250ms** for cache-hit and **p95 < 600ms** for cache-miss under typical dashboard query bounds
- What-if endpoint (Optimize path): **p95 < 2.0s** for bounded scenarios

### Correctness / Drift SLI
- A scheduled drift job compares predicted costs (from cost-model primitives) to observed spend attribution over an agreed reporting window.
- Alerting is based on drift thresholds that account for telemetry lag and overhead allocation windows.

### Error budget policy
- If latency or errors threaten Console UX, the Console integration must automatically fall back to the legacy breakdown path (flag-controlled), and SRE may request a rollout pause.

---

## Reliability: fallbacks and failure modes

### Client fallbacks (required)
- Console must implement:
  - Timeouts (short)
  - Retries (bounded)
  - Fallback behavior (legacy cost breakdown implementation) behind a feature flag

- Optimize must implement:
  - Timeouts (longer)
  - No unbounded retries
  - Safe default behavior (suppress recommendation / show “insufficient confidence”) when the what-if endpoint is unavailable

### Common failure modes
- **Telemetry lag / partial ingestion** → drift alerts, missing fields, inconsistent breakdowns
- **Schema mismatch / version negotiation errors** → 4xx from service; clients should downgrade gracefully
- **Cardinality explosion** from overly broad group-bys → request rejected with explicit error code
- **Cache stampede** on common dashboard keys → mitigated via request coalescing + short TTL caching

---

## Deployment & environments
- Environments: dev, staging, prod
- Deployed as a standard internal control-plane service with:
  - mTLS service-to-service auth
  - Tenant-aware authorization checks
  - Per-route rate limits (stricter for what-if)

Config highlights:
- Cache TTLs are endpoint-specific
- Feature flags control:
  - Console adoption percentage
  - Optimize what-if enablement
  - Strictness of schema enforcement (e.g., rejecting vs warning on unknown fields)

---

## On-call & escalation

### On-call rotation
- **Primary:** Platform Control Plane on-call (cost-model-api)
- **Secondary:** SRE on-call (platform services)

### Escalation
- Telemetry ingestion incidents: page Telemetry & Analytics on-call
- Runtime instrumentation regressions: page Runtime Scheduling/Kernels on-call
- Finance reconciliation concerns (non-urgent): route to FP&A partner (Rishi Malhotra) via ticket

### Operational readiness requirements
Before enabling Console in production beyond initial canary:
- Dashboards exist for latency, error rates, request volume, version distribution, and drift
- Runbook is current and linked in service alerts
- Client fallback is verified in staging with forced fault injection

---

## Observability
Metrics emitted by cost-model-api:
- Request volume by endpoint + tenant tier (bounded cardinality)
- Latency (p50/p95/p99) by endpoint
- Error rates by error class (validation, auth, upstream dependency, compute timeout)
- Cache hit ratio (endpoint-level)
- Schema version distribution (requested vs served)
- Drift metrics (from scheduled job) and telemetry lag indicators

Logging/tracing:
- Trace IDs propagated from Console/Optimize
- Logs must not include raw prompts or customer content; only derived counts and stable identifiers

---

## Rollout strategy

### Phase 0 — Service bootstrap (completed)
- Ship service skeleton, auth/tenancy, and schema package
- Implement bounded endpoints with deterministic behavior

### Phase 1 — Staging integrations
- Console integration behind flag with fallback enabled
- Optimize integration behind flag for internal tenants only
- Validate schema version negotiation behavior

### Phase 2 — Production canary
- Enable for a small set of internal tenants and low-risk customers
- Monitor: latency, errors, schema version distribution, and drift SLI
- Compare Console breakdowns vs legacy for a sample of dashboard queries

### Phase 3 — Expand adoption
- Increase Console coverage gradually (e.g., 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%)
- Expand Optimize what-if access with strict guardrails
- Align billing hooks to consume the same primitives (document intentional differences)

### Rollback plan
- Immediate rollback via feature flag to legacy breakdowns (Console)
- Disable what-if endpoint exposure (Optimize) and freeze new recommendation rollouts
- If drift alerts are driven by telemetry lag: widen lag tolerance window temporarily and open follow-up work with Telemetry

---

## Open items / follow-ups
- Finalize drift thresholds by deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- Reduce dependency on high-cardinality telemetry dimensions for dashboard queries (prefer pre-aggregations)
- Document a clear customer-support explanation template for “Console vs invoice differences” rooted in the standard taxonomy and reporting windows

---

## Appendix: operational checklist (quick)
- [ ] Pager routes to Platform Control Plane on-call
- [ ] Dashboards present in Grafana (latency/errors/version/drift)
- [ ] Alerts link to runbook
- [ ] Client timeouts + fallback verified
- [ ] Request bounds tested (reject oversized queries)
- [ ] Schema version negotiation tested across Console/Optimize client library versions

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_cef6bc52b49b4f459244b882d7187ab1",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4832-billing-hooks-alignment-with-cost-model.json",
    "title": "Align quotas/billing hooks to Standard Cost Model primitives + document intentional differences",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-4832\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Align quotas/billing hooks to Standard Cost Model primitives + document intentional differences\",\n  \"status\": \"In Review\",\n  \"priority\": \"P0\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-03\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-02-24\",\n  \"creator\": \"Talia Benson\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Cole Summers\",\n  \"project\": \"Standard Cost Model Spec + API\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W07\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-03-06\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"cost-model\",\n    \"billing\",\n    \"quotas\",\n    \"telemetry-contracts\",\n    \"finance-alignment\",\n    \"backward-compat\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-4822\",\n    \"ENG-4823\",\n    \"ENG-4830\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"description\": \"Problem\\n- Today Console/Optimize are converging on a Standard Cost Model spec + API, but quotas enforcement and billing hooks still use a separate set of token/cost primitives.\\n- This causes discrepancies between:\\n  (a) Console \\u201ccost breakdown\\u201d views\\n  (b) Optimize \\u201cwhat-if savings\\u201d projections\\n  (c) internal finance/unit economics reporting\\n  (d) customer invoice line items and quota burn\\n- We need quotas/billing hooks to be powered by the same canonical primitives so \\u201cwhat counts\\u201d is consistent, while explicitly documenting intentional differences where billing must diverge (e.g., pricing plans, rounding, credits, contractual adjustments).\\n\\nGoal\\n- Refactor quotas + billing hooks to consume Standard Cost Model primitives (schema v1), using the same token-attribution inputs and stage breakdown semantics (prefill/decode, cache, batch efficiency signals) where applicable.\\n- Provide a clear mapping layer from cost primitives -> billable units for invoicing (hosted API), and from primitives -> quota units for enforcement.\\n- Document (and test) any intentional differences so Support/Finance/Console can explain deltas and we can prevent drift regressions.\\n\\nNon-goals\\n- Replacing billing/RevRec systems or changing customer-facing pricing plans.\\n- Introducing new invoice line items (unless explicitly approved by Finance + PM; out of scope for v1).\\n\\nPrimary owners/stakeholders\\n- Owner: Cole Summers (billing hooks integration)\\n- Platform/API: Ethan Park, Kaitlyn Nguyen\\n- Telemetry: Nadia Rahman, Logan Wright\\n- Finance/FP&A: Laura Bennett, Rishi Malhotra\\n- Console: Chloe Martin / Jada Williams (for explaining deltas and support workflows)\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": \"Functional\\n- Quota burn (hosted API) and billing hooks both ingest the same canonical request primitives used by the cost-model service/library (schema v1).\\n- For every request, billing hooks persist:\\n  - cost_model_spec_version (e.g., cost-model/v1)\\n  - input primitive snapshot (bounded, no PII)\\n  - derived billable units (input/output tokens or equivalent)\\n  - mapping_version (billing-mapping/v1) to make future changes auditable.\\n- Console can reconcile: \\u201cinvoice tokens\\u201d vs \\u201cstandard cost model request-attributable cost\\u201d with a documented explanation of differences.\\n\\nCorrectness / determinism\\n- Deterministic mapping function from primitives -> billable units for the same spec version + mapping version.\\n- Backfill/replay on golden fixtures shows no material change to invoiced totals for a representative set of tenants (unless explicitly approved + communicated).\\n\\nObservability\\n- Emit metrics for:\\n  - billing_hook_primitive_missing_count (by field)\\n  - billing_hook_mapping_version_distribution\\n  - delta between billing-derived unit cost and cost-model-estimated request-attributable cost (aggregated)\\n  - telemetry lag impact indicators (so drift alerts don\\u2019t page spuriously)\\n\\nDocumentation\\n- Confluence page section or README update that enumerates intentional differences:\\n  - what billing includes/excludes vs cost-model breakdown\\n  - rounding policy\\n  - credit/minimum commit handling\\n  - contract pricing overrides\\n  - backfill/correction behavior\\n\\nRollout\\n- Feature-flagged rollout per environment (staging -> canary tenants -> broader).\\n- Safe fallback to legacy billing hook path if primitives are unavailable or validation fails (with alerting).\",\n  \"implementation_notes\": \"Proposed approach\\n1) Introduce a shared \\u201cbilling mapping\\u201d module that consumes cost-model primitives:\\n   - Input: CostModelRequestPrimitives (schema v1) + tenant pricing context\\n   - Output: BillableUnitsV1 { billable_input_tokens, billable_output_tokens, billable_embeddings_units, \\u2026 }\\n   - Versioned: billing-mapping/v1 (explicitly separate from cost-model spec version)\\n\\n2) Align quota enforcement to the same derived BillableUnitsV1 where possible.\\n   - Quotas should remain defined in customer-facing units (e.g., tokens) even if internal cost modeling uses richer breakdown.\\n\\n3) Persist both:\\n   - raw primitives (bounded and sanitized)\\n   - derived billable units\\n   to support auditability + reconciliation.\\n\\nKey mapping rules (v1 proposal; confirm with Finance)\\n- billable_input_tokens = request.input_tokens_total\\n  - Clarify cache behavior: if request uses server-side prefix/KV cache, we still bill based on customer plan policy.\\n  - Default v1: billable_input_tokens reflect tokens provided by customer in the prompt (not internal cache hits), unless plan explicitly bills for cache reads (currently we do not).\\n- billable_output_tokens = request.decode_tokens_total\\n- Do not include overhead allocation categories as billable line items.\\n- Any cost-model fields related to batch efficiency, queue time, kernel path, quantization deltas are non-billable diagnostics; they may affect internal cost estimates but should not directly change token billing units.\\n\\nIntentional differences to document (expected deltas)\\n- Billing vs standard cost:\\n  - Billing uses contract price tables, free credits, minimum commits, and invoice adjustments; cost-model returns internal estimated cost breakdown.\\n  - Billing rounds units according to invoicing rules (e.g., per 1K token blocks or cents precision) while cost-model returns high-precision floats.\\n  - Billing is based on finalized metering with late-arriving corrections; cost-model may use near-real-time telemetry and should expose \\u201cprovisional\\u201d flags.\\n- Quotas vs billing:\\n  - Quotas may be stricter/earlier (enforcement at request time) while billing is post-hoc; document behavior during telemetry lag or retries.\\n\\nOpen questions\\n- Cache billing policy: confirm current stance for hosted API for prefix/KV cache hits (policy appears to be \\u201cdon\\u2019t charge for internal cache reuse\\u201d). If incorrect, we need to update mapping rules and comms.\\n- Retries: ensure we don\\u2019t double-count billable units on upstream retry behavior (client retries vs internal hedging).\\n- Streaming: confirm token accounting boundaries for partial streams and aborted responses.\\n\\nTesting plan\\n- Add unit tests for mapping module using golden fixtures from ENG-4831.\\n- Add an integration test that replays a small anonymized request log through:\\n  (a) legacy billing hook\\n  (b) new primitives-based mapping\\n  and asserts equivalence within approved tolerances (ideally exact equality for billable token counts).\\n- Add a canary dashboard comparing legacy vs new derived billable tokens per tenant/day.\",\n  \"rollout_plan\": \"Phase 0 (prep)\\n- Land mapping module behind a flag (billing_mapping_v1_enabled=false by default).\\n- Add dual-write mode in staging: compute both legacy and new, log deltas.\\n\\nPhase 1 (staging)\\n- Enable for staging tenants and run replay/backfill validation.\\n\\nPhase 2 (prod canary)\\n- Enable for 1\\u20133 internal or friendly tenants (low spend) + monitor:\\n  - delta metrics\\n  - support ticket volume\\n  - any increase in quota enforcement errors\\n\\nPhase 3 (gradual ramp)\\n- Expand by tenant cohorts; stop the ramp if delta > threshold or missing primitives spike.\\n\\nPhase 4 (default)\\n- Make primitives-based path default; keep legacy path as emergency fallback for one release window.\\n\\nRollback\\n- Flip flag to disable mapping v1 and revert to legacy billing hook path; alert Finance if any invoices may be impacted.\",\n  \"links\": [\n    \"Confluence PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/standard-cost-model-prd.json\",\n    \"Cost Model API design: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/cost-model-api-v1-design-spec.json\",\n    \"ADR-021: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-021-standardize-cost-model-interfaces.json\",\n    \"ADR-022: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-022-cost-breakdown-taxonomy.json\",\n    \"Finance alignment: sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/budgeting-and-forecasting/unit-economics-cost-model-alignment.json\",\n    \"Related PR (planned/linked): sources/github/redwood/pr-28521-billing-hooks-align-to-standard-cost-primitives.json\",\n    \"Support case motivating reconciliation: sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-31844-console-cost-breakdown-does-not-match-invoice.json\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2026-02-05 (Cole Summers): Initial pass at mapping rules. Strong preference to keep billing in customer-facing units (input/output tokens) and treat cost-model breakdown as non-billable diagnostics. Will add mapping_version and persist primitive snapshots for audit/replay.\",\n    \"2026-02-06 (Laura Bennett): Finance requirement: any change that could affect invoice totals needs (1) replay evidence, (2) explicit sign-off, and (3) a way to reconstruct billed units from stored metering. Also please document rounding/credits/adjustments as the primary reasons invoice totals won\\u2019t equal \\u201crequest-attributable cost.\\u201d\",\n    \"2026-02-08 (Nadia Rahman): Telemetry contract note: prefill/decode split is stable now, but cache hit metrics may be delayed for some runtimes.       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Align quotas/billing hooks to Standard Cost Model primitives + document intentional differences\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4832-billing-hooks-alignment-with-cost-model.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: Standard Cost Model Spec + API\nTeam: engineering\n\nintentional differences to document ( expected deltas ) - billing vs standard cost : - billing uses contract price tables, free credits, minimum commits, and invoice adjustments ; cost - model returns internal estimated cost breakdown. - billing rounds units according to invoicing rules ( e. g., per 1k token blocks or cents precision ) while cost - model returns high - precision floats. - billing is based on finalized metering with late - arriving corrections ; cost - model may use near - real - time telemetry and should expose “ provisional ” flags. - quotas vs billing : - quotas may be stricter / earlier ( enforcement at request time ) while billing is post - hoc ; document behavior during telemetry lag or retries.",

document.title: Align quotas/billing hooks to Standard Cost Model primitives + document intentional differences
document.content:
{
  "key": "ENG-4832",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Align quotas/billing hooks to Standard Cost Model primitives + document intentional differences",
  "status": "In Review",
  "priority": "P0",
  "created_at": "2026-02-03",
  "updated_at": "2026-02-24",
  "creator": "Talia Benson",
  "assignee": "Cole Summers",
  "project": "Standard Cost Model Spec + API",
  "cycle": "2026-W07",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2026-03-06",
  "labels": [
    "cost-model",
    "billing",
    "quotas",
    "telemetry-contracts",
    "finance-alignment",
    "backward-compat"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-4822",
    "ENG-4823",
    "ENG-4830"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Problem
- Today Console/Optimize are converging on a Standard Cost Model spec + API, but quotas enforcement and billing hooks still use a separate set of token/cost primitives.
- This causes discrepancies between:
  (a) Console “cost breakdown” views
  (b) Optimize “what-if savings” projections
  (c) internal finance/unit economics reporting
  (d) customer invoice line items and quota burn
- We need quotas/billing hooks to be powered by the same canonical primitives so “what counts” is consistent, while explicitly documenting intentional differences where billing must diverge (e.g., pricing plans, rounding, credits, contractual adjustments).

Goal
- Refactor quotas + billing hooks to consume Standard Cost Model primitives (schema v1), using the same token-attribution inputs and stage breakdown semantics (prefill/decode, cache, batch efficiency signals) where applicable.
- Provide a clear mapping layer from cost primitives -> billable units for invoicing (hosted API), and from primitives -> quota units for enforcement.
- Document (and test) any intentional differences so Support/Finance/Console can explain deltas and we can prevent drift regressions.

Non-goals
- Replacing billing/RevRec systems or changing customer-facing pricing plans.
- Introducing new invoice line items (unless explicitly approved by Finance + PM; out of scope for v1).

Primary owners/stakeholders
- Owner: Cole Summers (billing hooks integration)
- Platform/API: Ethan Park, Kaitlyn Nguyen
- Telemetry: Nadia Rahman, Logan Wright
- Finance/FP&A: Laura Bennett, Rishi Malhotra
- Console: Chloe Martin / Jada Williams (for explaining deltas and support workflows)",
  "acceptance_criteria": "Functional
- Quota burn (hosted API) and billing hooks both ingest the same canonical request primitives used by the cost-model service/library (schema v1).
- For every request, billing hooks persist:
  - cost_model_spec_version (e.g., cost-model/v1)
  - input primitive snapshot (bounded, no PII)
  - derived billable units (input/output tokens or equivalent)
  - mapping_version (billing-mapping/v1) to make future changes auditable.
- Console can reconcile: “invoice tokens” vs “standard cost model request-attributable cost” with a documented explanation of differences.

Correctness / determinism
- Deterministic mapping function from primitives -> billable units for the same spec version + mapping version.
- Backfill/replay on golden fixtures shows no material change to invoiced totals for a representative set of tenants (unless explicitly approved + communicated).

Observability
- Emit metrics for:
  - billing_hook_primitive_missing_count (by field)
  - billing_hook_mapping_version_distribution
  - delta between billing-derived unit cost and cost-model-estimated request-attributable cost (aggregated)
  - telemetry lag impact indicators (so drift alerts don’t page spuriously)

Documentation
- Confluence page section or README update that enumerates intentional differences:
  - what billing includes/excludes vs cost-model breakdown
  - rounding policy
  - credit/minimum commit handling
  - contract pricing overrides
  - backfill/correction behavior

Rollout
- Feature-flagged rollout per environment (staging -> canary tenants -> broader).
- Safe fallback to legacy billing hook path if primitives are unavailable or validation fails (with alerting).",
  "implementation_notes": "Proposed approach
1) Introduce a shared “billing mapping” module that consumes cost-model primitives:
   - Input: CostModelRequestPrimitives (schema v1) + tenant pricing context
   - Output: BillableUnitsV1 { billable_input_tokens, billable_output_tokens, billable_embeddings_units, … }
   - Versioned: billing-mapping/v1 (explicitly separate from cost-model spec version)

2) Align quota enforcement to the same derived BillableUnitsV1 where possible.
   - Quotas should remain defined in customer-facing units (e.g., tokens) even if internal cost modeling uses richer breakdown.

3) Persist both:
   - raw primitives (bounded and sanitized)
   - derived billable units
   to support auditability + reconciliation.

Key mapping rules (v1 proposal; confirm with Finance)
- billable_input_tokens = request.input_tokens_total
  - Clarify cache behavior: if request uses server-side prefix/KV cache, we still bill based on customer plan policy.
  - Default v1: billable_input_tokens reflect tokens provided by customer in the prompt (not internal cache hits), unless plan explicitly bills for cache reads (currently we do not).
- billable_output_tokens = request.decode_tokens_total
- Do not include overhead allocation categories as billable line items.
- Any cost-model fields related to batch efficiency, queue time, kernel path, quantization deltas are non-billable diagnostics; they may affect internal cost estimates but should not directly change token billing units.

Intentional differences to document (expected deltas)
- Billing vs standard cost:
  - Billing uses contract price tables, free credits, minimum commits, and invoice adjustments; cost-model returns internal estimated cost breakdown.
  - Billing rounds units according to invoicing rules (e.g., per 1K token blocks or cents precision) while cost-model returns high-precision floats.
  - Billing is based on finalized metering with late-arriving corrections; cost-model may use near-real-time telemetry and should expose “provisional” flags.
- Quotas vs billing:
  - Quotas may be stricter/earlier (enforcement at request time) while billing is post-hoc; document behavior during telemetry lag or retries.

Open questions
- Cache billing policy: confirm current stance for hosted API for prefix/KV cache hits (policy appears to be “don’t charge for internal cache reuse”). If incorrect, we need to update mapping rules and comms.
- Retries: ensure we don’t double-count billable units on upstream retry behavior (client retries vs internal hedging).
- Streaming: confirm token accounting boundaries for partial streams and aborted responses.

Testing plan
- Add unit tests for mapping module using golden fixtures from ENG-4831.
- Add an integration test that replays a small anonymized request log through:
  (a) legacy billing hook
  (b) new primitives-based mapping
  and asserts equivalence within approved tolerances (ideally exact equality for billable token counts).
- Add a canary dashboard comparing legacy vs new derived billable tokens per tenant/day.",

- Land mapping module behind a flag (billing_mapping_v1_enabled=false by default).
- Add dual-write mode in staging: compute both legacy and new, log deltas.

Phase 1 (staging)
- Enable for staging tenants and run replay/backfill validation.

Phase 2 (prod canary)
- Enable for 1–3 internal or friendly tenants (low spend) + monitor:
  - delta metrics
  - support ticket volume
  - any increase in quota enforcement errors

Phase 3 (gradual ramp)
- Expand by tenant cohorts; stop the ramp if delta > threshold or missing primitives spike.

Phase 4 (default)
- Make primitives-based path default; keep legacy path as emergency fallback for one release window.

Rollback
- Flip flag to disable mapping v1 and revert to legacy billing hook path; alert Finance if any invoices may be impacted.",

exact models vary by workspace)\"\n  ],\n  \"sla_due_at\": \"2026-02-21\",\n  \"first_response_due_at\": \"2026-02-20\",\n  \"related_incident_id\": \"INC-2026-02-19-telemetry-lag-drift-alert\",\n  \"linked_issues\": [\n    \"SUP-31905-latency-spike-on-cost-model-endpoint\",\n    \"INT-10992-request-access-cost-model-dashboards\",\n    \"SUP-31877-what-if-cost-savings-seem-too-optimistic\"\n  ],\n  \"related_github_prs\": [\n    \"sources/github/redwood/pr-28470-console-cost-breakdown-switch-to-cost-model-api.json\",\n    \"sources/github/redwood/pr-28521-billing-hooks-align-to-standard-cost-primitives.json\",\n    \"sources/github/redwood/pr-28490-cost-model-drift-monitoring-job.json\"\n  ],\n  \"related_confluence_pages\": [\n    \"sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-022-cost-breakdown-taxonomy.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/budgeting-and-forecasting/unit-economics-cost-model-alignment.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/cost-model-api-observability.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/cost-model-api-incident-runbook.json\"\n  ],\n  \"description\": \"Issue summary\\n- Customer reports that the Redwood Console \\\"Cost breakdown\\\" totals for Feb do not match their Feb invoice totals. They are treating Console as the authoritative cost number for internal allocation and are seeing a ~6\\u20139% delta depending on workspace.\\n\\nCustomer / account context\\n- Customer: Northbridge Security Labs (enterprise)\\n- Deployment: Hosted API + some Dedicated capacity add-on (per CSM notes)\\n- Stakeholders: Engineering + Finance (invoice reconciliation)\\n- Customer expectation: Console breakdown totals should reconcile to invoice for the same period when filtered to the same org/workspaces.\\n\\nImpact\\n- High trust risk with finance stakeholder; customer is escalating internally.\\n- Customer blocked on monthly internal chargeback using Console exports.\\n\\nWhat customer is seeing\\n- Console (Cost Breakdown view) totals: lower than invoice.\\n- Invoice includes line items for: usage (tokens), reserved capacity commit true-up, platform/enterprise fee, and credits/adjustments.\\n- Customer is currently comparing invoice grand total vs Console usage-only total.\\n\\nEnvironment\\n- Production\\n- Regions: mostly us-east; some eu-west.\\n\\nInitial hypotheses (triage)\\n1) Mismatched reporting window/timezone: invoice is calendar month UTC; Console default filter uses local timezone and/or includes partial current day unless explicitly bounded.\\n2) Console view currently powered by Standard Cost Model behind flag for some orgs; invoice still sourced from billing ledger logic. If overhead allocation or \\\"non-request-attributable\\\" costs are represented differently, totals will not reconcile.\\n3) Telemetry lag event around 2026-02-19 triggered drift alert; possible missing late-arriving usage events in Console aggregation, later corrected in invoice.\\n4) Credits/discounts/commit true-ups appear on invoice but not included in Console breakdown taxonomy (Console currently shows request-attributable runtime costs + configured overhead allocation policy, but not contract artifacts).\\n\\nRequested outcome\\n- Provide customer a reconciliation explanation and a concrete, repeatable method to reconcile Console vs invoice.\\n- If there is an actual defect (e.g., Console includes overhead but invoice excludes, or vice versa), identify and fix.\\n\\nSupport request details / customer message excerpt (paraphrased)\\n\\\"We exported Console cost breakdown for 2026-02-01..2026-02-29 and the total is $X, but the invoice shows $Y. We need to understand what Console includes/excludes and how to reconcile. Our finance team expects these to match.\\\"\\n\\nAttachments / links (internal)\\n- Grafana: Cost Model drift dashboard (org-level drift around 2026-02-19)\\n- Console cost export shared in ticket (uploaded to support case file store; not attached here)\\n- Slack: #finance thread on overhead allocation policy and reporting windows\\n\\nNext steps\\n- Confirm whether customer is opted into Console->Cost Model API integration flag.\\n- Align on exact date range and timezone used by customer export.\\n- Compare Console \\\"request-attributable\\\" subtotal to invoice usage subtotal (excluding platform fee, reserved capacity commit true-ups, taxes, and credits).\\n- Validate whether telemetry lag affected customer\\u2019s February window aggregates.\\n\",\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2026-02-20 09:18 PT \\u2014 Marissa Cole (Reporter / Console Product): Opened on behalf of CSM escalation. Customer finance team expects Console to reconcile 1:1 with invoice for the month. Please prioritize explanation + any fix needed.\",\n    \"2026-02-20 10:02 PT \\u2014 Chloe Martin (Assignee / Console Integration): Confirming Console cost breakdown for this org is behind feature flag \\\"console_cost_breakdown_use_cost_model_api\\\"; rollout began last week for ~10% enterprise orgs. I\\u2019ll verify flag state for Northbridge and pull a sample response from Cost Model API for the same window.\",\n    \"2026-02-20 10:34 PT \\u2014 Logan Wright (Telemetry Lead): Noted drift alert on 2026-02-19 correlated with telemetry lag from ingestion backlog (see incident thread). Lag window was ~2\\u20134 hours; late events backfilled. If Console materializes aggregates before late events arrive, you can see temporary undercount until backfill completes.\",\n    \"2026-02-20 11:10 PT \\u2014 Laura Bennett (Finance): Reminder: invoice includes non-usage line items (platform fee, commit true-ups, credits/adjustments, taxes). Console should be presented as usage + (optional) overhead allocation, not contract artifacts. We need an explicit reconciliation note + a stable mapping for enterprise customers.\",\n    \"2026-02-20 13:26 PT \\u2014 Chloe Martin: Verified flag ON for Northbridge. Console is showing Cost Model v1 breakdown. Console \\\"Total\\\" currently sums: request_attributable_total + overhead_allocated_total. Invoice grand total includes additional items. For this customer, the delta seems to match their reserved capacity commit true-up + enterprise platform fee.\",\n    \"2026-02-21 08:41 PT \\u2014 Jada Williams (Console Backend): Also found a UI bug: in the export CSV, the header says \\\"Total (USD)\\\" without clarifying it\\u2019s usage-only (plus allocated overhead) and excludes credits/commit/platform fees. Suggest we rename column and add tooltip + docs link. This isn\\u2019t a cost computation bug, it\\u2019s a semantics/UX mismatch.\",\n    \"2026-02-21 09:15 PT \\u2014 Ethan Park (Service/API Lead): Confirming Cost Model API taxonomy is per ADR-022: request-attributable costs + explicitly modeled overhead allocation. It intentionally does not model contract-level items (fees, discounts, credits, taxes). Billing is aligned to primitives, but invoice assembly is separate. Recommend we add a Console banner/learn-more for enterprise invoices.\",\n    \"2026-02-21 10:27 PT \\u2014 Marissa Cole: Action items:\\n1) Support response to customer with reconciliation steps and explicit exclusions.\\n2) Console UX: change label \\\"Total\\\" to \\\"Usage total\\\" and add invoice reconciliation note.\\n3) Confirm telemetry lag did not permanently affect Feb totals (only transient).\",\n    \"2026-02-24 14:03 PT \\u2014 Chloe Martin: Ran backtest for Feb 1\\u201329 UTC (org_id redacted). Cost Model API aggregates match billing usage subtotal within 0.4% after late-arrival backfill; remaining difference is explained by (a) commit true-up and (b) platform fee not represented in Console breakdown. No evidence of ongoing undercount.\",\n    \"2026-02-25 09:32 PT \\u2014 Support (via Marissa): Sent customer reconciliation note: compare invoice \\\"Usage\\\" line item subtotal to Console \\\"Usage total\\\" for matching UTC calendar month; exclude platform fee/commit true-ups/credits/taxes. Provided screenshot and filter settings (UTC, Feb 1 00:00 to Mar 1 00:00). Customer acknowledged and will update their internal process.\",\n    \"2026-03-01 16:20 PT \\u2014 Chloe Martin: Closing as Resolved. Follow-up product task opened for Console labeling and docs link (tracked in Console backlog; not a support ticket).\"\n  ],\n  \"resolution\": \"Resolved with reconciliation guidance and validation. Root cause was expectation mismatch: Console breakdown represents request-attributable usage costs (plus configured overhead allocation) per Standard Cost Model taxonomy, while invoice grand total includes contract-level items (platform fee, reserved capacity commit true-ups, credits/adjustments, taxes). Also identified a Console export labeling issue contributing to confusion. Verified no persistent telemetry undercount for Feb after late-arrival backfill; usage subtotal reconciles within expected tolerance.\",\n  \"workaround\": \"For reconciliation: use UTC calendar month boundaries; compare Console \\\"Usage total\\\" (request-attributable + allocated overhead) to invoice usage subtotal only. Do not compare to invoice grand total. Account for platform fee, commit true-ups, credits/adjustments, and taxes separately.\",\n  \"next_steps\": [\n    \"Update Console UI/CSV export labels to clarify what is included/excluded (usage vs invoice).\",\n    \"Add a docs link in Console to Standard Cost Model taxonomy and enterprise invoice reconciliation guidance.\",\n    \"Add monitoring note to Console export flow to avoid materializing aggregates during telemetry lag windows (or display 'data still backfilling' state).\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"summary\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"comments\",\n    \"resolution\",\n    \"workaround\",\n    \"next_steps\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_ebccf3a528bc4b0097206c04ebbf5dbd\"\n}",
