document.title: Console cost breakdown totals do not match invoice totals (Northbridge Security Labs)
document.content:
{
  "key": "SUP-31844",
  "project": "customer-support",
  "issue_type": "Bug",
  "summary": "Console cost breakdown totals do not match invoice totals (Northbridge Security Labs)",
  "status": "Resolved",
  "priority": "P1",
  "severity": "Sev2",
  "created_at": "2026-02-20",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-01",
  "reporter": "Marissa Cole",
  "assignee": "Chloe Martin",
  "customer_company": "Northbridge Security Labs",
  "customer_tier": "enterprise",
  "components": [
    "console",
    "billing",
    "telemetry",
    "cost-model-api"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "cost-attribution",
    "invoice-mismatch",
    "standard-cost-model",
    "drift-sli",
    "enterprise"
  ],
  "environment": "prod (Console + Billing); customer primarily in us-east with some eu-west usage",
  "affected_regions": [
    "us-east",
    "eu-west"
  ],
  "affected_models": [
    "multiple (customer uses mixed chat + embeddings routes; exact models vary by workspace)"
  ],
  "sla_due_at": "2026-02-21",
  "first_response_due_at": "2026-02-20",
  "related_incident_id": "INC-2026-02-19-telemetry-lag-drift-alert",
  "linked_issues": [
    "SUP-31905-latency-spike-on-cost-model-endpoint",
    "INT-10992-request-access-cost-model-dashboards",
    "SUP-31877-what-if-cost-savings-seem-too-optimistic"
  ],
  "related_github_prs": [
    "sources/github/redwood/pr-28470-console-cost-breakdown-switch-to-cost-model-api.json",
    "sources/github/redwood/pr-28521-billing-hooks-align-to-standard-cost-primitives.json",
    "sources/github/redwood/pr-28490-cost-model-drift-monitoring-job.json"
  ],
  "related_confluence_pages": [
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-022-cost-breakdown-taxonomy.json",
    "sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/budgeting-and-forecasting/unit-economics-cost-model-alignment.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/cost-model-api-observability.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/cost-model-api-incident-runbook.json"
  ],
  "description": "Issue summary\n- Customer reports that the Redwood Console \"Cost breakdown\" totals for Feb do not match their Feb invoice totals. They are treating Console as the authoritative cost number for internal allocation and are seeing a ~6\u20139% delta depending on workspace.\n\nCustomer / account context\n- Customer: Northbridge Security Labs (enterprise)\n- Deployment: Hosted API + some Dedicated capacity add-on (per CSM notes)\n- Stakeholders: Engineering + Finance (invoice reconciliation)\n- Customer expectation: Console breakdown totals should reconcile to invoice for the same period when filtered to the same org/workspaces.\n\nImpact\n- High trust risk with finance stakeholder; customer is escalating internally.\n- Customer blocked on monthly internal chargeback using Console exports.\n\nWhat customer is seeing\n- Console (Cost Breakdown view) totals: lower than invoice.\n- Invoice includes line items for: usage (tokens), reserved capacity commit true-up, platform/enterprise fee, and credits/adjustments.\n- Customer is currently comparing invoice grand total vs Console usage-only total.\n\nEnvironment\n- Production\n- Regions: mostly us-east; some eu-west.\n\nInitial hypotheses (triage)\n1) Mismatched reporting window/timezone: invoice is calendar month UTC; Console default filter uses local timezone and/or includes partial current day unless explicitly bounded.\n2) Console view currently powered by Standard Cost Model behind flag for some orgs; invoice still sourced from billing ledger logic. If overhead allocation or \"non-request-attributable\" costs are represented differently, totals will not reconcile.\n3) Telemetry lag event around 2026-02-19 triggered drift alert; possible missing late-arriving usage events in Console aggregation, later corrected in invoice.\n4) Credits/discounts/commit true-ups appear on invoice but not included in Console breakdown taxonomy (Console currently shows request-attributable runtime costs + configured overhead allocation policy, but not contract artifacts).\n\nRequested outcome\n- Provide customer a reconciliation explanation and a concrete, repeatable method to reconcile Console vs invoice.\n- If there is an actual defect (e.g., Console includes overhead but invoice excludes, or vice versa), identify and fix.\n\nSupport request details / customer message excerpt (paraphrased)\n\"We exported Console cost breakdown for 2026-02-01..2026-02-29 and the total is $X, but the invoice shows $Y. We need to understand what Console includes/excludes and how to reconcile. Our finance team expects these to match.\"\n\nAttachments / links (internal)\n- Grafana: Cost Model drift dashboard (org-level drift around 2026-02-19)\n- Console cost export shared in ticket (uploaded to support case file store; not attached here)\n- Slack: #finance thread on overhead allocation policy and reporting windows\n\nNext steps\n- Confirm whether customer is opted into Console->Cost Model API integration flag.\n- Align on exact date range and timezone used by customer export.\n- Compare Console \"request-attributable\" subtotal to invoice usage subtotal (excluding platform fee, reserved capacity commit true-ups, taxes, and credits).\n- Validate whether telemetry lag affected customer\u2019s February window aggregates.\n",
  "comments": [
    "2026-02-20 09:18 PT \u2014 Marissa Cole (Reporter / Console Product): Opened on behalf of CSM escalation. Customer finance team expects Console to reconcile 1:1 with invoice for the month. Please prioritize explanation + any fix needed.",
    "2026-02-20 10:02 PT \u2014 Chloe Martin (Assignee / Console Integration): Confirming Console cost breakdown for this org is behind feature flag \"console_cost_breakdown_use_cost_model_api\"; rollout began last week for ~10% enterprise orgs. I\u2019ll verify flag state for Northbridge and pull a sample response from Cost Model API for the same window.",
    "2026-02-20 10:34 PT \u2014 Logan Wright (Telemetry Lead): Noted drift alert on 2026-02-19 correlated with telemetry lag from ingestion backlog (see incident thread). Lag window was ~2\u20134 hours; late events backfilled. If Console materializes aggregates before late events arrive, you can see temporary undercount until backfill completes.",
    "2026-02-20 11:10 PT \u2014 Laura Bennett (Finance): Reminder: invoice includes non-usage line items (platform fee, commit true-ups, credits/adjustments, taxes). Console should be presented as usage + (optional) overhead allocation, not contract artifacts. We need an explicit reconciliation note + a stable mapping for enterprise customers.",
    "2026-02-20 13:26 PT \u2014 Chloe Martin: Verified flag ON for Northbridge. Console is showing Cost Model v1 breakdown. Console \"Total\" currently sums: request_attributable_total + overhead_allocated_total. Invoice grand total includes additional items. For this customer, the delta seems to match their reserved capacity commit true-up + enterprise platform fee.",
    "2026-02-21 08:41 PT \u2014 Jada Williams (Console Backend): Also found a UI bug: in the export CSV, the header says \"Total (USD)\" without clarifying it\u2019s usage-only (plus allocated overhead) and excludes credits/commit/platform fees. Suggest we rename column and add tooltip + docs link. This isn\u2019t a cost computation bug, it\u2019s a semantics/UX mismatch.",
    "2026-02-21 09:15 PT \u2014 Ethan Park (Service/API Lead): Confirming Cost Model API taxonomy is per ADR-022: request-attributable costs + explicitly modeled overhead allocation. It intentionally does not model contract-level items (fees, discounts, credits, taxes). Billing is aligned to primitives, but invoice assembly is separate. Recommend we add a Console banner/learn-more for enterprise invoices.",
    "2026-02-21 10:27 PT \u2014 Marissa Cole: Action items:\n1) Support response to customer with reconciliation steps and explicit exclusions.\n2) Console UX: change label \"Total\" to \"Usage total\" and add invoice reconciliation note.\n3) Confirm telemetry lag did not permanently affect Feb totals (only transient).",
    "2026-02-24 14:03 PT \u2014 Chloe Martin: Ran backtest for Feb 1\u201329 UTC (org_id redacted). Cost Model API aggregates match billing usage subtotal within 0.4% after late-arrival backfill; remaining difference is explained by (a) commit true-up and (b) platform fee not represented in Console breakdown. No evidence of ongoing undercount.",
    "2026-02-25 09:32 PT \u2014 Support (via Marissa): Sent customer reconciliation note: compare invoice \"Usage\" line item subtotal to Console \"Usage total\" for matching UTC calendar month; exclude platform fee/commit true-ups/credits/taxes. Provided screenshot and filter settings (UTC, Feb 1 00:00 to Mar 1 00:00). Customer acknowledged and will update their internal process.",
    "2026-03-01 16:20 PT \u2014 Chloe Martin: Closing as Resolved. Follow-up product task opened for Console labeling and docs link (tracked in Console backlog; not a support ticket)."
  ],
  "resolution": "Resolved with reconciliation guidance and validation. Root cause was expectation mismatch: Console breakdown represents request-attributable usage costs (plus configured overhead allocation) per Standard Cost Model taxonomy, while invoice grand total includes contract-level items (platform fee, reserved capacity commit true-ups, credits/adjustments, taxes). Also identified a Console export labeling issue contributing to confusion. Verified no persistent telemetry undercount for Feb after late-arrival backfill; usage subtotal reconciles within expected tolerance.",
  "workaround": "For reconciliation: use UTC calendar month boundaries; compare Console \"Usage total\" (request-attributable + allocated overhead) to invoice usage subtotal only. Do not compare to invoice grand total. Account for platform fee, commit true-ups, credits/adjustments, and taxes separately.",
  "next_steps": [
    "Update Console UI/CSV export labels to clarify what is included/excluded (usage vs invoice).",
    "Add a docs link in Console to Standard Cost Model taxonomy and enterprise invoice reconciliation guidance.",
    "Add monitoring note to Console export flow to avoid materializing aggregates during telemetry lag windows (or display 'data still backfilling' state)."
  ],
  "title_field_name": "summary",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "comments",
    "resolution",
    "workaround",
    "next_steps"
  ],

}

document.title: Console cost dashboard: release choreography, micro-training, and escalation playbook
document.content:
{
  "key": "PM-51902",
  "team": "product-management",
  "title": "Console cost dashboard: release choreography, micro-training, and escalation playbook",
  "status": "In Review",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2025-02-10",
  "updated_at": "2025-02-18",
  "creator": "Ava Martinez",
  "assignee": "Liam O'Connor",
  "project": "console-cost-controls",
  "cycle": "2025-W07",
  "estimate": "5",
  "due_date": "2025-02-25",
  "labels": [
    "console",
    "launch",
    "cost-insights",
    "training",
    "release-notes"
  ],
  "parent_issue": [
    "PM-48800"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-7621",
    "DES-3412",
    "PM-49211"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "medium",
  "release": "console-2025.02",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Coordinated launch plan for the new Console Cost Breakdown dashboard feature. This ticket covers release choreography across PM/Eng/Design/Docs/Support, a micro-training curriculum for internal teams, the customer-facing release notes blurb, and an escalation playbook for post-launch anomalies (cost regressions, telemetry gaps, or rollout failures).",
  "goals": [
    "Ensure console cost dashboard ships with clear customer messaging and measurable adoption targets",
    "Equip support, sales engineering, and CSMs with a 20-minute micro-training and 1-page cheatsheet",
    "Define escalation paths and automated alerts for any cost telemetry regressions within the first 7 days"
  ],
  "stakeholders": [
    "Ava Martinez (PM)",
    "Priya Kapoor (Design)",
    "Diego Chen (Engineering - Runtime)",
    "Nikhil Rao (Engineering - Observability)",
    "Samira Nadeem (Docs)",
    "Maya Lewis (Support Lead)",
    "Jordan Patel (Sales Engineering)"
  ],
  "milestones": [
    "2025-02-11: Draft release notes and feature blurb complete",
    "2025-02-14: Design assets and micro-training deck signed off",
    "2025-02-16: Observability hooks + feature flag gated rollout in staging",
    "2025-02-20: Docs published and support runbook distributed",
    "2025-02-25: Public rollout scheduled (canary -> regional waves)"
  ],
  "launch_steps": [
    "PM: finalize customer-facing blurb and target messaging (Ava)",
    "Design: finalize dashboard microcopy + screenshots for release notes (Priya)",
    "Eng: implement feature-flag gating, telemetry events, and alert thresholds (Diego / Nikhil)",
    "Docs: short-form quickstart + 1-page cheatsheet for SE/Support (Samira)",
    "Support: tabletop run-through and escalation contract review (Maya)",
    "Sales Eng: prepare 30-min demo script and FAQs (Jordan)",
    "PMPS: coordinate customer comms list and timing (Ava)",
    "Launch: canary (10% customers) -> region waves with rollback window (Eng ops)",
    "Post-launch: 48h monitoring window with automatic rollback criteria"
  ],
  "training_plan": [
    "Module 0 (10m): What changed \u2014 feature summary + ideal use cases",
    "Module 1 (20m): Walkthrough of dashboard \u2014 filters, cost attribution, and comparison views",
    "Module 2 (15m): Troubleshooting common anomalies and interpreting telemetry",
    "Module 3 (15m): Escalation flow and SLAs \u2014 when to open an incident vs support ticket",
    "Artifacts: 1-page cheatsheet, 5-slide microdeck, recorded 30-min session"
  ],
  "comms_matrix": [
    "Internal - All-Hands email: high-level announcement + link to microtraining (owner: PM)",
    "Internal - Support Slack channel: runbook + escalation playbook (owner: Support Lead)",
    "External - Release notes page: feature blurb + screenshots (owner: Docs)",
    "External - Customer newsletter: targeted subset with beta opt-in (owner: Growth)",
    "External - Help center article: quickstart + FAQ (owner: Docs)",
    "Sales Eng - enablement: 30-min live session + replay link (owner: Sales Eng)",
    "Developer - changelog and SDK notes: API names and telemetry events (owner: Engineering)",
    "Monitoring - Pager rotation: alert routing and contact list (owner: SRE)",
    "Feedback - product-feedback channel: capture customer usability issues (owner: PM)",
    "Localization - i18n schedule: target locales and deadlines (owner: Localization PM)"
  ],
  "release_notes_blurb": "New: Cost Breakdown dashboard \u2014 see per-route and per-model token costs, customizable groupings, and quick comparisons across time ranges. Designed to surface unit economics and identify high-cost outliers. Available in Console for all paid accounts; toggleable via feature flag for staged rollout.",
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Telemetry event coverage >= 95% for dashboard interactions in staging",
    "Docs and release notes published and linked in console release banner",
    "Support and SE teams completed micro-training and acknowledged runbook",
    "Canary rollout executed with no critical regressions for 48h",
    "Automated alerts for cost deviation configured (thresholds and on-call routing)"
  ],
  "risks": [
    "Cost telemetry under-reporting causing incorrect cost attribution",
    "High-traffic queries produce increased latency in dashboard rendering",
    "Customer confusion about cost units leading to support volume spike",
    "Rollout gating misconfiguration exposes feature to unintended customers"
  ],
  "mitigations": [
    "Telemetry: add redundant events and a daily reconciliation job to catch gaps",
    "Performance: enforce query timeouts and limit default time window to 7 days",
    "Docs/Comms: include explicit unit examples (per-token, per-embed) and in-dashboard tooltips",
    "Rollout: require two-person approval to lift feature flag from canary to global"
  ],
  "links": [
    "https://confluence.redwoodinc.com/display/CON/Cost+Dashboard+Spec",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2345",
    "https://dashboard.redwood-inference.com/runs/telemetry/5241",
    "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-cost-dashboard-assets",
    "https://confluence.redwoodinc.com/display/OPS/Launch+Runbook+Template"
  ],
  "updates": [
    "2025-02-11: PM draft of release blurb posted; requested sample screenshots from Design",
    "2025-02-12: Design provided screenshot variants; recommended copy tweak to clarify per-token vs per-embed",
    "2025-02-14: Design sign-off (Priya) after copy tweak; microdeck initial draft complete",
    "2025-02-15: Eng added telemetry hooks and feature flag; staging endpoint available for validation",
    "2025-02-16: Observability added alert thresholds; PR #2345 opened for review (link in links)",
    "2025-02-17: Docs draft published to staging; Support runbook v0.1 shared with Maya for feedback",
    "2025-02-18: Cross-functional review scheduled; two outstanding items: i18n timeline and canary approval policy"
  ],

    "risks",
    "mitigations",
    "updates"
  ],

}

# Hosted API capability launch readiness

Decision owner: Ethan Park, Platform & Console  
Capability: Standard Cost Model Spec + internal Cost Model API v1  
Revision: 1 — product and delivery baseline  
Decision status: Pending cross-functional evidence

## Capability and supported scope

The planned capability is an internal, versioned Cost Model API used by Console, Optimize, billing hooks, and finance reporting to share canonical inference-cost primitives. V1 includes per-request estimates, bounded aggregated breakdowns, guarded what-if projections, schema negotiation, telemetry input contracts, and feature-flagged integrations. It is not a public customer API, a billing system of record, a pricing calculator, or a promise that Console grand totals equal invoices. [PM-1482](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/PM-1482-standard-cost-model-prd.json>) [PRD](</knowledge/company/sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/standard-cost-model-prd.json>)

## Satisfied product gates

- Product scope, non-goals, canonical taxonomy, success measures, and phased rollout are documented; PM-1482 is Done with required stakeholder approvals recorded. [PM-1482](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/PM-1482-standard-cost-model-prd.json>)
- The internal service skeleton, internal-only routing, scoped service principals, tenant resolution, audit fields, endpoint envelopes, initial bounds, and observability hooks are complete in ENG-4821. Owner: Benji Okafor; accountable: Ethan Park. [ENG-4821](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4821-cost-model-service-skeleton.json>)
- Console adoption is feature-flagged and has a legacy fallback requirement; v1 explicitly bounds synchronous work and keeps ad hoc analytics out of the hot path. Owners: Chloe Martin, Jada Williams, Ethan Park. [Platform decision thread](</knowledge/company/sources/slack/eng-platform/1768427740.json>)

## Unresolved delivery items

- Confirm schema/codegen completion and compatibility evidence for ENG-4822. Owner: Thomas Baird.
- Complete shared-client adoption and confirm timeout/retry/schema-negotiation behavior across Console and Optimize. Owner: Benji Okafor.
- Complete drift SLI, dashboards, alerts, and SRE approval in ENG-4827. Owner: Rafael Mendes.
- Complete billing-hook alignment, replay evidence, intentional-difference documentation, and Finance/Telemetry/Auth reviews in ENG-4832. Owners: Cole Summers, Laura Bennett, Nadia Rahman, Kaitlyn Nguyen.
- Close PRD checklist items whose authoritative Confluence page remains in review, including SLO/on-call, support enablement, and Finance mapping. Owners: Marissa Cole and named gate owners. [PRD](</knowledge/company/sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/standard-cost-model-prd.json>)

## Preliminary recommendation

Pending operational, security, release, customer, and support evidence. No launch date is asserted.

## Revision history

- Revision 1: established capability, product gates, scope, delivery gaps, and owners from product and engineering evidence.

Revision: 2 — operations, security, and release evidence  
Decision status: Conditional-go candidate for a tightly scoped flagged cohort; no broad launch

## Capability and supported launch scope

The capability is an internal, versioned Cost Model API that supplies canonical inference-cost primitives to Console, Optimize, billing hooks, and finance reporting. V1 supports request-bounded estimates, bounded reads from precomputed rollups, guarded what-if projections, schema negotiation, telemetry contracts, and feature-flagged integrations. It is not a public Hosted API, billing system of record, pricing calculator, ad hoc analytics engine, or guarantee that Console usage totals equal invoice grand totals. [PM-1482](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/PM-1482-standard-cost-model-prd.json>) [PRD](</knowledge/company/sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/standard-cost-model-prd.json>) [Platform decision](</knowledge/company/sources/slack/eng-platform/1769536063.json>)

Supported launch scope is limited to internal callers and an allowlisted Console cohort behind `console_cost_breakdown_use_cost_model_api`, with legacy aggregation fallback, bounded default views, cached last-known UI data, explicit freshness/partial-result states, and one-click flag rollback. Optimize or billing expansion must remain gated until their own acceptance evidence is complete.

## Gate assessment

| Gate | State | Evidence and owner |
|---|---|---|
| Product definition and stakeholder alignment | Satisfied | PM-1482 is Done and records required stakeholder approvals. Owner: Talia Benson / Marissa Cole. [PM-1482](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/PM-1482-standard-cost-model-prd.json>) |
| Internal service foundation | Satisfied | ENG-4821 is Done: internal-only exposure, service auth, tenant middleware, audit fields, endpoint scaffolding, bounds, and base observability. Owner: Benji Okafor; accountable: Ethan Park. [ENG-4821](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4821-cost-model-service-skeleton.json>) |
| Scope and complexity controls | Satisfied for limited scope | Request-level synchronous calls and bounded rollup reads are accepted; unbounded filtering and raw synchronous aggregation are excluded. Owner: Ethan Park / Thomas Baird. [Platform decision](</knowledge/company/sources/slack/eng-platform/1768427740.json>) [Performance budget](</knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/cost-model-performance-budget.json>) |
| Client build/CI | Satisfied at library level | Shared client PR reports passing build, unit, lint, API compatibility, license, and SAST checks. Adoption verification remains separate. Owner: Benji Okafor. [PR 28462](</knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood/pr-28462-add-cost-model-client-library.json>) |
| Reliability validation | Blocked for broad launch | ENG-4827 is In Progress; formal SLO/alerts/approval evidence is not complete. Owner: Rafael Mendes. [ENG-4827](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4827-cost-model-drift-sli-and-alerts.json>) |
| Security authorization | Blocked | ENG-4821 requires security review and implements internal OIDC/mTLS, allowlisted service principals, tenant enforcement, cross-tenant rejection, and audit fields, but no authoritative final security approval was found. Owner: Kaitlyn Nguyen / Security reviewer; accountable: Ethan Park. [ENG-4821](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4821-cost-model-service-skeleton.json>) |
| Release readiness | Blocked for broad launch | Feature flags and fallback exist, but the evidence set does not establish an accepted canary report, two-person promotion approval, or completed 48-hour regression-free observation for this capability. Owner: Chloe Martin / Rafael Mendes / release approver. [Console adoption](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4825-console-cost-breakdown-adoption.json>) |
| Finance/billing alignment | Blocked for broad launch | ENG-4832 still required replay evidence, intentional-difference docs, and Telemetry/Auth/Finance reviews in its latest cited update. Owners: Cole Summers, Nadia Rahman, Kaitlyn Nguyen, Laura Bennett. [ENG-4832](</knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4832-billing-hooks-alignment-with-cost-model.json>) |

## Operational gates and rollback criteria

Before any cohort increase:

- Demonstrate endpoint SLO and error-budget compliance for the intended request shapes; publish latency, errors, cache hit rate, request-shape/cardinality, telemetry freshness, and drift panels. Owner: Rafael Mendes.
- Exercise Console degradation: cached last-known value plus banner for aggregate failure; hide request detail rather than failing the page; legacy fallback retained. Owners: Jada Williams / Chloe Martin.
- Enforce server bounds, per-tenant cache quotas, top-K plus “other,” deterministic ordering, client timeouts, bounded retries with jitter, and request coalescing. Owners: Ethan Park / Benji Okafor / Thomas Baird.
- Stop or roll back if latency exceeds the accepted SLO, 504s recur, request-shape saturation appears, cross-tenant/auth audit failures occur, drift breaches the approved lag-aware threshold, or customer-facing totals lack freshness/estimate labeling. Owner: Rafael Mendes; rollback operator: Console release owner.

## Blockers and remaining approvals

1. Security: recorded production authorization for the internal service controls and audit evidence.
2. SRE: approved SLO/SLIs, alert thresholds, on-call assignment, runbook, and successful rollback exercise.
3. Release: accepted limited-cohort canary evidence and two-person authorization for any expansion.
4. Delivery: verified completion/adoption evidence for schema compatibility, client behavior, caching/bounds, and Console UX fallback.
5. Finance/Telemetry/Auth: accepted ENG-4832 replay and mapping evidence.

## Evidence-backed next steps

- Rafael Mendes: finish ENG-4827; attach SLO approval, dashboards, alert routing, and rollback-drill result.
- Kaitlyn Nguyen plus Security: record final review of identity, tenant isolation, service-principal scopes, audit fields, and negative cross-tenant tests.
- Ethan Park, Benji Okafor, Thomas Baird: attach load-test and request-bound evidence, including cache hit rate and deterministic top-K behavior.
- Chloe Martin and Jada Williams: demonstrate flagged fallback, labeling, freshness state, request coalescing, and safe default groupings.
- Cole Summers, Nadia Rahman, Laura Bennett: complete replay reconciliation and sign off intentional Console-versus-invoice differences.
- Release approvers: run and accept a limited-cohort canary before increasing exposure.

## Recommendation

**Conditional-go only for an internal/allowlisted, feature-flagged cohort with legacy fallback; no-go for broad Hosted/Console rollout.** The limited scope is supportable because product scope and the internal service foundation are established and rollback containment exists. Broad launch is not reviewable as go until security authorization, SRE readiness, canary acceptance, and Finance/Telemetry alignment are recorded. No launch date is proposed.

## Revision history

- Revision 1: established capability, product gates, scope, delivery gaps, and owners from product and engineering evidence.
- Revision 2: incorporated operations, security, and release evidence; narrowed supported scope; added operational gates, blockers, approvals, next steps, and a conditional-go candidate.

4. **Release acceptance:** documented limited-cohort canary, stable observation against accepted thresholds, and two-person authorization for exposure increase.
5. **Finance/Telemetry/Auth acceptance:** accepted replay and mapping evidence for ENG-4832 and stable documentation of intentional invoice differences.

- Scope remains internal and feature-flagged until broad approval.

- A limited cohort completes the approved observation window without critical regression or rollback trigger.
- Console copy and exports clearly say “usage” and explain excluded fees, commitments, credits, adjustments, and taxes.
- Console usage reconciles to the billing usage subtotal within the accepted, lag-corrected tolerance; contract-level invoice items remain separately explained.
- Support owns a published troubleshooting/reconciliation path; SRE owns the pager/runbook; Security, SRE, Release, Finance/Telemetry/Auth, Product, and Console approvals are recorded.

## Operational stop and rollback criteria

Pause exposure growth or disable the flag if any approved SLO is breached; 504s or retry amplification recur; saturation or high-cardinality shapes escape bounds; cache/request-shape telemetry is unavailable; freshness or estimate labeling is absent; drift exceeds the approved lag-aware threshold; cross-tenant/auth/audit tests fail; or support cannot explain a customer-visible total.

**Conditional-go for the contained cohort; no-go for broad rollout.** Product definition, service foundations, CI, feature flags, and a working fallback make a limited cohort defensible. The invoice case proves that customer trust depends on permanent product copy and support guidance.
